readmePreview: Node.js Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment.

overview.summary: This is the Node.js runtime itself at v26.10.0 — a C++/V8 host (src/, ~495 files) wrapping a JavaScript standard library (lib/, ~429 files) that is compiled into a V8 startup snapshot at build time. Beyond upstream-familiar surface, this tree carries several large experimental subsystems wired through the same plumbing: a `node:vfs` virtual file system that intercepts `node:fs` and the module loaders at reserved mount points under `os.devNull/vfs/<id>`, a `node:ffi` libffi-backed foreign function interface gated by a `kFFI` permission scope, a `node:dtls` endpoint/session stack, a `node --experimental-bench` benchmark runner mirroring the test runner, and a vendored Rust crate set (`deps/crates`, temporal_rs + ICU) linked as a staticlib. The audience is Node core collaborators; the distinctive engineering property is that every new capability is a triple — a CLI option in `src/node_options.cc`, a `setupX()` in `pre_execution.js` that calls `BuiltinModule.allowRequireByUsers()`, and an internal binding registered in `src/node_binding.h`.

system_map.summary: Execution begins in `src/node_main.cc` (`main`/`wmain`) which calls `node::Start`, which after SEA argv fixup loads the V8 startup snapshot and runs a `NodeMainInstance`. C++ then picks exactly one main script from `lib/internal/main/` via a linear dispatch in `src/node.cc`; that script calls into `lib/internal/process/pre_execution.js` to configure the realm before user code. The JS layer talks to C++ only through `internalBinding()`, whose registry is the `NODE_BUILTIN_*_BINDINGS` macro list in `src/node_binding.h`. Build is GYP/Make (`configure.py` → `node.gyp` → `Makefile`) with a secondary GN path, plus Cargo for `deps/crates`. There is no deployment target in the usual sense: the artifact is the `node` binary, optionally repackaged as a single executable application by `src/node_sea.cc`.

claims.claim: The process entrypoint is `main()` (POSIX) / `wmain()` (Windows, which UTF-8-converts wide argv and refuses pre-Windows-10 unless `NODE_SKIP_PLATFORM_CHECK=1`), both delegating to `node::Start`.

`node::Start` first runs `sea::FixupArgsForSEA` so a single-executable build can rewrite its own argv, then calls `StartInternal`, which branches to `sea::BuildSingleExecutable`/`WriteSingleExecutableBlob` or `GenerateAndWriteSnapshotData` before falling through to `LoadSnapshotData` + `NodeMainInstance::Run`.

C++ selects the JS main script by an ordered if-chain in `src/node.cc`: worker_thread → inspect → print_help → prof_process → eval_string → check_syntax → bench_runner → test_runner → watch_mode → run_main_module → repl → eval_stdin. Adding a new run mode means adding a branch here plus a file in `lib/internal/main/`.

The JS↔C++ boundary is the `internalBinding()` registry declared by macro lists in `src/node_binding.h`; optional subsystems are compiled in conditionally — `quic` behind `HAVE_OPENSSL && OPENSSL_NO_QUIC != 1`, `dtls` behind `HAVE_OPENSSL && HAVE_DTLS`, `sqlite`/`webstorage` behind `HAVE_SQLITE`, `ffi` behind `HAVE_FFI`.

`lib/internal/bootstrap/node.js` is executed by `Realm::BootstrapRealm()` and is normally *not* run at startup — its resulting V8 heap is captured into the build-time snapshot by `SnapshotBuilder::Generate()`; `--no-node-snapshot` forces real execution. It must stay synchronous and must not read argv or env at top level.

`prepareExecution()` in `pre_execution.js` is the single funnel every main script passes through; it patches the process object, runs ~25 `setupX()` initializers, calls `initializePermission()`, initializes the module loaders, and mounts the VFS before returning the resolved main entry.

The storage layer is threefold: the real file system via the `fs`/`fs_dir`/`glob` bindings, SQLite via `src/node_sqlite.cc` (which now exposes virtual tables through a `VirtualTableModule` wrapping `sqlite3_module`), and Web Storage via the `webstorage` binding gated on `--experimental-webstorage`.

External native dependencies are vendored under `deps/` (v8, uv, openssl, ada, llhttp, nghttp2, ngtcp2, simdjson, sqlite, undici, zlib, zstd, libffi, LIEF, perfetto, postject) rather than fetched, so builds are hermetic.

`deps/crates` is a Rust staticlib (`crate-type = ["staticlib"]`, `node_crates` v14.6.202, rust-version 1.86) vendoring `temporal_rs`/`temporal_capi` and the ICU4X crates; its Cargo.toml is generated by node-core-utils and must not be hand-edited.

Build/test commands: `./configure && make -j4`, `make test` (tooltest + addon builds + cctest + jstest), `make test-only` (skips doc build), `make test-ci` for CI, `make lint` (js/cpp/md/yaml), `make coverage`.

`configure.py` owns feature toggles that become gyp variables — `--shared-ffi`/`--without-ffi` set `node_use_ffi`, and `--v8-enable-temporal-support` gates the Rust temporal path; `node.gyp` defaults `node_use_ffi%` to `false` and only pulls in `deps/libffi/libffi.gyp:libffi` when it is true.

Type checking of `lib/` is opt-in and non-emitting: `tsconfig.json` sets `allowJs: true`, `checkJs: false`, `noEmit: true`, excludes `src`/`tools`, and maps every public builtin id to its `lib/*.js` file plus `internal/*` to `lib/internal/*`.

Hand-written ambient types for the C++ boundary live in `typings/internalBinding/*.d.ts` (one file per binding, including `ffi.d.ts`), loaded via `tsconfig.json`'s `files` list alongside `typings/globals.d.ts` and `typings/primordials.d.ts`.

Python tooling is linted by ruff configured in `pyproject.toml` with deliberately huge thresholds (`max-complexity = 100`, `max-statements = 289`, `line-length = 172`), reflecting long-lived legacy scripts like `configure.py` (112 KB) and `tools/test.py`.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface is the CLI plus the `node:*` builtin module set. The CLI's 'subcommands' are really the run-mode branches in `src/node.cc` — `node inspect`, `node --test`, `node --experimental-bench`, `node --watch`, `node -e`, `node --check`, `node --prof-process`, `node --build-snapshot`, `node --build-sea`, and the default script/REPL/stdin paths. Module features are individually flag-gated and only become requirable when a `setupX()` in `pre_execution.js` calls `BuiltinModule.allowRequireByUsers()`. This tree's notable additions over a stock runtime are `node:vfs`, `node:ffi`, `node:dtls`, `node:bench`, `node:quic`, `node:sqlite` with virtual tables, and `stream/iter`/`zlib/iter`.

claims.claim: `node:vfs` exposes `create()`, `registerProvider()`, and the classes `VirtualFileSystem`, `VirtualProvider`, `MemoryProvider`, `RealFSProvider`, `ZipProvider`; it is `node:`-scheme-only and requires `--experimental-vfs`.

`--vfs-mount <src>` (repeatable) and `--vfs-load <src>` both append to the same `vfs_mounts` option vector; `--vfs-load` additionally sets the `[vfs_load_set]` implied bool so the entry point can be taken from inside a mount.

`node:ffi` provides `DynamicLibrary` plus typed pointer accessors (`getInt8`…`getFloat64`, `setInt8`…, `exportBytes`, `getRawPointer`, `kFastArguments`) and emits an experimental warning at module load.

`node:bench` mirrors the test runner's API shape — `bench`, `suite`/`describe`, `before`/`after`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach`, `run`, `runFile`, `createRunner` — and is reached from the CLI by `node --experimental-bench`, which routes to `internal/main/bench_runner`.

`node:dtls` exposes `connect`, `listen`, `createSecureContext`, and `DTLSEndpoint`/`DTLSSecureContext`/`DTLSSession`, backed by `src/dtls/{dtls,dtls_context,dtls_endpoint,dtls_session}.cc`; `DTLSEndpoint` manages a UDP socket and routes datagrams to sessions.
The permission model (`--permission`) exposes `process.permission.has()` / `.drop()` and nine scopes: fs (with read/write children), child, wasi, worker, inspector, net, addon, ffi, openssl.store.
`--permission-audit` is a distinct mode from `--permission`: `isAuditMode()` reads it separately and `Permission::EnableWarningOnly()` makes denials warn rather than throw.

Single-executable applications are configured by a JSON file parsed in `src/node_sea.cc` supporting `useSnapshot`, `useCodeCache`, `assets`, and `disableExperimentalSEAWarning`; assets are serialized into the blob and read back as `string_view` pairs.

SEA assets can be surfaced as a read-only mounted VFS via `initSeaVfs()`, which places the SEA main script at the mount-point root so `__dirname`-relative `require()` calls inside a bundled app resolve to bundled assets.

`node --watch` is implemented as a supervisor process: `internal/main/watch_mode.js` strips watch flags into `argsWithoutWatchOptions`, re-`spawn`s `process.execPath`, and drives restarts from a `FilesWatcher` with a 200 ms debounce in `filter` or `all` mode.

The test runner CLI parses options via `parseCommandLine()`, supports `--test-isolation=none` (which defers user-module loading into `run()`), forces concurrency 1 when the inspector is active, and sets a nonzero exit code from the `test:summary` event.
`--experimental-stream-iter` unlocks two additional builtins in one shot, `stream/iter` and `zlib/iter`, via the same `allowRequireByUsers` mechanism.

`node:sqlite` is enabled by default (disabled only by `--no-experimental-sqlite`) and now supports user-defined virtual tables: `VirtualTableModule` populates an `sqlite3_module` with `xCreate`/`xConnect`/`xBestIndex`/`xOpen`/`xClose` trampolines.

Documented public API pages exist for every new subsystem — `doc/api/vfs.md`, `ffi.md`, `dtls.md`, `bench.md`, `quic.md`, `stream_iter.md` — so a feature is not considered landed without its doc page.

data_flow.summary: Input boundaries are argv/env (parsed into `EnvironmentOptions` by `src/node_options.cc` and read from JS via `getOptionValue()`), the file system, sockets, and the SEA blob embedded in the binary. Options are the master state: essentially every JS feature branch keys off `getOptionValue('--flag')`, and options are re-read after deserialization by `refreshRuntimeOptions()`. The heaviest transform in this tree is the VFS path router, which reroutes `node:fs` calls and module-loader fs calls whose resolved path falls under a reserved mount prefix, before those calls reach the native `fs` binding. State owners are the `Environment` object on the C++ side and, on the JS side, module-level singletons: `vfsState.handlers` in `internal/fs/utils.js`, the `loaderOverrides` map in `internal/modules/helpers.js`, the `providers` array in `provider_registry.js`, and `Module._cache`/`_pathCache` in the CJS loader.

claims.claim: CLI/NODE_OPTIONS parsing populates `EnvironmentOptions` fields declared in `src/node_options.h` (`vfs_mounts`, `experimental_vfs`, `vfs_load`, `allow_fs_vfs`) which JS then reads through `internal/options`'s `getOptionValue()`.
`refreshRuntimeOptions()` is the first call inside `prepareExecution()`, re-reading options after snapshot deserialization so a snapshotted heap does not carry stale build-time option values.

Every VFS mount is assigned a numeric layer id and is served at `${os.devNull}/vfs/<id>`; because `os.devNull` is a character device (`/dev/null`, `\\.\NUL`) it can have no children, so path ownership is decidable from the string alone without touching the disk.

`getLayerIdFromPath()` parses the layer id with a hand-rolled digit scan over char codes 47/92 (`/`, `\`) rather than splitting — a deliberate hot-path optimisation since it runs on candidate fs calls.

Dispatch into the VFS is a single null-check per fs function: `lib/fs.js` reads `vfsState.handlers` and, if non-null, calls the handler and routes the returned promise through `vfsResult()`/`vfsVoid()` to the error-first callback; when no VFS is mounted the field is `null` and overhead is one comparison.
`setVfsHandlers()` is the only writer of `vfsState.handlers` and is imported by `internal/vfs/setup.js`, making that file the single install point for fs interception.

Module resolution is redirected separately from `fs`: `internal/modules/helpers.js` wraps each native loader method and consults a `loaderOverrides` map installed by `setLoaderOverrides()`, with a `hasLoaderOverrides` boolean short-circuit when the map is empty.

`internal/modules/run_main.js` deliberately calls loader methods through `loaderMethods` rather than the `modules` binding directly, precisely so a mounted VFS can override them and a worker entry point can live inside one.

Unmounting must invalidate loader state: `cleanForVfsPrefix()` walks `Module._cache`, `Module._pathCache`, `statCache`, `realpathCache`, and the package.json caches, deleting entries under a mount prefix — by value for `_pathCache`, whose keys are `request\0parent` tokens.

The provider selection pipeline is source-sniffing, not extension-based: `canHandle()` for `zip` attempts `ZipFile.openSync()` (which locates the end-of-central-directory record) and stashes the opened archive in `pendingZipFile` so `create()` does not reopen it; `dir` falls back to `stats.isDirectory()`.

Permission denials feed a diagnostics channel: `Permission::is_scope_granted` calls `Publish()` on failure, which emits `{scope, resource, dropped}` on a per-scope channel and guards against recursion with a `publishing_` flag so a subscriber's own checks cannot re-enter.

`normalizeReference()` in the JS permission layer canonicalises input across three representations — `URL` (converted with `fileURLToPath` only for `fs.*` scopes), `Uint8Array` (passed through raw so non-UTF-8 paths are not mangled), and validated strings.

SEA data flows binary→memory: `WriteSingleExecutableBlob` serialises the asset map with a length-prefixed count, and the reader rebuilds an `unordered_map<string_view, string_view>` pointing into the still-mapped blob rather than copying.

Worker threads receive their entry through the message port (`LOAD_SCRIPT` in `internal/worker/io`), not argv, and call `finishVfsMounts()` themselves so mounts are re-created per thread rather than shared.

behavior_traces.summary: Three flows characterise the runtime: cold startup of a script, mounting a VFS and loading an entry point from inside it, and a permission-checked FFI `dlopen`. All three share the same spine — C++ picks a main script, that script calls `prepareExecution()`, and `prepareExecution()` decides what the realm is allowed to do. The VFS trace is the most intricate because mounting is deliberately deferred past `--import` preloads so a preload can register a custom provider. The FFI trace is the clearest example of a two-check security path, where a purely in-memory operation still demands filesystem-write permission for platform-consistency reasons.

claims.claim: Cold start (script): `main()` → `node::Start` → `sea::FixupArgsForSEA` → `StartInternal` → `LoadSnapshotData` → `NodeMainInstance::Run` → C++ `StartExecution` picks `internal/main/run_main_module`.

`run_main_module.js` then calls `prepareMainThreadExecution(!isEntryURL)` → `markBootstrapComplete()` → `RegExpPrototypeExec(/^/, '')` to reset RegExp statics before user code → `Module.runMain(mainEntry)`.

`Module.runMain` is invoked even for ESM entry points solely to preserve legacy monkey-patchability of `Module.runMain` by `--require` preloads; the file comments this as undesirable and slated for removal once module customization hooks suffice.

Inside `prepareExecution()` the order is fixed: `refreshRuntimeOptions()` → `patchProcessObject()` → trace/inspector/navigator/warning setup → the feature `setupX()` block → `initializeReport()` → `setupDiagnosticsChannel()` → `initializePermission()` → source maps → deprecations → `setupVmModules()` → `initializeModuleLoaders()` → `finishVfsMounts()` → `setupHttpProxy()`.

Each flag-gated builtin is unlocked by the same three lines — check `getOptionValue('--experimental-X')`, require `BuiltinModule` from `internal/bootstrap/realm`, call `allowRequireByUsers('X')` — repeated verbatim in `setupBench`, `setupFFI`, `setupSQLite`, `setupStreamIter`, `setupDTLS`, `setupQuic`, `setupVfs`.

VFS mount trace: `finishVfsMounts()` guards on `vfsMounted` → reads `--vfs-mount` entries → `path.resolve` + `fs.statSync` each (throwing `ERR_VFS_INVALID_TARGET` on failure or on a non-file/non-dir) → `selectProvider()` → `new VirtualFileSystem(provider)` → `vfs.mount()`.

Mounting is called from two places with an idempotence guard: from `prepareExecution()` only when `--import` is empty, otherwise from `run_main` after the `--import` loop — so an `--import` preload can `registerProvider()` before any source's provider is chosen.

For `--vfs-load`, `getVfsLoadIndex()` re-walks `process.execArgv`-style option names to recover which position in the shared `vfs_mounts` list came from `--vfs-load`, because the option parser stores plain strings and cannot record provenance.

The `--vfs-load` source is spliced into `process.argv` at index 1 rather than overwriting it, so the program's own first positional argument is not silently dropped; `argv[1]` names the real source while the reserved mount point stays an implementation detail.
`src/node.cc` routes to `run_main_module` when `vfs_load` is set even with no positional argument, instead of falling through to the REPL or stdin-eval — a dedicated branch added for this flag.

FFI trace: `new ffi.DynamicLibrary(path)` → `DynamicLibrary::New` → construct-call check → `THROW_IF_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS(kFFI)` → null-byte check on the path → optional byte materialisation → `uv_dlopen` → `image.AfterOpen()`.

When an FFI library is supplied as bytes (a library living inside a VFS that `dlopen` cannot reach by path), the code additionally demands `kFileSystemWrite` on `AddonImage::TempDir()` — and comments that the check is enforced even on Linux where an anonymous memfd is used, so grants do not vary by platform.

`initializePermission()` hardens the realm before granting: it replaces `process.binding` with a thrower, `ObjectFreeze`s the `path` module so it cannot be monkey-patched to defeat path checks, emits `SecurityWarning` codes PERM0001–PERM0007 for each dangerous `--allow-*`, and only then defines `process.permission`.
Without `--permission`, passing any `--allow-*` flag is a hard error: the else-branch iterates `availableFlags()` and throws `ERR_MISSING_OPTION`, preventing a false sense of restriction.

Worker startup diverges: `internal/main/worker_thread.js` calls `prepareWorkerThreadExecution()` (which asserts `initializeModules === false`), waits for a `LOAD_SCRIPT` message on the env message port, and only then calls `initializeModuleLoaders` and `finishVfsMounts`.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is dominated by the bespoke Python harness `tools/test.py`, which discovers suites under `test/<suite>/`, applies per-suite `.status` files for SKIP/SLOW/FLAKY expectations, and shells out to the built `node` binary per test file. There is no Vitest/Jest; the stack tag is misleading. Native code is covered by `cctest` (googletest) and the `js-native-api`/`node-api`/`addons` suites, which require a build step before they can run. Coverage is collected by nyc/c8 with `.nycrc` thresholds of 95% lines/statements and 93% branches, uploaded to Codecov from two Linux workflows. The new subsystems are well covered at the JS level — ~121 `test-vfs-*` files in `test/parallel` alone plus a dedicated `test/ffi/` suite — but SEA-specific paths are explicitly excluded from coverage.

claims.claim: The harness is `tools/test.py`, a Python 3 runner invoked as `./tools/test.py --flaky-tests keep_retrying -p actions -j 4`; suites are directories under `test/` and each may carry a `<section>.status` file read by `ReadConfigurationInto`.

`test/root.status` encodes mode-dependent expectations (e.g. a long list of `parallel/test-*: SLOW` entries under `[$mode==debug]`), and `test/ffi/ffi.status` skips `test-ffi-calls`, `test-ffi-shared-buffer`, and `test-ffi-weakref-calls` on Solaris/SmartOS where bundled libffi callbacks crash.

`test/parallel` is by far the largest suite (~4976 files), followed by `test/fixtures` (~6108 support files), `test/es-module` (246), `test/addons` (185), `test/sequential` (125), `test/module-hooks` (114), and `test/test-runner` (113).

VFS has roughly 121 dedicated files in `test/parallel` covering per-API parity (`test-vfs-fs-mkdirSync`, `test-vfs-fs-copyFileSync`, `test-vfs-fs-createReadStream`), edge cases (`test-vfs-bigint-position`, `test-vfs-ctime-update`), and an explicit `test-vfs-fs-matches-real-fs` differential test.

FFI has its own compiled suite `test/ffi/` with a `fixture_library`, a `testcfg.py`, and permission-focused tests: `test-ffi-permissions.js`, `test-ffi-permission-allow-cli.js`, `test-ffi-permission-audit.js`, `test-ffi-permission-drop.js`, plus `test-ffi-vfs.js` for the load-from-bytes path.

Running the JS suites requires native build steps first: `make jstest` depends on `build-addons build-js-native-api-tests build-node-api-tests build-sqlite-tests build-ffi-tests` — running `tools/test.py` on a clean tree will fail those suites.
`make cctest` runs the C++ googletest binary built from `test/cctest/` (37 files) and is a separate gate from the JS suites.

CI suite composition is `CI_JS_SUITES = $(JS_SUITES) pummel` and `CI_NATIVE_SUITES = $(NATIVE_SUITES) benchmark`, with `doctool` conditionally appended; `make test-ci` runs all three plus the prerequisite builds.

`.github/workflows/test-linux.yml` builds on ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-24.04-arm with clang-19, Python 3.14, Rust 1.88 and sccache, runs `make build-ci` then `make test-ci -j1 TEST_CI_ARGS="-p actions --measure-flakiness 9"`.

CI asserts test hygiene two ways: a `git add -A && git diff --exit-code --staged` step fails the build if running tests dirtied the tree, and the whole suite is re-run from a directory named with spaces, quotes, and non-ASCII characters to catch path-handling bugs.
Coverage thresholds are declared in `.nycrc` — 95% lines, 95% statements, 93% branches — over `lib/` only, with `test/`, `tools/`, `benchmark/`, and `deps/` excluded.

Codecov is configured to wait for two coverage builds (`coverage-linux.yml` and `coverage-linux-without-intl.yml`; the Windows one is noted as manually disabled) and both project and patch status gates are turned off, so coverage is informational rather than blocking.

`test/common/index.js` exposes capability predicates that tests use to self-skip — `hasCrypto`, `hasIntl`, `hasFullICU`, `hasTemporal`, `hasDtls`, `hasQuic`, `hasSQLite`, `hasFFI`, `hasInspector`, `hasLocalStorage` — so conditionally-compiled bindings do not produce false failures.

SEA-plus-VFS initialisation is explicitly uncovered: `internal/vfs/sea.js` opens with `/* c8 ignore start -- SEA VFS initialization requires an actual SEA binary */`, so that path is exercised only by the separate `test/sea` suite (43 files), not by line coverage.

Recent commit history shows active flake management (`test: deflake test-bench-errors`, `test-http2-debug`, `test-benchmark-crypto`) alongside a `label-flaky-test-issue.yml` workflow and `--measure-flakiness 9` in CI.

risk_map.summary: The highest-value security surfaces are the permission model, `node:ffi`, and the VFS path router — and they interact. FFI is a documented memory-unsafe API whose only guard is the `kFFI` scope; the VFS is documented as explicitly *not* a security boundary despite superficially resembling a sandbox; and the permission model's correctness depends on non-obvious hardening (freezing `path`, killing `process.binding`) that a refactor could silently undo. Fragile coupling concentrates in the VFS's reliance on string-prefix path ownership and on cache invalidation across five separate module-loader caches. The `--vfs-load` provenance recovery by re-parsing execArgv is the most brittle single mechanism in the tree.

claims.claim: `node:ffi` is memory-unsafe by design — the docs state that invalid pointers, wrong signatures, or use-after-free 'can crash the process or corrupt memory' — and its only gate is `THROW_IF_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS(kFFI)`, which is a no-op unless `--permission` is on.

`--allow-ffi` is only offered in `availableFlags()` when `--experimental-ffi` is set, so the flag surface changes shape depending on another flag; a script probing `availableFlags()` for capability discovery can get inconsistent answers.

The VFS is documented as NOT a sandbox: 'The VFS API is not a sandbox, permission system, or access-control mechanism', and `RealFSProvider`'s root-escape rejection is explicitly stated not to be a security boundary. Any code treating a mount as isolation is wrong.

VFS path ownership is decided purely by string prefix against `${os.devNull}/vfs`; the safety argument rests on `os.devNull` being a character device that cannot have children. A platform where that assumption fails, or a `path.resolve` normalisation difference, would break routing exactness.

`getVfsLoadIndex()` recovers which mount came from `--vfs-load` by re-walking argument names and counting `--vfs-mount`/`--vfs-load` occurrences, including manual handling of the space-separated `--vfs-mount value` form. Any change to option parsing or aliasing silently misattributes the entry point.

Unmount correctness depends on `cleanForVfsPrefix()` clearing five distinct caches (`Module._cache`, `Module._pathCache` by value, `statCache`, `realpathCache`, package.json caches); missing one leaves resolvable stale entries pointing into an unmounted layer.

The permission model's integrity relies on two side effects that look like incidental hardening: replacing `process.binding` with a thrower and `ObjectFreeze(require('path'))`. Removing either reopens a documented bypass.

`Permission::Publish` guards re-entrancy with a mutable `publishing_` flag rather than a scope guard; an exception thrown from a diagnostics-channel subscriber would leave `publishing_` stuck true and silently suppress all further permission telemetry.

Zip provider detection performs a trial `ZipFile.openSync()` inside `canHandle()` and caches the handle in module-level `pendingZipFile`; if a later provider's `canHandle` throws or `create()` is never reached, that file handle leaks and a subsequent probe reuses stale state.

`registerProvider()` unshifts onto a module-global array with no removal API and no ordering control beyond 'newest wins', and the doc comment confirms a registered provider 'can back, wrap, or vet any source' — a `--require`/`--import` preload can therefore intercept every subsequent mount.

`node --watch` shells out: it `spawn`s `process.execPath` with reconstructed argv and manipulates `NODE_OPTIONS`, making it a command-construction path where flag stripping bugs change what the child is allowed to do (a recent commit addressed exactly this: 'watch: strip watch flags from NODE_OPTIONS in child process').

`src/node_file.cc` is the largest source file (5851 lines) and contains ~55 `THROW_IF_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` call sites; each new fs syscall wrapper is an opportunity to omit one, and there is no compile-time enforcement that a binding method performs its check.

Blast radius: `lib/internal/process/pre_execution.js` is on the critical path of every execution mode (main thread, worker, shadow realm, test runner, bench runner), so a fault in any `setupX()` breaks all entry points at once.

`--vfs-load` is force-disabled for workers by mutating `per_isolate_opts->per_env->vfs_load = false` in `src/node_worker.cc`; this cross-layer write means main-thread and worker option state intentionally diverge, which is easy to overlook when reasoning about option values in JS.

SEA construction writes an executable to disk from a JSON config with `assets` and `useSnapshot`/`useCodeCache`, and `FixupArgsForSEA` rewrites argv before any option parsing — a supply-chain-relevant path where the config file fully determines the resulting binary's behaviour.

extension_points.summary: This codebase is unusually explicit about where new code plugs in, because adding a feature is a repeated four-part ritual. New native capability goes in the `NODE_BUILTIN_*_BINDINGS` macro lists; new CLI surface goes in `src/node_options.cc` with a field in `node_options.h`; new run modes go in the `StartExecution` if-chain plus a file in `lib/internal/main/`; new user-visible builtins are gated by a `setupX()` in `pre_execution.js` calling `BuiltinModule.allowRequireByUsers()`. Beyond core, the VFS provider registry, the CJS `Module._extensions` table, the loader-override map, and the SQLite virtual-table module are genuine runtime plugin surfaces.

claims.claim: `BuiltinModule.allowRequireByUsers(id)` is the runtime gate that makes a `lib/*.js` module requirable by user code; it adds to `canBeRequiredByUsersList` and conditionally to `canBeRequiredByUsersWithoutSchemeList` (new experimental modules are added `node:`-scheme-only).

`vfs.registerProvider({ name, canHandle, create })` is the public plugin interface for `--vfs-mount` sources; registrations are unshifted ahead of the built-in `zip` and `dir` providers, so a custom provider outranks both.

`VirtualProvider` in `lib/internal/vfs/provider.js` is the base class a custom provider subclasses; the shipped implementations (`MemoryProvider`, `RealFSProvider`, `ZipProvider`, and the internal SEA provider) are the reference shapes.

`setLoaderOverrides(overrides)` installs per-key replacements for the module loader's fs and package.json operations; passing a nullish field restores the native fast path, which is how unmount cheaply reverts loader interception.

`Module._extensions` is the classic CJS extension table (`.js`, `.json`, `.node` assigned in `cjs/loader.js`) and `findLongestRegisteredExtension` supports multi-dot extensions, so a loader plugin can register e.g. `.test.ts`.

`Module._load`, `Module._resolveFilename`, and `Module._findPath` remain intentionally monkey-patchable — `resolveMainPath()` comments that `Module._findPath` 'is monkey-patchable here', and the repo's own `eslint.config.mjs` patches `Module._resolveFilename` to resolve vendored ESLint plugins.

Adding a native binding means adding `V(name)` to the appropriate macro list in `src/node_binding.h` — `NODE_BUILTIN_STANDARD_BINDINGS` for unconditional ones, or a new `#if`-guarded `NODE_BUILTIN_X_BINDINGS(V)` block for optional subsystems.

Adding a CLI flag is a paired edit: `AddOption("--flag", help, BOOL_FIELD(field), kAllowedInEnvvar-style)` in `src/node_options.cc` and the field declaration in `src/node_options.h`; `Implies()` links derived bools (as `--vfs-load` implies `[vfs_load_set]`).

Adding an execution mode requires a branch in the `StartExecution` chain in `src/node.cc` and a corresponding script in `lib/internal/main/`; `bench_runner` is the most recent instance of this pattern and mirrors `test_runner` line for line.

`sqlite.createModule()` backed by `VirtualTableModule` lets user JS supply `xBestIndex`/`xOpen`/`xClose` behaviour into SQLite's `sqlite3_module` vtable — a genuine C++-level plugin surface reachable from JS.

Permission scopes are extended by adding a `V(Name, "dotted.name", Parent, "--allow-flag")` entry to the `PERMISSIONS(V)` macro in `permission_base.h`; the enum, the diagnostics channel names, and the string mapping are all generated from it.
Test suites are pluggable: each `test/<suite>/` may carry a `testcfg.py` and a `<suite>.status` file that `tools/test.py` discovers, as `test/ffi/` does.

Lint is composed from per-directory partial configs (`lib/eslint.config_partial.mjs`, `test/`, `doc/`, `benchmark/`, `tools/eslint/`) assembled by the root `eslint.config.mjs`, plus a custom `tools/eslint-rules` plugin directory — the place to add core-specific rules.

The internal binding type surface is extended by adding a `typings/internalBinding/<name>.d.ts` file; recent commits ('typings: wire up quic internal binding types', 'typings: add mksnapshot internal binding types') show this is expected alongside the C++ change.

agent_handoff.summary: Read `AGENTS.md` first — it is binding policy, not advice, and it forbids an agent from pushing, opening PRs, or posting comments without active human oversight. Code style in `lib/` is not ordinary JavaScript: everything goes through `primordials` to be immune to user monkey-patching, and a custom ESLint plugin enforces it. Before editing, understand that `lib/` is snapshotted at build time, so top-level side effects in bootstrap files have outsized consequences. Nothing in `deps/` should be hand-edited. The realistic verification loop is a full build followed by targeted `tools/test.py` runs, not a fast unit-test cycle.

claims.claim: `AGENTS.md` requires `Signed-off-by:` from the human contributor and an `Assisted-by: <agent name>` annotation, and explicitly prohibits `Signed-off-by:`/`Co-authored-by:` naming an agent, pushing to any branch or tag, and creating unsupervised PRs or issues.

Read these first, in order: `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `doc/contributing/primordials.md`, `doc/contributing/cpp-style-guide.md`, and `lib/internal/bootstrap/node.js` (whose header comment is the best single explanation of startup ordering).

Every file in `lib/` destructures from `primordials` at the top (`ArrayPrototypePush`, `StringPrototypeStartsWith`, `ObjectFreeze`, …) instead of using built-in methods directly; new code must match this or `tools/eslint-rules` will reject it.

Never hand-edit `deps/`: `deps/crates/Cargo.toml` states 'This manifest is generated by node-core-utils. Do not modify it directly', and dependency bumps are driven by `tools/dep_updaters/` and scheduled workflows.

Anything added to `lib/internal/bootstrap/` must be synchronous and must not read argv or env at top level, because it is executed at snapshot-build time; runtime-dependent setup belongs in `pre_execution.js` or a `lib/internal/main/` script.

Verification loop: `./configure && make -j<n>` then `python3 tools/test.py parallel/test-<pattern>` for targeted runs; full validation is `make test-only` (build addons + cctest + jstest + tooltest without rebuilding docs).

Lint before proposing a change: `make lint` runs js/cpp/md/yaml; `make lint-ci` adds Python lint and a merge-conflict-marker scan across `benchmark deps doc lib src test tools` that fails the build on stray `<<<<<<<`/`>>>>>>>`.

Safe edit boundary: a feature that is JS-only (a new provider, a runner reporter, a stream helper) can be added without touching C++. Anything needing a new syscall, a new option, or a new permission scope requires coordinated edits across `src/node_options.{cc,h}`, `src/node_binding.h`, and `pre_execution.js`.

Trap: options are read twice — once at parse time into `EnvironmentOptions` and again in JS via `getOptionValue()` after `refreshRuntimeOptions()`. Caching an option value at JS module scope before that call yields a stale snapshot-time value.
Trap: `permission.js` memoizes `_permission`, `_audit`, and `_ffi` on first read, so an option consulted before `refreshRuntimeOptions()` is frozen for the process lifetime.

Trap: worker option state is not the main thread's — `src/node_worker.cc` overwrites `vfs_load` to false per worker, so a JS-side `getOptionValue('--vfs-load')` reasoning must account for thread identity.

Trap: `test/ffi`, `test/sqlite`, `test/addons`, `test/js-native-api`, and `test/node-api` all need a build step (`make build-ffi-tests`, etc.) before `tools/test.py` will pass on them; failures there on a fresh tree usually mean 'not built', not 'broken'.
CI asserts the tree is unchanged after tests run, so any test that writes into the repo (rather than a tmpdir) will fail the Linux workflow even if the assertions pass.

Use `test/common/index.js` capability predicates (`hasFFI`, `hasDtls`, `hasQuic`, `hasSQLite`, `hasTemporal`, `hasCrypto`) to guard new tests for conditionally-compiled features rather than assuming a full-featured build.
Public API changes are incomplete without the matching `doc/api/*.md` page and YAML metadata block (`added: vX.Y.Z`, `Stability: 1 - Experimental`), as every subsystem in this tree carries one.

readmePreview: Opinionated Code Formatter JavaScript · TypeScript · Flow · JSX · JSON CSS · SCSS · Less HTML · Vue · Angular GraphQL · Markdown · YAML Your favorite language? Intro Prettier is an opinionated code formatter.

overview.summary: Prettier 3.10.0-dev is an opinionated, plugin-based code formatter: it parses source into an AST, attaches comments, converts that AST to a Wadler-style Doc IR, then pretty-prints to a string. The public Node API in src/index.js is fully async (format, check, formatWithCursor, resolveConfig, getFileInfo, getSupportInfo); the CLI enters through bin/prettier.cjs into src/cli/index.js, with an opt-in rewrite re-exported from @prettier/cli. Built-in languages (JS/TS/Flow, JSON, CSS/Less/SCSS, HTML/Vue/Angular/LWC/MJML, GraphQL, Markdown/MDX, YAML, Handlebars) are themselves plugins, lazily loaded, and last-registered plugins win when resolving parsers and printers.

system_map.summary: The runtime has three public surfaces: the Node ESM/CJS API (src/index.js / src/index.cjs), the CLI (bin/prettier.cjs → src/cli), and a browser standalone bundle (src/standalone.js, no config/plugin autoload). Formatting is owned by src/main/core.js; languages live under src/language-*; plugins are assembled by src/main/plugins and the generated builtin registries. Config search/load lives in src/config; the Doc printer in src/document. Development requires Node >=22 and Yarn 4; production tests still exercise dist/ down to Node 14. The website is a Docusaurus + Vite playground published via Netlify; npm packages are built by scripts/build/build.js into dist/.

claims.claim: package.json names the project prettier 3.10.0-dev, sets type module, engines.node >=22, bin to ./bin/prettier.cjs, main to ./src/index.cjs, and exports '.' (types src/index.d.ts, require src/index.cjs, default src/index.js), './standalone' to src/standalone.js, and './plugins/*' to src/plugins/*.js.
The published browser/unpkg entry is standalone.js; package.json also defines #universal import maps that swap src/universal/*.browser.js in browsers versus src/universal/*.js on Node.

bin/prettier.cjs is the real CLI bootstrap: it optionally enables Node compile cache, rejects Node versions below package.json engines.node, strips --experimental-cli / PRETTIER_EXPERIMENTAL_CLI, then dynamically imports either src/experimental-cli/index.js or src/cli/index.js and calls cli.run().

src/index.js is the Node API: withPlugins loads builtin plus user plugins, then format/check/formatWithCursor/getSupportInfo/inferParser wrap src/main/core.js; it also exports resolveConfig, getFileInfo, doc, util, version, __debug, and __internal (shared with the CLI).
src/standalone.js reimplements withPlugins without filesystem plugin loading: plugins may be an array or an object (prettierPlugins); there is no resolveConfig/getFileInfo.

Builtin plugins are generated (do NOT edit) by scripts/generate-builtin-plugins.js into development-plugins.js (language-* modules) and production-plugins.js (src/plugins/*.js bundles), then lazy-loaded via toLazyLoadPlugins. loadBuiltinPlugins() picks production vs development based on NODE_ENV.

Language implementations live in src/language-{js,json,css,html,graphql,handlebars,markdown,yaml}; each exports languages, parsers, printers, and options. JS printers are a single estree printer; HTML covers angular/html/lwc/mjml/vue parsers with one html printer.

The build is node ./scripts/build/build.js; scripts/build/packages/index.js emits four packages (prettier, plugin-hermes, plugin-oxc, plugin-yuku) into dist/. prepublishOnly exits 1 so the source tree cannot be published.

The website is Docusaurus 3 plus a separate Vite/Vue playground (website/vite.config.mjs, website/playground/). Netlify builds with yarn build:website and publishes website/build/. Playground formatting runs in a Worker at /worker.mjs.

CI is GitHub Actions: Dev runs yarn test (and c8 coverage) on Node 22/26; Prod first yarn build --clean then tests dist/ across Node 14–26, OS matrix, standalone, and Chrome/Firefox ESM+UMD via Puppeteer; Lint runs deps/tsc/eslint/prettier/cspell/changelog/format-test plus actionlint.

Config resolution is src/config/resolve-config.js: searchPrettierConfig + optional EditorConfig (editorconfig-without-wasm), mergeOverrides via micromatch, and relative plugin paths resolved against the config file directory.

The experimental CLI is a thin re-export of @prettier/cli/bin (and worker from @prettier/cli/dist/prettier_serial.js), selected by --experimental-cli or PRETTIER_EXPERIMENTAL_CLI rather than a first-party implementation in src/cli.

feature_catalog.summary: Users format via CLI, Node API, or browser standalone. The CLI writes, checks, lists, caches, and inspects files; the API formats text, maps cursor offsets, resolves config, and infers parsers. Built-in languages cover the web stack with multiple JS parsers (babel/acorn/espree/meriyah/oxc/yuku/typescript/flow/hermes). Plugins, EditorConfig, ignore files, pragmas, range format, and a playground are first-class. Prettier refuses new formatting options by policy.

claims.claim: prettier.format(text, options) is withPlugins(core.formatWithCursor) with cursorOffset -1; prettier.check is format === text; prettier.formatWithCursor returns {formatted, cursorOffset, comments}.

Public Node APIs also include resolveConfig, resolveConfigFile, clearConfigCache, getFileInfo, getSupportInfo, plus prettier.doc and prettier.util. All public APIs are async; src/index.d.ts is the shipped types.

CLI surface from src/cli/cli-options.evaluate.js includes --write/-w, --check/-c, --list-different/-l, --cache, --cache-location, --cache-strategy content|metadata, --config/--no-config, --config-precedence cli-override|file-override|prefer-file, --editorconfig, --ignore-path (default .gitignore and .prettierignore), --ignore-unknown/-u, --with-node-modules, --file-info, --find-config-path, --support-info, --help, --version.

Debug CLI flags --debug-print-doc, --debug-print-ast, --debug-print-comments, --debug-check, --debug-benchmark, --debug-repeat (and PRETTIER_PERF_REPEAT) short-circuit the format path in src/cli/format.js.

Core format options in src/main/core-options.evaluate.js include parser, plugins (--plugin, array), printWidth (80), tabWidth (2), useTabs, endOfLine (lf|crlf|cr|auto), filepath/--stdin-filepath, rangeStart/rangeEnd, cursorOffset, insertPragma, requirePragma, checkIgnorePragma.

JS builtin parsers registered in development-plugins.js include babel, babel-flow, babel-ts, acorn, espree, meriyah, oxc, oxc-ts, typescript, flow, hermes, yuku, yuku-ts plus internal __js_expression / __vue_* / __ng_* parsers.

Non-JS builtins: css/less/scss (postcss), graphql, glimmer/handlebars, html/angular/lwc/mjml/vue, json/json-stringify/json5/jsonc, markdown/mdx/remark, yaml. Parser names are also listed as core option choices.

Official in-repo extra packages @prettier/plugin-oxc, @prettier/plugin-hermes, and @prettier/plugin-yuku wrap the corresponding JS parsers, set a distinct astFormat (estree-oxc/estree-hermes/estree-yuku), and reuse the estree printer.

Plugin loading is documented for CLI --plugin, API options.plugins, and config plugins; plugin modules export languages, parsers, printers, options, defaultOptions. Strings go through import() / importFromDirectory.

Config files searched in order: package.json prettier key, package.yaml, .prettierrc, .prettierrc.json/yml/yaml/json5, .prettierrc.js/ts and prettier.config.js/ts, mjs/mts, cjs/cts, .prettierrc.toml. JS/TS configs are executed via import(pathToFileURL).

CLI --cache uses FormatResultsCache (file-entry-cache) at node_modules/.cache/prettier/.prettier-cache by default, keyed by prettier version + Node version + stable-stringified options, strategy content (checksum) or metadata (mtime). Cache is forbidden with stdin.

The playground (website/playground/PrettierFormat.js) posts {type:'format', version, code, options, settings} to a versioned Worker; docs/technical-details.md notes a special parser value doc-explorer for inspecting the Doc IR. Prettier will not accept PRs that add formatting options.

data_flow.summary: Text enters via CLI files/stdin or the format() API. Options are normalized, a parser is inferred or selected, plugins are loaded, and the parser produces an AST. Comments are attached, embedded languages may be re-parsed, printers emit a Doc, and printDocToString measures/breaks groups to a string. CLI then writes, diffs, or caches that string. Config, ignore, and EditorConfig are filesystem side channels that never run in standalone.

claims.claim: formatWithCursor in src/main/core.js: normalizeFormatOptions → normalizeInputAndOptions (BOM strip, EOL guess/normalize, index clamp) → optional pragma skip → formatRange or coreFormat → re-add BOM. Empty/whitespace-only input short-circuits to formatted: ''.

normalizeFormatOptions infers parser from filepath via inferParser if options.parser is missing, then initParser/initPrinter, copies locStart/locEnd/getVisitorKeys/astFormat onto options, and fills defaults from getSupportInfo. Throws UndefinedParserError if neither parser nor filepath is usable.

parse() in src/main/parse.js resolves the parser, optional parser.preprocess, then parser.parse(text, options, options) (third arg kept for v3 compat, slated for removal in v4). Parse errors with loc get a @babel/code-frame attached.

printAstToDoc: prepareToPrint attaches comments (attachComments) and optional printer.preprocess; printEmbeddedLanguages walks the tree; callPluginPrintFunction dispatches printer.print, prettier-ignore via printIgnored, and comment printing.

The Doc IR (string | Doc[] | commands such as group/fill/ifBreak/indent/line/cursor) is printed by src/document/printer/printer.js using MODE_FLAT vs MODE_BREAK and a fits() probe against remainingWidth. Public builders are re-exported as prettier.doc.

Cursor preservation: getCursorLocation finds cursorNode/nodeBeforeCursor/nodeAfterCursor; print wraps those nodes with the cursor symbol; coreFormat diffs old vs new region with diffArrays to compute the new cursorOffset.
Range format (formatRange) slices AST-calculated rangeStart/rangeEnd, formats with extra alignment, then splices the trimmed result back, converting EOL if needed.

CLI file input: expandPatterns (literal file, recursive dir **/*, or fast-glob; followSymbolicLinks:false; skip .git/.svn/.hg/.jj/.sl and node_modules unless --with-node-modules) → ignore() from .gitignore/.prettierignore → getOptionsForFile → formatWithCursor → optional fs.writeFile.

getOptionsForFile: resolveConfig (unless --no-config) with editorconfig flag, then applyConfigPrecedence (cli-override default), temporarily pushContextPlugins if the config lists plugins. Invalid config process.exit(2).

Config loaders execute user JS/TS/MJS/CJS via import(pathToFileURL); JSON via parse-json; JSON5 via @bybrave/json5; TOML via smol-toml; YAML via the yaml plugin's __parsePrettierYamlConfig. A string prettier field is treated as an external package and loaded with requireFromFile then importFromFile.

Standalone/browser path never searches the filesystem: plugins must be passed in; docs/browser.md states no config, ignore, CLI, or automatic plugin loading. withPlugins only Object.values(plugins) if not an array.

Embedded-language formatting (printer.embed) is skipped unless embeddedLanguageFormatting === 'auto' (default). Embed errors are swallowed unless PRETTIER_DEBUG is set. Plugins using the old embed arity throw with a v3 migration URL.

behavior_traces.summary: Three user-visible flows were walked in source. CLI startup validates Node, builds a Context from argv/plugins, then dispatches to version/help/support/config-path/file-info, stdin, or formatFiles. Formatting a file expands globs, resolves per-file options, optionally hits cache, then runs the parse→doc→string pipeline. Persistence is either in-place write via mockable.writeFormattedFile, stdout, or a check/list-different exit code.

claims.claim: CLI startup order: bin/prettier.cjs run() → version check against engines.node → shouldEnableExperimentalCli → import src/cli/index.js → cli.run(process.argv.slice(2)).

src/cli/index.js run(): parseArgvWithoutPlugins for log-level → new Context → context.init() (parse --plugin, getContextOptions, parseArgv, filePatterns=argv._) → main(context) with mutually exclusive flag checks.

main() dispatch: --version prints prettier.version; --help uses createUsage/createDetailedUsage; --support-info → printSupportInfo; --find-config-path → logResolvedConfigPathOrDie; --file-info → logFileInfoOrDie; else stdin if no patterns and (stdin not TTY or --stdin-filepath); else formatFiles; else usage + exitCode 1.

formatFiles: createIsIgnoredFromContextOrDie → optional FormatResultsCache → for await expandPatterns → skip ignored in write/check/list-different/debug-check → getOptionsForFile → fs.readFile utf8 → cache hit returns input unchanged else format() → maybe mockable.writeFormattedFile → set/remove cache → check summary + exitCode 1 if unformatted and not --write.

format() inner function: debugPrintDoc → __debug.printToDoc then formatDoc; debugPrintComments → formatWithCursor.comments JSON; debugPrintAst → JSON.stringify(ast); debugCheck double-formats and compares massaged ASTs; else performance loop or prettier.formatWithCursor.

API format path: prettier.format → formatWithCursor(cursorOffset:-1) → withPlugins loads loadBuiltinPlugins()+loadPlugins(plugins) → core.formatWithCursor → coreFormat: parseText → printAstToDoc → printDocToStringWithoutNormalizeOptions.

Parser/printer resolve loops plugins.findLast so later plugins override builtins (comment: temporarily solution, see #13729). Missing parser/printer throws ConfigError; in PRETTIER_TARGET=universal the message says plugins must be added to the standalone bundle.
JS print dispatch in printWithoutParentheses tries printAngular, printJsx, printFlow, printTypescript, then printEstree in order, returning the first defined Doc.

JS babel parser is createParser(createParse(...)) over @babel/parser with errorRecovery, a long plugin list (doExpressions, decorators, pipelineOperator combinations, etc.), then postprocess. Tests for those plugins live in tests/format/js/babel-plugins/ and are generated by scripts/update-babel-plugin-tests.js.
oxc parser uses oxc-parser parseSync with preserveParens:true, maps labels to Prettier loc errors via index-to-position, and shares postprocess/createParser with other JS parsers.

Playground flow: PrettierFormat setup() watches code/options/version → worker.format → WorkerApi posts to /worker.mjs?version=… → worker replies {uid, message, error}. Website README requires yarn build:website so UMD bundles exist in static/lib/.

Config persistence is not a write of Prettier state: --write overwrites source files; --cache writes .prettier-cache JSON via file-entry-cache.reconcile(); clearConfigCache clears prettier-config, editorconfig, and plugin import caches.

testing_signals.summary: Jest 30 with jest-light-runner drives four suites: snapshot format tests, CLI/API integration tests, unit tests, and dts tests. Format tests are directory fixtures plus runFormatTest, which implicitly adds extra JS parsers and, under FULL_TEST=1, AST-compare, second-format, EOL, and BOM checks. Production tests install dist/prettier and also run standalone and browser (Puppeteer) matrices. Unit tests are skipped in production; integration tests are skipped in standalone/browser.

claims.claim: jest.config.js testMatch: tests/format/**/format.test.js, tests/integration/__tests__/**/*.js, tests/unit/**/*.js, tests/dts/unit/**/*.js. Runner is jest-light-runner (child-process unless ENABLE_CODE_COVERAGE). Snapshot serializers: jest-snapshot-serializer-raw and -ansi.

runFormatTest(import.meta, parsers, options) is the format-test DSL. getParsers implicitly adds acorn/espree/meriyah/oxc/yuku when babel is listed under tests/format/js|jsx; babel-ts/oxc-ts/yuku-ts when typescript is listed; hermes when flow is listed; __babel_estree when babel is listed.

test-format.js snapshots eolVisualizedOutput via createSnapshot; expectFail directories use toThrowErrorMatchingSnapshot. Additional FULL_TEST checks are described in CONTRIBUTING.md (compare AST, second format, CRLF/CR, BOM) and implemented under tests/config/format-test/.

tests/format is partitioned by language (js, jsx, typescript, flow, css, scss, less, html, vue, angular, markdown, mdx, yaml, graphql, handlebars, json, mjml, lwc, misc) with per-directory __snapshots__/format.test.js.snap. Flow’s tests/format/flow/flow-repo/ is synced via scripts/sync-flow-tests.cjs, not edited by hand.

Integration tests cover CLI behaviors (check, write, cache, patterns, ignore, stdin, plugins, config-resolution, experimental-cli, node-version-check, help-options) with snapshot files under tests/integration/__tests__/__snapshots__/.

Unit tests (tests/unit/) cover doc-printer, doc-builders, ast-path, visitor-keys, config-loader, resolve-parser, builtin-plugins, editorconfig-to-prettier, massage-ast; they are ignored when NODE_ENV=production. Bundle tests are ignored in development.

Production Jest installs the built package via tests/config/install-prettier.js into a temp node_modules/prettier (unless SKIP_PRODUCTION_INSTALL); TEST_STANDALONE and TEST_RUNTIME=browser remap the entry and skip tests/integration/. Browser tests skip several plugin/front-matter format tests.

package.json test scripts: test=jest; test:dev-package=INSTALL_PACKAGE=1; test:production=NODE_ENV=production; test:production-standalone=TEST_STANDALONE=1; test:production:browser with TEST_RUNTIME_BROWSER chrome|firefox and TEST_BUNDLE_FORMAT umd. Coverage via c8 include src/** and bin/**.

Lint CI also runs yarn lint:format-test (scripts/format-test-lint.js), prettier check on docs with PRETTIER_DEBUG=true so embedded format errors throw, yarn lint:deps, tsc, knip (separate lint:knip script), and codecov upload of coverage/lcov.info.

Release-script tests live in scripts/release/tests/; dts tests in tests/dts/unit/run.js (skipped on Node <=14). Dummy plugins under tests/config/prettier-plugins/ exercise embed/async printer/missing comments.

Prod CLI job runs dist/prettier on Node v0.10.48 solely to assert the engines check message 'Prettier requires at least version 14 of Node.js' — the production engine floor advertised by that job is 14, while package.json engines.node is >=22 for this source tree.

risk_map.summary: The largest security surface is intentional code execution: config files and plugins are imported from user-controlled paths, and --write overwrites arbitrary matched files. Plugin last-wins lets a later plugin replace builtin parsers/printers. Cache writes with restrictAccessToCwd:false. Generated plugin registries and the dist/ publish boundary are easy to edit in the wrong place. Option policy and the removed custom-parser API are social/API traps, not memory-safety bugs.

claims.claim: loadPlugin/importPlugin will import() a URL, an absolute path, a cwd-relative file, or a node_modules specifier via importFromDirectory (import-meta-resolve from a fake noop.js parent). This is how --plugin and config plugins run third-party code in-process.

JS/TS Prettier configs are executed, not parsed: loaders['.js'|'.mjs'|'.cjs'|'.ts'|'.mts'|'.cts'] = importModuleDefault via import(pathToFileURL(file)). External string configs try requireFromFile first then importFromFile.

--write calls mockable.writeFormattedFile(filename, output) which is fs.writeFile; expandPatterns can match any non-ignored file under cwd. docs/cli.md warns this overwrites files. process.exitCode is set per-file rather than aborting the whole run on a single IO error.

FormatResultsCache constructs file-entry-cache with restrictAccessToCwd: false. --cache-location can point anywhere that is not a directory; default falls back to os.tmpdir() if find-cache-directory fails.

Parser/printer lookup uses plugins.findLast, so a user or config plugin can silently replace babel/estree/html printers. Integration tests exist for plugin-override-builtin-printers and plugin-override-buitin-plugins (filename typo).

scripts/release/release.js uses child_process.exec(command) for git fetch --tags and yarn before importing run.js. The comment says it cannot use dependencies because they may not be installed yet. This is maintainer-only, not the formatter runtime.

development-plugins.js and production-plugins.js are generated ('do NOT edit'); editing them by hand will be overwritten by yarn generate-builtin-plugins. Production plugin graph (src/plugins/*.js) is a different split than language-* modules.

src/index.cjs in non-production throws if prettier.util or prettier.doc is accessed (ESM-only in dev CJS). Production CJS requires those files directly. Mixing NODE_ENV and CJS consumers is a support trap.
Custom Parser API was removed in v3.0.0 (docs/api.md); plugins must use the Plugin API. printer.embed with >2 parameters throws, telling authors the v3 plugin API changed.
No-new-options policy is enforced socially: CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/option-philosophy.md say option-request PRs are closed without discussion. Agents that add a formatting flag will be rejected.

handleError maps UndefinedParserError to exit 2 (or ignore with --ignore-unknown); ConfigError/validation calls process.exit(1) immediately (fails the whole CLI); parse errors set exitCode 2 and continue. Check mode uses exit 1 for unformatted files.

Website playground Worker loads /worker.mjs?version= and production Vite aliases npm deps to esm.sh CDN URLs (website/vite.config.mjs buildCdnAlias). That is a supply-chain/runtime dependency of prettier.io, not of the formatter library.

extension_points.summary: New languages are plugins: export languages/parsers/printers/options and load via --plugin, options.plugins, or config. Builtins are the same API, registered in the generated lazy-load tables. JS syntax work lands in src/language-js/parse and the printAngular/printJsx/printFlow/printTypescript/printEstree chain. Doc commands are the IR extension point. CLI flags are two tables (cli-options.evaluate.js and core-options.evaluate.js). Config file names are the CONFIG_FILES array.

claims.claim: A plugin is a module (default or named exports) with languages, parsers (parse/astFormat/locStart/locEnd/hasPragma/preprocess), printers (print/embed/massageAstNode/hasPrettierIgnore/getVisitorKeys), options, defaultOptions.

toLazyLoadPlugin turns {name, load, parsers[], printers[]} into objects whose parsers/printers entries are async thunks that import() the real module on first use — the intended way builtins stay tree-shakeable.

Adding a production-bundled parser means adding src/plugins/<name>.js (see src/plugins/babel.js re-exporting language-js/parse/babel plus json parsers) and regenerating production-plugins.js. Dev mode loads language-*/index.js instead.

JS printer extension: add a node-type handler in src/language-js/print/{estree,jsx,typescript,flow,angular}.js; printWithoutParentheses tries those five in order. Comment attachment hooks are canAttachComment/handleComments/willPrintOwnComments on the estree printer.

JS parser extension: export from src/language-js/parse/<engine>.js via createParser, then re-export from parse/index.js. babel.js documents the add/remove plugin checklist (tests/format/js/babel-plugins + scripts/update-babel-plugin-tests.js).

Doc IR extension for printers is the builders in src/document/builders (group, fill, ifBreak, indent, line, cursor, label, trim, …) plus printer.printDocToString. prettier.doc.utils exposes traverseDoc/mapDoc/willBreak. concat is a deprecated alias for identity on arrays, TODO remove in v4.

CLI option tables: src/cli/cli-options.evaluate.js (CLI-only) merged with API options from getSupportInfo via apiOptionToCliOption in get-context-options.js. New forwarded flags belong in core-options.evaluate.js with cliName/cliCategory.

CONFIG_FILES in config-searcher.js is the ordered list of config filenames; loaders.js maps extensions to load functions. Adding a config format means both arrays. Search uses search-closest FileSearcher with a stopDirectory mockable.

Language metadata is linguist-languages plus createLanguage() in each languages.evaluate.js (extensions, filenames, vscodeLanguageIds, interpreters). inferParser matches basename, then extension, then shebang interpreter.

In-repo extra plugins under packages/plugin-{oxc,hermes,yuku} are the template for shipping an alternate JS parser as a separate npm package: remap astFormat, reuse estree printer, export languages/options from the core tree. They are included in the dist build package list.

__debug APIs (parse, formatAST, formatDoc, printToDoc, printDocToString) and __internal (shared with CLI) are the in-tree hooks tests and the CLI use; they are not documented as stable public API. mockable objects in src/common/mockable.js and src/cli/mockable.js exist so tests can stub writeFormattedFile/isTTY/getTimestamp.
changelog_unreleased/<area>/<pr>.md plus yarn generate-changelog is the required contributor extension point for user-facing changes; PRs without it may be closed.

agent_handoff.summary: Read src/index.js, src/main/core.js, and the language module you are touching before editing. Do not add formatting options. Do not hand-edit generated builtin-plugin files; run generate-builtin-plugins. Format tests are snapshots — yarn test -u then git diff. Prefer small, reviewable diffs. Dev Node is >=22; production behavior is what dist/ does after yarn build. Run the matching tests/format/<lang> directory plus yarn test tests/unit if you change Doc/parser resolve.

claims.claim: Must-read first files for any change: package.json (scripts/exports), src/index.js (API), src/main/core.js (pipeline), src/main/parser-and-printer.js (plugin resolve), and CONTRIBUTING.md (test DSL + no-new-options).

Language work: edit src/language-<lang>/ (parse, print, embed, comments) and add a tests/format/<lang>/<topic>/ directory with format.test.js calling runFormatTest(import.meta, [parser]). Never add files next to format.test.js that you do not want snapshotted.

After changing languages.evaluate.js, options.js, or plugin parser/printer exports, run yarn generate-builtin-plugins (or yarn fix:builtin-plugins) so development-plugins.js and production-plugins.js stay in sync.

Safe edit boundaries: src/language-* printers and tests/format snapshots are the normal contributor surface. Avoid src/index.cjs dual ESM/CJS shim, bin/prettier.cjs version gate, and scripts/build/hacks/* unless the change is specifically about bundling.

Tests to run locally: yarn test <path> for a focused directory; yarn test -u to update snapshots; FULL_TEST=1 yarn test for AST/second-format/EOL/BOM. Production: yarn build then yarn test:production. Do not use yarn test:production without a dist/.
yarn debug <file> runs bin/prettier.js with --ignore-path=.prettierignore against the source tree (no dist needed). yarn perf / perf:inspect / perf:benchmark require a production build.

Trap: plugins listed last win. Tests that list ['babel','flow','typescript'] also run oxc/yuku/hermes/acorn/espree/meriyah implicitly — a JS print change can fail snapshots in those extra parsers even if babel looks fine.

Trap: standalone and website need explicit plugins (estree must be loaded to print JS). Node API autoloads builtins; copying Node samples into src/standalone.js consumers will fail with ConfigError 'Plugins must be explicitly added to the standalone bundle.'

Trap: prettier.util/doc are unavailable from the development CJS build. package.json main points at src/index.cjs, so require('prettier') in this checkout without NODE_ENV=production cannot use those namespaces.
PRs must follow .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md and add changelog_unreleased/<area>/<id>.md. AI-generated low-quality PRs are closed. ESLint + Prettier are required (yarn fix).

This repo’s own prettier.config.js forces parser meriyah for **/*.{js,mjs,cjs}, trailingComma none for bin/prettier.cjs, and jsonc for .vscode/*.json and tsconfig.json — dogfooding, not defaults for users.

Coverage tooling (c8 in package.json, codecov in Dev workflow) excludes src/standalone.js, src/index.cjs, src/plugins/**, and src/universal/*.browser.js — those paths can regress without coverage signal.
