overview.summary: Prisma 8 (root package @internal/monorepo at 8.0.0-rc.11) is a contract-first TypeScript data layer for application developers and coding agents. A schema is emitted as contract.json plus contract.d.ts; queries are a composable DSL compiled at runtime, not a generated client of findMany methods. The same contract gates migrations (control plane) and execution (runtime plane). Postgres and MongoDB are first-class targets, SQLite is a proof of concept, and dialect behavior is added as extension packs rather than branches in the core.

system_map.summary: The repo is a pnpm/Turbo workspace that requires Node >=24. Framework code lives under packages/1-framework, SQL and Mongo families under packages/2-*, concrete adapters under packages/3-targets and packages/3-mongo-target, and user-facing facades under packages/3-extensions with publishable shells in packages/9-public/@prisma. architecture.config.json assigns every glob a domain, layer, and plane; dependency-cruiser enforces those edges. The in-repo prisma binary is a stand-in that mounts the ORM command family; the published host is the separate prisma-cli repo. Local Postgres is docker-compose on port 5433; CI and npm publish run from GitHub Actions.

claims.claim: The workspace root is the private package @internal/monorepo version 8.0.0-rc.11, with packageManager pnpm@10.27.0 and engines.node >=24. pnpm build delegates to turbo run build; pnpm test:all chains test:packages, test:examples, test:integration, and test:e2e.

pnpm-workspace.yaml includes packages/**, examples/*, apps/*, and test/**, excludes **/dist-*, and pins a catalog (typescript 5.9.3, vitest 5.0.0-rc.2, arktype ^2.2.2, pg 8.22.0, vite 8.1.4). minimumReleaseAge is 1440 minutes, with explicit exclusions for @prisma/dev and prisma@7.10.0; trustPolicy is no-downgrade.

architecture.config.json maps globs to domain, layer, and plane. Framework-components splits shared, migration (src/control, exports/control.ts, exports/emission.ts), and runtime (src/execution, exports/runtime.ts). pnpm lint:deps runs dependency-cruiser plus lint-framework-target-imports, lint-app-space-id, and lint-single-import-root.

Cross-plane rule: migration must not import runtime; runtime may import migration only for artifacts; shared may be imported from either plane. Overlapping globs resolve most-specific-wins so src/core/migrations/** is migration even when src/core/** is shared.

Documented domains are Framework (packages/framework in the overview; on disk packages/1-framework), SQL family, Targets, and Extensions. Named internal packages include @internal/contract, @internal/emitter, @internal/cli, @internal/sql-runtime, @internal/adapter-postgres, @internal/driver-postgres, and @internal/postgres.

Two planes share contract.json: the control plane authors, plans, and applies contract changes; the execution plane compiles DSL/ORM/raw/TypedSQL plans. Both check storageHash and profileHash against a database marker and an append-only ledger.
The in-repo binary is @internal/cli's bin prisma -> ./dist/bin.mjs. bin.ts calls runOrmCli(process) and then unrefs stdin so the lsp stdio session cannot keep the process alive after settlement.

createOrmCli mounts ormCommandFamily under the binary name prisma. The file comment states this bin is a stand-in for the unified CLI whose real host lives in the prisma-cli repo and consumes ormCommandFamily. runtimeFromProcess sets managementApi.baseUrl to https://api.prisma.io and loadConfig to loadOrmConfig.

The user-facing Postgres install is @prisma/orm-postgres, described as the one package a Postgres application installs. It depends on @prisma/orm-family-sql, @prisma/orm-framework, @prisma/orm-target-postgres, @prisma/orm-toolchain, and pg, and re-exports adapter, builder, contract, control, and driver subpaths. @prisma/orm-toolchain packages the CLI family, emitter, config loader, language server, telemetry, and Vite plugin.

Turbo build depends on ^build and emits dist/**. typecheck depends on both ^build and build so packages that import their own published subpaths (for example @internal/extension-pgvector/pack) do not typecheck against a missing or stale dist.

docker-compose.yaml runs postgres:15-alpine, publishes host port 5433 to container 5432, sets POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres, and stores data on tmpfs. CI service containers separately use postgres:15 on port 5432 with user/password/db postgres.

Publish-to-npm triggers on push to main (tags excluded) and workflow_dispatch. An unchanged root version publishes a <base>-dev.N under the dev dist-tag; a version bump publishes latest and a GitHub Release (pre-release for 8.0.0-rc.N). docs/oss/versioning.md says publishing uses npm OIDC trusted publishing and that no long-lived NPM_TOKEN is stored.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface is the prisma CLI command family plus three database facades (postgres, mongo, sqlite) and extension packs. Contract commands are offline; db commands need a live connection; migration commands manage on-disk contract-to-contract edges and named refs. The language server speaks LSP over stdio. A Vite plugin re-emits the contract during dev. The Postgres client exposes sql, orm, raw, enums, transactions, and prepared statements, with a separate serverless entry that returns a connectable runtime.

claims.claim: ormCommandFamily registers these command keys: contract emit, contract format, contract infer, db init, db migrate, db schema, db sign, db update, db verify, lsp, migration check, migration graph, migration list, migration log, migration new, migration plan, migration ref delete, migration ref list, migration ref set, migration show, migration status, and orm init.

Retired invocations redirect rather than fuzzy-match: migration apply becomes {bin} db migrate --to <contract>; migration status --graph becomes migration graph; migration status --all and --limit become migration log --db <url>; migration status --ref becomes migration status --to <contract>.

BIN_GROUPS documents four user groups: orm (only init), contract (offline emit/sign/verify artifacts), db (live database; every command needs a connection), and migration plus migration ref (on-disk packages and named pointers such as staging/production under migrations/app/refs/). The telemetry group from @prisma/cli-engine is spread in beside them.

contract emit reads TypeScript or Prisma schema via the config source provider and writes contract.json and contract.d.ts. It is documented as offline (no database). Flags include --output-path. The human presentation prints storageHash, optional executionHash, and profileHash.

db update compares the live database to the emitted contract and applies additive, widening, and destructive operations. Destructive work requires typing the database name, or --no-interactive --confirm <database> when there is no TTY. --dry-run previews; --to accepts a hash, prefix, ref, migration directory, or path; --advance-ref moves a named ref.

lsp is a server command. It lazy-imports startServer from @internal/language-server, speaks stdio, accepts --clientProcessId from vscode-languageclient, and maps SIGTERM to exit 143 and other aborts to 130. The server publishes PSL diagnostics and whole-document formatting for contract.source.inputs.

README documents the product entrypoints npm create prisma (scaffolds Next.js, Hono, Nuxt, Astro, NestJS, SvelteKit, TanStack Start, or Elysia against PostgreSQL or MongoDB) and npx prisma orm init, which writes prisma.config.ts, a starter contract, and db.ts under src/prisma/. npx prisma skills sync installs per-workflow SKILL.md files.

Shipped extensions named in the README are @prisma/orm-extension-pgvector, @prisma/orm-extension-postgis, @prisma/orm-extension-paradedb (experimental BM25), @prisma/orm-extension-supabase (experimental), and @prisma/orm-extension-arktype-json. Postgres is the primary target, MongoDB is first-class, SQLite is a proof of concept, and MySQL is explicitly later.

The default postgres() factory returns a PostgresClient with sql, orm, enums, nativeEnums, raw, context, contract, stack, connect, runtime, transaction, prepare, close, and Symbol.asyncDispose. Passing contract keeps a no-emit TypeScript authoring path; passing contractJson requires an explicit Contract type parameter.

postgres/serverless exports a PostgresServerlessClient whose connect({ url }) returns a Runtime that is also AsyncDisposable. It still takes extensions, middleware, verifyMarker, and cursor options, and builds the same postgres target, adapter, and driver stack.

Mongo and SQLite each expose defineConfig that returns PrismaNextConfig<'mongo','mongo'> or PrismaNextConfig<'sql','sqlite'> and threads an extensions array into the core config. Mongo defineConfig accepts a .ts contract path or a PSL path with enum inference codecs.

prismaVitePlugin (default config prisma.config.ts, debounce 150ms) watches the contract source and calls the same executeContractEmit path as the CLI, serializing overlapping emits and ignoring writes to the emitted artifacts themselves.

data_flow.summary: Authoring starts in prisma.config.ts, where defineConfig binds a family, target, adapter, driver, and extensions to a contract source. Emit loads that source, enriches it with component descriptors, round-trips it through the target serializer, and writes a canonical JSON document plus a generated contract.d.ts. At runtime the Postgres client revalidates that JSON into a typed contract, and the SQL runtime lowers a query plan to SQL, encodes parameters, checks the marker, and decodes rows. Schema changes are a separate pipeline: introspect the database, plan a contract-space aggregate, and apply operations under a class policy. CLI telemetry is a side channel that forks a sender after the command settles.

claims.claim: Postgres defineConfig calls core defineConfig with family sql, target postgres, adapter postgresAdapter, driver postgresDriver, the caller extensions array, and a normalized contract config. Output defaults beside the first contract input when the caller omits it.

executeContractEmit is the single publication path for the CLI and the Vite plugin. It requires config.contract, a source.load function, and an output path; builds a control stack; calls source.load with composed extension ids, authoring contributions, codec lookup, and capabilities; then enrichContract, target serializeContract, and family deserializeContract before emit.

@internal/emitter emit rejects the call unless to-one relations declare nullability, canonicalizes with schemaVersion "1" via the target serializeContract hook, stamps a _generated warning, and returns contractJson, prettier-formatted contract.d.ts, storageHash, optional executionHash, and profileHash.

The emit JSDoc says publication is serialized per output JSON path by queueEmitByOutput (last submission wins) and that publishContractArtifactPair stages temp files, renames contract.d.ts before contract.json, and tries to restore the previous pair if a rename fails.

postgres() either serializes an in-memory contract or accepts contractJson, then always deserializes through PostgresContractSerializer so the runtime object is the validated form. A url binding becomes a pg Pool (connectionTimeoutMillis default 20000, idleTimeoutMillis default 30000) wrapped in suppressIdleConnectionErrors.

sql() builds a BuilderContext from contract capabilities, query operation types, target, storageHash, and mutation defaults, then returns a Proxy: the first key is a storage namespace id, the second is a table resolved by resolveTableInNamespace and wrapped in TableProxyImpl.

queryAgainstQueryable validates the codec registry once, calls prepareQueryExecution, buildDecodeContext, and streamRows. prepareOperation, for a not-yet-lowered plan, runs compilePlan, lowerToDraft, a SqlParamRefMutator before-hook, and encodeParams. streamRows then setupDriverExecution, runQueryWithMiddleware, and decodeRow.

verifyMarker reads the family marker. If the marker is absent it logs CONTRACT.MARKER_MISSING and returns. If storageHash or profileHash differs it logs CONTRACT.MARKER_MISMATCH and returns. It does not throw, so execution continues. The first call is single-flighted on verifyMarkerPromise unless verifyMarker was set to false.

executeDbUpdate uses policy classes additive, widening, and destructive and delegates to executeRun. db-run.ts documents the strategy as introspect then planMigration, and imports buildContractSpaceAggregate, planMigration, and runMigration. In apply mode without acceptDataLoss or consent, guardDestructiveChanges pre-plans and returns DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGES with databaseName and planHash.

createControlClient builds a ControlStack from family, target, adapter, driver, and extensions, creates the family instance, and asserts framework-component compatibility before any connect. connect refuses a second connection until close and errors with CONFIG.DB_CONNECTION_REQUIRED when no connection was supplied.

On non-CI processes with telemetry enabled, resolveTelemetryHooks prints a first-run notice, then onSettled fires runTelemetry with the command path, CLI version, exit code, and cwd. The sender forks detached. The POST URL is TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT_PATH /events on https://cmpbfbsdp09hr3jf7pojjs5qs.ewr.prisma.build, overridable only by PRISMA_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT.

loadContractFromTs bundles a user TypeScript contract with esbuild (platform node, target es2022) into a file under os.tmpdir named prisma-8-contract-*.mjs. The default import allowlist is @internal/*, @prisma/orm-*, and node:crypto. Imports from the entry that fail the allowlist become CONTRACT.SOURCE_IMPORT_DISALLOWED. Relative and absolute imports are not filtered.

behavior_traces.summary: Three flows dominate. Process startup wires telemetry, a CLI engine, and a host runtime, then dispatches one mounted command. Contract emit is offline: config, source provider, enrichment, canonical JSON, and a dts pair. A Postgres query stays lazy until first use, then compiles middleware, lowers SQL, encodes codecs, checks the marker, and streams decoded rows. db update is the persistence path: prepare a control client, pre-plan destructive work, and only then introspect, plan, and apply.

claims.claim: Startup order is bin.ts calling runOrmCli(process); runOrmCli calling resolveTelemetryHooks then createOrmCli().run(argv.slice(2), runtimeFromProcess(proc), hooks). A throw before a command exists is caught by reportStartupFailure, which writes a single stderr line and returns exit code 1.

createOrmCli builds the engine with name prisma, version from the CLI package.json, commandFamilies [ormCommandFamily], groups BIN_GROUPS, and commands BIN_COMMANDS. BIN_COMMANDS is createBinCommands(createControlClient), so db and migration commands close over the real control client while tests can inject a double.

runtimeFromProcess copies stdout, stderr, stdin, cwd, env, TTY flags, Node version, platform, and arch; registers SIGINT and SIGTERM; sets loadConfig to loadOrmConfig; sets managementApi.baseUrl to https://api.prisma.io; and installs runPackageManager as the package-manager capability. The engine, not the bin, owns signal policy.

contract emit handler order: resolve optional --output-path against ctx.cwd; call executeContractEmit with config, cwd, controlProgressReporter, and AbortSignal; surface validationWarning; build an EmitDocument with hashes and files; return ok(ctx.present(...)). The command factory injects executeContractEmitOperation as the dependency.

Inside executeContractEmit the ordered steps are: require config.contract and source.load; getEmittedArtifactPaths; queueEmitByOutput; createControlStack(config); source.load(sourceContext); validateProviderResult; family.create plus assertFrameworkComponentsCompatible; enrichContract; serializeContract; deserializeContract; emitter emit with the project import-specifier resolver.

Emitter emit order is requireToOneRelationNullability, canonicalizeContractToObject (schemaVersion 1 plus the target serializer), JSON.stringify of the canonical object with a _generated banner, generateContractDts, and prettier format (typescript parser, singleQuote, semi, printWidth 100).

postgres() query startup order: resolveContract; resolveOptionalPostgresBinding; createSqlExecutionStack({ target: postgresTarget, adapter: postgresAdapter, driver: postgresDriver, extensions }); createExecutionContext; buildPostgresStaticContext for the sql Proxy, raw tag, enums, and native enums. ormBuilder delegates query, execute, and connection to getRuntime().

getRuntime order on first use: instantiateExecutionStack; driverDescriptor.create({ cursor: { disabled: true } }); if a binding exists, connectDriver in the background; construct PostgresRuntimeImpl with context, adapter, driver, verifyMarker, and middleware. A later call after close() throws DRIVER.NOT_CONNECTED. connectDriver turns a url into a Pool and connects the driver once.

Row execution order on SqlRuntimeBase: query calls queryAgainstQueryable; that calls ensureCodecRegistryValidated, prepareQueryExecution, buildDecodeContext, and streamRows. prepareQueryExecution ends in prepareOperation. For a query plan, prepareOperation calls compilePlan (runBeforeCompileChain), lowerToDraft (lowerSqlPlan), the before-hook mutator, and encodeDraftParams. streamRows calls setupDriverExecution (verifyMarker), runQueryWithMiddleware, queryable.query({ sql, params }), and decodeRow, checking the abort signal between rows.

withTransaction order: runtime.connection(), connection.transaction(), invoke the callback with a guarded query/execute surface, set invalidated in a finally, then transaction.commit(). A callback throw triggers rollback; if rollback throws, the connection is destroy()ed and the error is RUNTIME.TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK_FAILED with the original as cause. A failed commit attempts rollback and destroys the connection if that also fails. The connection is release()d when it was not destroyed.

db update handler starts with prepareMigrationRun({ config, cwd, db, commandName: 'db update', createClient }). The operation layer then either returns the destructive-change refusal from a plan-mode executeRun or calls executeRun in the requested mode with the consented plan hash.

Non-CI telemetry order: resolveGating against env and the user config file; if no installationId, write the first-run notice that names DO_NOT_TRACK, PRISMA_DISABLE_TELEMETRY, and enableTelemetry; return an onSettled hook. The hook calls ensureInstallationId if needed and runTelemetry, which returns immediately with spawned true, gated-off, ci, or fork-failed. Failures are swallowed.

testing_signals.summary: Vitest is the package, integration, and e2e runner. The root config discovers every package vitest.config.ts, forces telemetry off, and on CI caps workers at 50% because PGlite plus Postgres oversubscribes the runner. Package tests are sharded four ways with v8 coverage; integration tests are also sharded but, until about 2026-08-21, do not run in merge queue. A large scorecard separates features proven by a database integration test from features that are only unit-tested. Fixture drift is a git diff of emitted contract files, not an ad-hoc snapshot.

claims.claim: Root vitest.config.ts sets test.projects to packages/**/vitest.config.ts, env.PRISMA_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1, and maxWorkers 50% when CI is set. Coverage uses @vitest/coverage-v8 via provider v8, reportOnFailure, and composeCoverageConfig. A VITEST_COVERAGE_SHARD env var suppresses text/json reporters and thresholds so shards can emit blobs.

pnpm test:packages builds everything except examples and test workspaces, then runs vitest run. pnpm test:e2e is pnpm --filter e2e-tests test. pnpm test:integration is pnpm --filter integration-tests test. pnpm test:journeys and pnpm test:vite-plugin are separate integration-tests scripts.

integration-tests pretest builds integration-tests and the postgres, mongo, and pgvector public packages. Its test script is vitest run. test:journeys uses vitest.journeys.config.ts. The tree includes cli-journeys e2e files, authoring parity fixtures, sql-orm-client suites, mongo runtime tests, and vite-plugin.hmr.e2e.test.ts.

e2e-tests emit runs prisma contract emit against test/fixtures/prisma.config.ts and the sqlite fixture config. The Testing Guide says e2e loads committed fixtures under test/fixtures/generated/contract.json instead of emitting on every test, with one emission check.

CI workflow CI (PR) triggers on pull_request and merge_group with permissions contents: read and cancel-in-progress concurrency. An inert-diff job lets docs-only PRs skip expensive steps. The build job runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, pnpm build, and pnpm check:clean-tree.

The lint job runs lint:deps, lint:code, lint:packages, lint:examples, lint:rules, lint:rules:symlinks, lint:skills, lint:rules:footprint, lint:docs, lint:manifests, lint:workflows, test:scripts, lint:casts, lint:throws, lint:framework-vocabulary, lint:consumer-internal-imports, lint:legacy-name, lint:vitest-timeouts, lint:publishability, check:upgrade-coverage, check:error-reference, and check:release-notes.

Package tests run as a 4-way matrix on ubuntu with a postgres:15 service, TEST_TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER=2, and pnpm coverage:packages --shard=i/4 writing blob reports. Coverage merges the four blobs with pnpm coverage:packages:merge and pnpm coverage:report. Examples tests start the cloudflare-worker compose Postgres on 5433 and fetch the Prisma 7 schema engine for prisma7-adoption.

Integration tests are sharded 1/4 through 4/4 via pnpm test:integration --shard. The job comment says that until about 2026-08-21 they do not run on merge_group, still run on every PR, and also run nightly from integration-nightly.yml. E2E runs pnpm test:e2e against postgres:15 unless the diff is inert.

A supabase-acceptance job (timeout 25 minutes) installs a pinned Supabase CLI 2.95.4 by checksummed tarball and starts a local stack from examples/supabase so role, grant, and JWT behavior is tested against real Supabase defaults, not only a hermetic shim.

pnpm fixtures:check runs fixtures:emit (examples, selected apps, sql-builder, sql-orm-client, postgres, extension-supabase, e2e-tests, integration-tests, plus extension contract spaces and migration regen) and then git diff --exit-code on **/contract.* and **/expected.contract.json.

pnpm test:scripts runs node --test on dozens of scripts/*.test.mjs and scripts/*.test.ts files (coverage, workflow triggers, publish deps, casts, skills, package manifests). That is the Node test runner, not Vitest.

scorecard.md defines ✅ as proven by a Prisma 8 integration test that hits Postgres (PGlite), SQLite, or MongoDB (mongodb-memory-server) and asserts a runtime result. Unit tests of SQL, AST, plans, or types do not qualify. 🟡 means the public surface is reachable but no such integration test exists. Categories include 123 migration rows and 32 CLI-command rows.

risk_map.summary: The sharp edges are warn-only marker checks, a contract loader that bundles and imports user TypeScript from the temp directory, package-manager and telemetry child processes, and a destructive migration consent flow that can be satisfied non-interactively. Supply-chain controls exist (frozen lockfile, release-age cooldown, OIDC publish, least-privilege CI tokens) but several trust exclusions are intentional. SQLite is not at parity, integration tests do not block the merge queue during the launch window, and the in-repo CLI can drift from the external prisma-cli host.

claims.claim: verifyMarker never throws. CONTRACT.MARKER_MISSING and CONTRACT.MARKER_MISMATCH are log.warn events, after which setupDriverExecution continues into runQueryWithMiddleware. A database whose marker does not match the contract still serves queries unless a caller set verifyMarker to a stricter mode outside this default path.

loadContractFromTs writes an esbuild bundle to os.tmpdir and, on the lines read, is about to import that module. The allowlist plugin ignores relative and absolute specifiers (args.path starting with . or /). Only bare imports from the entry are checked against @internal/*, @prisma/orm-*, and node:crypto. A contract file can therefore pull arbitrary relative modules into the bundle.

runPackageManager spawns request.file with request.args, cwd, and signal, piping stdout to the engine and keeping only the last 64 KiB of stderr. The bin comment says the CLI engine chooses the manager and the argv and never imports child_process itself, so a bug in argv composition becomes a shell-out.
redactSecrets only strips URL userinfo and _authToken/_auth/_password assignments from package-manager stderr during init. It does not scrub database URLs in general command output.

Telemetry is on by default outside CI. resolveTelemetryHooks returns undefined when isCI() is true or resolveGating says disabled. Otherwise a detached fork POSTs to a compile-time backend URL. A malformed PRISMA_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT falls back to production rather than failing closed. The root vitest config sets PRISMA_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 so tests do not fork the sender.

The private app telemetry-backend (bun >=1.3 or node >=24) is the storage side of that channel: scripts include deploy, prisma contract emit, and start via bun run src/server.ts, and it depends on @prisma/orm-postgres. The sender URL is a Prisma Compute host, not this app's source path.

db update's destructive gate is skippable. executeDbUpdate only calls guardDestructiveChanges when mode is apply and both acceptDataLoss and consent are unset. The CLI help says a CI or --no-interactive run takes the database name from --confirm. Consent is bound to a planHash and a mismatch returns CONSENT_PLAN_MISMATCH, but a matching hash or acceptDataLoss applies destructive ops.

CI integration tests are explicitly not merge-blocking during the launch window: the test-integration job is skipped when github.event_name == merge_group. Package tests, e2e, and fixtures still run unless the diff is inert. A green merge queue therefore does not include the integration shard.

scorecard.md records large areas that are implemented but only unit-tested (🟡) or absent (❌). SQLite is described in the README as a proof of concept, and MySQL is not a target yet. A passing package suite is not evidence that every scorecard row is ✅.

Root pnpm.overrides force hono 4.11.4, js-yaml 3.14.2, lodash 4.17.23, minimatch patches, and rollup 4.59.0. That is a supply-chain pin, not a removal of those libraries. CI installs with --frozen-lockfile.

The in-repo prisma bin and the published CLI are different repositories. cli.ts says this process mounts ormCommandFamily the same way the prisma-cli host does, but nothing in this repo compiles that host. Behavioral drift between the two is possible if one side changes command paths or config loading.

runtimeFromProcess always sets managementApi.baseUrl to https://api.prisma.io. Combined with the telemetry sender and the package-manager spawn, a normal CLI invocation can perform network and process side effects even for commands whose own handler is offline, unless telemetry gating suppresses the fork.

extension_points.summary: New behavior is supposed to arrive as a composed descriptor, not a core branch. The control stack orders extension packs and merges authoring contributions, codecs, aggregates, and capabilities. The same extensions array is accepted by defineConfig and by the postgres() runtime options. CLI commands are a record passed to defineCommandFamily, with a factory injection point for the control client. Public npm names are thin shells over internal packages. pgvector is the concrete pattern: a pack meta id, authoring types, a codec registry, and SQL lowering templates.

claims.claim: createControlStack takes family, target, adapter, driver, and extensions. It orders extensions with buildExtensionLoadOrder, then assembleAuthoringContributions over family, target, optional adapter, and those extensions. The returned stack carries codecLookup, codecDescriptors, aggregateDescriptors, authoringContributions, scalarTypes, controlMutationDefaults, and a merged capability matrix.

assembleAuthoringContributions walks each descriptor's authoring.entityTypes and claims paths so two packs cannot occupy the same entity slot. The architecture overview names AuthoringContributions.entityTypes as the way a target adds entity kinds without the framework branching on target identity.
Postgres, Mongo, and SQLite defineConfig all default extensions to [] and pass that array into the core config. Adding a pack is a config edit, not an edit to the family runtime.

postgres() accepts extensions?: readonly SqlRuntimeExtensionDescriptor<'postgres'>[] and middleware?: readonly SqlMiddleware[], and forwards extensions into createSqlExecutionStack and middleware into PostgresRuntimeImpl. SqlRuntimeBase checks each middleware with checkMiddlewareCompatibility(mw, 'sql', target) in the constructor.

pgvector's pack meta is kind extension, id pgvector, familyId sql, targetId postgres, and declares capability postgres['pgvector.cosine']. Its authoring.type is pgvectorAuthoringTypes and its codec descriptors come from pgvectorCodecRegistry. The default export of exports/pack.ts is pgvectorPackMeta.

pgvectorQueryOperations registers cosineDistance and cosineSimilarity on codec pg/vector@1. cosineDistance lowers with template {{self}} <=> {{arg0}} to codec pg/float8@1. That is the extension operation registry the SQL builder consults via queryOperationTypes.

CLI commands plug in as a Readonly<Record<string, AnyCommand>> passed to defineCommandFamily, plus a redirects array for retired spellings. defineOrmCommand wraps @prisma/cli-engine defineCommand with the ORM error boundary so new commands should not call defineCommand directly.

createBinCommands(createClient) is the test seam: swapping CreateControlClient remounts db init, db migrate, db schema, db sign, db update, db verify, migration new, and migration plan without mocking modules. Offline commands stay the real implementations.

Target packages are expected to export three planes: src/exports/control.ts (migration), src/exports/runtime.ts (runtime), and src/exports/pack.ts (shared). New targets must register those globs, including src/core/migrations/** even before the directory exists, or later files inherit the shared plane and hide violations.

Emitter options are the family SPI: serializeContract, deserializeContract, shouldPreserveEmpty, sortStorage, supportsNamespaces, and resolveImportSpecifier. The framework does not walk the in-memory contract with Object.entries; the target serializer owns the JSON shape.

The Vite plugin and the CLI are two front doors onto executeContractEmit. A third authoring path is no-emit: pass a TypeScript contract object straight to postgres({ contract }) and skip the files. Both still deserialize through PostgresContractSerializer.

Skills are an extension surface for agents. Canonical files live in skills-contrib/; the prepare script runs skills add ./skills-contrib and sync-agent-rules. Published facades copy skills in prepack (orm-postgres prepack runs scripts/sync-package-skills.ts). README says each installed Prisma package ships the SKILL.md files that match that version.

agent_handoff.summary: Agents should treat this as a layered contract compiler plus a runtime, not as a Next.js app. Start from Agents.md, the architecture overview, and architecture.config.json. Use pnpm on Node 24, rebuild before typecheck, and do not bypass lint:deps. Tests are written first and run with Vitest; name the Contract type at every JSON boundary; never use any, zod, or a bare cast. Skills and rules have one canonical directory each. The traps that waste a session are stale dist types, plane violations, fixture drift, warn-only marker checks, and editing a gitignored symlink tree.

claims.claim: Agents.md requires Node from the shell (engines.node in the root package.json; do not run nvm/fnm), pnpm instead of npm, and never npx. Build with pnpm build. Use the repo scripts pnpm typecheck and pnpm test rather than hand-rolled tsc or vitest. Use arktype, not zod. Never add extensions to TypeScript imports.

Type rules from Agents.md: never any; never @ts-expect-error outside negative type tests; never @ts-nocheck; never suppress biome lints; no bare as in production code. Use blindCast or castAs from @internal/utils/casts. as const and test files are exempt. pnpm lint:casts is the ratchet.

Write tests before changing implementation. Omit the word should in test names. In sql-orm-client tests, assert the whole result shape with toEqual or a snapshot and an explicit select. Do not reexport from one file to another except under exports/ folders. Do not add backwards-compat exports unless asked. Do not branch on target; add an adapter.

Where JSON enters the runtime, name the contract.d.ts type: postgres<Contract>({ contractJson, url }) or validateSqlContractFully<Contract>(contractJson). Do not use a wide generic such as SqlContract<SqlStorage>. The postgres() overloads encode that split between a live contract object and contractJson.

After changing exported types in a package other packages consume, rebuild that package so dist/*.d.mts updates before downstream typecheck. Turbo already makes typecheck depend on build and ^build because self-imports of published subpaths read dist.

Safe command set for a small change: pnpm build for the touched package, pnpm test:packages or that package's vitest, pnpm typecheck:packages, and pnpm lint:deps if imports moved. Contract artifact edits need pnpm fixtures:check rather than a hand-rolled emit-and-diff. Integration behavior needs pnpm test:integration; CLI journeys need pnpm test:journeys.

Edit skills at skills-contrib/<name>/SKILL.md and rules at .agents/rules/<name>.mdc. .claude, .cursor, and .agents skill/rule trees are presentation symlinks materialized by prepare (skills add and scripts/sync-agent-rules.mjs). A rule added only under .cursor/rules is gitignored and lost. pnpm rules:sync and pnpm lint:rules:symlinks check the trees.

New packages must be registered in architecture.config.json with plane-specific globs, broad to specific, including a migration glob for src/core/migrations/** even if the directory is empty. pnpm lint:deps fails the PR if a migration file imports a runtime package.

Every workspace package, including examples and the private root, carries the same version. docs/oss/versioning.md says internal packages are not published, extension authors must pin framework internals to an exact minor, and RC releases may break. Do not bump a single package.json by hand; pnpm bump-version is the maintainer path.

Files to read before editing a query path: packages/3-extensions/postgres/src/runtime/postgres.ts, packages/2-sql/4-lanes/sql-builder/src/runtime/sql.ts, and packages/2-sql/5-runtime/src/sql-runtime.ts. Before editing emit or migrations: packages/1-framework/3-tooling/cli/src/control-api/operations/contract-emit.ts, emitter/src/emit.ts, and db-update.ts. Subsystem index pages live under docs/architecture docs/subsystems/.

Known traps: verifyMarker logs and continues; loadContractFromTs allows relative imports; the CLI bin here is not the published prisma host; integration tests do not run in merge_group during the launch window; PGlite-heavy suites need the CI worker cap or they drop Postgres sockets; typecheck against a dirty dist lies.

Do not start a dev server or a migration against a caller-supplied production URL from this repo without an explicit ask. docker-compose.yaml is a disposable local Postgres on 5433. db update can destroy data once consent or --confirm is provided. Telemetry posts to a production Compute URL unless disabled.

readmePreview: Welcome to Rails What's Rails? Rails is a web application framework that includes everything needed to create database-backed web applications according to the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern.

overview.summary: Ruby on Rails 8.2.0.alpha is a monorepo of loosely coupled gems that together implement a Model-View-Controller web framework. The meta-gem rails pins Active Support, Active Model, Active Record, Action View, Action Pack, Action Mailer, Active Job, Action Cable, Active Storage, Action Mailbox, Action Text, and Railties to one version and requires Ruby >= 3.3.1. Applications are created and driven by the rails CLI in Railties; boot is a Railtie initializer pipeline, HTTP is a Rack middleware stack plus the Journey router, and persistence is Active Record over sqlite3, mysql2/trilogy, or postgresql. This tree is distinctive for versioned load_defaults through 8.2 (header-only CSRF, YJIT, enqueue-after-commit), encrypted credentials, multi-database connections, and first-party engines for jobs, WebSockets, file storage, inbound email, and rich text.

system_map.summary: The repository root is a Bundler workspace plus an npm workspace, not a single application. railties/exe/rails is the user-facing executable; rails/all.rb is the full framework require list; Rails::Application#initialize! is the runtime boot boundary. Persistence and file storage sit behind adapter registries. The in-repo test entry points are Rake and each component's bin/test. Gem and npm publishing is tools/releaser, triggered by the GitHub Actions release workflow; the full suite gate documented for releases is Buildkite, whose pipeline YAML is not in this checkout.

claims.claim: RAILS_VERSION is 8.2.0.alpha and rails.gemspec requires Ruby >= 3.3.1 and RubyGems >= 1.8.11, with MIT license and rubygems_mfa_required metadata.

The meta-gem depends on activesupport, actionpack, actionview, activemodel, activerecord, actionmailer, activejob, actioncable, activestorage, actionmailbox, actiontext, and railties, each at the same version, plus bundler >= 1.15.0.
railties/exe/rails unshifts railties/lib onto $LOAD_PATH when a sibling .git directory exists, then requires rails/cli.

Rails::AppLoader.exec_app walks parent directories looking for bin/rails or script/rails and execs Gem.ruby on that binstub when the file references APP_PATH or ENGINE_PATH; a Bundler-generated bin/rails prints BUNDLER_WARNING and then requires config/boot plus rails/commands.
In-app dispatch is railties/lib/rails/commands.rb, which maps g, d, c, s, db, r, and t onto generate, destroy, console, server, dbconsole, runner, and test, then calls Rails::Command.invoke.

rails/all.rb requires, in order, active_record/railtie, active_storage/engine, action_controller/railtie, action_view/railtie, action_mailer/railtie, active_job/railtie, action_cable/engine, action_mailbox/engine, action_text/engine, and rails/test_unit/railtie, swallowing LoadError only when the missing path is that railtie.

Rails::Application#initialize! runs Bootstrap.initializers_for, then railties_initializers, then Finisher.initializers_for, and refuses a second call. Bootstrap loads Active Support, the logger, the error reporter, the cache, and the once-autoloader; Finisher builds the middleware stack, eager-loads, adds internal routes, and enables YJIT.

DefaultMiddlewareStack#build_stack assembles HostAuthorization, optional AssumeSSL and SSL, Static, Executor, RequestId, RemoteIp, Logger, ShowExceptions, DebugExceptions, Reloader, Cookies, the configured session store, Flash, ContentSecurityPolicy, and optional ActiveRecord DatabaseSelector and ShardSelector middleware.

ActiveRecord.protocol_adapters maps DATABASE_URL schemes sqlite to sqlite3, mysql to mysql2, and postgres to postgresql; external adapters may replace those strings. The root Gemfile's :db group installs pg, mysql2, and trilogy, and sqlite3 is a default dependency.

ActiveStorage::Service documents Disk, GCS, S3, and Mirror. Service.configure delegates to Service::Configurator.build, which require's active_storage/service/<name>_service and instantiates the matching Service subclass. Registry#fetch memoizes built services from the YAML configuration hash.

Root Rakefile task test iterates Releaser::FRAMEWORKS and runs rake test in each directory; task smoke does the same except Active Record, which runs sqlite3:test. Per-adapter tasks exist for mysql2, trilogy, postgresql, sqlite3, and sqlite3_mem, plus activerecord:db:create/drop/rebuild.

Releaser::FRAMEWORKS is ordered so dependents follow dependencies, ending in railties. The release GitHub workflow checks out the repo, configures RubyGems trusted publishing and npm, bundle-installs tools/releaser, and runs bundle exec rake push.

package.json is a private npm workspace of actioncable, actiontext, and activestorage. @rails/actioncable, @rails/actiontext, and @rails/activestorage are versioned 8.2.0-alpha, matching RAILS_VERSION.

RELEASING_RAILS.md tells releasers to treat https://buildkite.com/rails/rails as the CI status and not to release on red CI. This checkout has no .buildkite directory; the GitHub workflows that do exist cover release publishing, a rails-new Docker smoke, rail_inspector, markdown, devcontainer, labeling, and staleness.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface area is the rails CLI, the generators that stamp a new app, the Rack endpoints mounted by the framework itself, and the adapter-backed subsystems for jobs, cable, storage, mail, and passwords. Generated apps load framework defaults for the version they were created with and, unless skipped, depend on Solid Cache, Solid Queue, Solid Cable, Thruster, and Kamal. Guides and bug-report templates are part of the product, not side docs.

claims.claim: Command classes under railties/lib/rails/commands include about, application, boot, console, credentials, dbconsole, destroy, dev, devcontainer, encrypted, generate, help, initializers, middleware, new, notes, plugin, query, rake, restart, routes, runner, secret, server, stats, test, unused_routes, and version.

ServerCommand#perform requires APP_PATH, chdirs to Rails.application.root, and starts Rails::Server. Defaults are port 3000, pid tmp/pids/server.pid, config.ru, and recommended Rack handler puma; supported handler names include cgi, webrick, scgi, thin, puma, unicorn, falcon, fastcgi, and lsws. Host defaults to localhost in development and 0.0.0.0 otherwise.

The app generator template Gemfile.tt includes solid_cache, solid_queue, and solid_cable, adds thruster unless skip_thruster, and adds kamal unless skip_kamal. The root Gemfile mirrors those gems for framework tests, with kamal >= 2.1.0 and thruster require: false.

Generated config/application.rb calls config.load_defaults with the generator's config_target_version, or Rails::VERSION::STRING.to_f for dummy apps. A new_framework_defaults_8_2.rb.tt initializer tells upgraders to uncomment flags and then set load_defaults to 8.2.

CredentialsCommand implements edit, show, diff, and fetch. edit opens the decrypted YAML in $VISUAL or $EDITOR, writing config/credentials/<env>.yml.enc and a sibling .key when an environment is specified. fetch walks a dotted YAML path.
RunnerCommand#perform boots the app and either evals stdin, Kernel.loads a .rb file, or evals the argument string in TOPLEVEL_BINDING, optionally inside the Rails executor.

Rails::HealthController#show renders HTML or JSON status up with 200, and rescue_from(Exception) renders status down with 500. The controller comment states the endpoint does not check the database or Redis and that new apps route it at /up via rails/health#show.

In development, Finisher#add_internal_routes prepends /rails/info/properties, /rails/info/routes, /rails/info/notes, /rails/info, and a Chrome DevTools well-known path, and appends GET / to rails/welcome#index. WelcomeController skips forgery protection and renders without a layout.

Action Mailbox draws unauthenticated-looking ingress routes under /rails/action_mailbox for Postmark, Relay, Sendgrid, Mandrill (HEAD health check plus POST), and Mailgun (mime). A conductor UI under rails/conductor/action_mailbox exposes inbound email index, create, reroute, and incinerate.

Active Storage routes, under ActiveStorage.routes_prefix, serve blob redirect and proxy, representation redirect and proxy, disk GET and PUT, and POST /direct_uploads when draw_direct_upload_route is set. Signed ids are the public identifier.

ActionCable.server memoizes ActionCable::Server::Base. The internal protocol table uses message types welcome, disconnect, ping, confirm_subscription, and reject_subscription, default mount path /cable, and protocols actioncable-v1-json and actioncable-unsupported. Redis and PostgreSQL subscription adapters are not eager-loaded.

Active Job's default queue adapter is :async. QueueAdapters.lookup constantizes the camelized name plus Adapter. Built-ins are async, inline, and test; optional backends are backburner, delayed_job, queue_classic, resque, and sneakers. The file states new adapter pull requests are not accepted.

ActiveRecord::Encryption::EncryptableRecord#encrypts declares encrypted attributes with deterministic, downcase, ignore_case, previous schemes, and compression options. ActiveModel::SecurePassword.register_algorithm ships :bcrypt and :argon2; has_secure_password defaults to BCryptPassword when algorithm is nil. The root Gemfile loads bcrypt and argon2 with require: false so Active Model does not depend on those native gems.

Rails::Generators.invoke finds classes whose files end in _generator.rb under rails/generators or generators, trying base:name, name:context, name:name, rails:name, and configured fallbacks. Hidden namespaces include app, plugin, encrypted_file, encryption_key_file, master_key, credentials, and db:system:change.

Guides source lives in guides/source (getting_started.md covers app layout, REST, and Kamal deploy). Bug reports are expected to start from guides/bug_report_templates for Active Record, migrations, Action View, Active Job, Active Storage, Action Mailer, Action Mailbox, Action Pack, or the generic template.

data_flow.summary: Three boundaries dominate. HTTP enters as a Rack env, passes DefaultMiddlewareStack, and is recognized by Journey into a controller action whose callbacks and render produce a Rack triple. Records enter through Active Record attribute hashes, are validated and callback-wrapped, then inserted or updated on a leased connection. Secrets enter as ENV or a key file, are decrypted with AES-128-GCM, and feed secret_key_base, which signs and encrypts cookies and messages. Jobs, uploads, and filtered logs are side channels off those paths.

claims.claim: RouteSet#call builds a request, normalizes path_info with Journey::Router::Utils.normalize_path, and calls @router.serve. Journey::Router#serve yields each match to route.app.serve and returns the response unless the X_CASCADE header is pass; otherwise it returns 404.

RouteSet::Dispatcher#serve reads path parameters, instantiates the controller response, and calls controller.dispatch. On RoutingError it re-raises only when @raise_on_name_error is set; otherwise it returns a 404 cascade triple.

ActionController::Metal#dispatch assigns the request and response, calls process(name), commits the flash, and returns to_a. AbstractController::Base#process sets @_action_name, raises ActionNotFound when _find_action_name fails, and calls process_action. Callbacks#process_action wraps super in run_callbacks(:process_action).

Journey path captures are CGI.unescapeURIComponent'd when they contain % and then forced to UTF-8 before being merged with route defaults. recognize_path separately binary-encodes and URI-unescapes string params and raises RoutingError when the controller constant is missing.

Persistence#save calls create_or_update and returns false on RecordInvalid. create_or_update raises if the record is readonly, returns false if destroyed, and chooses _create_record or _update_record. _create_record filters attributes_for_create, opens with_connection, calls _insert_record with _returning_columns_for_insert, writes returned columns, and clears @new_record.

ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection resolves a symbol or hash via resolve_config_for_connection and delegates to connection_handler.establish_connection with owner_name, current_role, and current_shard. connects_to accepts database: or shards: but not both, and only on Base or abstract classes. ConnectionPool#lease_connection checks out a connection once per thread and marks the lease sticky.

secret_key_base prefers ENV[SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY] (a generated local secret), then ENV[SECRET_KEY_BASE], then credentials.secret_key_base, then a generated secret when Rails.env.local?. A missing non-local secret raises ArgumentError naming bin/rails credentials:edit. Application#key_generator memoizes an ActiveSupport::CachingKeyGenerator per secret, used for MessageVerifier and MessageEncryptor including cookies.

ActiveSupport::EncryptedFile uses cipher aes-128-gcm. #key reads the env var named by env_key, then the key file, then raises MissingKeyError if raise_if_missing_key. #read decrypts content_path.binread. generate_key is SecureRandom.hex of MessageEncryptor.key_len, and a key of any other length raises InvalidKeyLengthError.

Application#creds returns ActiveSupport::CombinedConfiguration. In development the lookup order is envs, then dotenv, then encrypted credentials; in other environments dotenv is omitted. The documented API is creds.require and creds.option.

ActiveJob::Enqueuing::ClassMethods#perform_later instantiates the job and calls enqueue. The class attribute enqueue_after_transaction_commit defaults to false in the module, but load_defaults 8.2 sets active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true so new 8.2 apps defer enqueue until the outermost transaction commits.

ActionDispatch::Http::FilterParameters#filtered_parameters runs ActiveSupport::ParameterFilter over the request parameters and substitutes matches with the mask [FILTERED]. ParseError yields an empty hash so a bad body does not leak into logs via the filter path.

sanitize_sql_for_conditions sends Arrays through sanitize_sql_array and quotes bound values, but returns a bare String unchanged. The comment states the helper is not schema-aware and that MySQL numeric binds are quoted as strings.

An upload enters ActiveStorage::Service#upload(key, io, checksum:) and, when a checksum is given, must raise ActiveStorage::IntegrityError on mismatch. Disk, S3, GCS, and Mirror are selected by the service: key in the configuration passed to Service.configure, not by a hardcoded global.

behavior_traces.summary: Four flows are fully ordered in source: process start for an existing app, one HTTP request after boot, an Active Record insert, and editing encrypted credentials. Action Cable's socket open and Active Job's perform_later are shorter traces on the same boot. Names below are the methods actually called, not a conceptual MVC sketch.

claims.claim: Startup outside an app: railties/exe/rails requires rails/cli; cli.rb calls Rails::AppLoader.exec_app; if that returns, ARGV is help, plugin, or application, and Rails::Command.invoke dispatches gem_help, plugin, or application (rails new).

Startup inside an app: AppLoader#exec_app finds bin/rails and execs it, so the gem CLI stops. The binstub eventually loads railties/lib/rails/commands.rb, which shifts ARGV and calls Rails::Command.invoke. Command#invoke splits namespace, find_by_namespace loads *_command.rb, and command.perform runs, falling through to the rake command when no Thor command matches.

rails server order: ServerCommand#perform calls set_application_directory! and prepare_restart, constructs Rails::Server with server_options, requires APP_PATH, Dir.chdir(Rails.application.root), then Server#start. start traps INT, create_tmp_directories (tmp/cache, tmp/pids, tmp/sockets), setup_dev_caching in development, optionally log_to_stdout, then Rackup::Server#start.

Application boot order inside require APP_PATH: the Application subclass is defined, then initialize!(group = :default) calls run_initializers. initializers concatenates Bootstrap (:load_environment_hook, :load_active_support, :set_eager_load, :initialize_logger, :initialize_error_reporter, :initialize_event_reporter, :initialize_cache, :setup_once_autoloader, :bootstrap_hook), each railtie's initializers, then Finisher (:setup_default_session_store, :build_middleware_stack, :eager_load!, :add_internal_routes, :set_routes_reloader_hook, :enable_yjit).

Request order after the middleware stack: RouteSet#call -> make_request -> Journey::Router#serve -> recognize -> route.app.serve. For a dispatcher endpoint that is Dispatcher#serve -> controller(req) -> make_response! -> dispatch -> ActionController::Metal#dispatch -> set_request! -> set_response! -> AbstractController::Base#process -> Callbacks#process_action -> the action method.

Forgery checks are before-actions installed by protect_from_forgery: verify_authenticity_token and verify_request_for_forgery_protection, plus after-actions verify_same_origin_request and append_sec_fetch_site_to_vary_header. verified_request? allows GET, HEAD, a real QUERY (not a POST tunneled via _method=query), or a forgery strategy pass. load_defaults 8.2 sets the strategy to :header_only and the failure strategy to :exception.

Insert order: Model#save -> create_or_update -> _create_record -> attributes_for_create -> self.class.with_connection -> _returning_columns_for_insert(connection) -> _insert_record -> type-cast returned columns -> @new_record = false. Update order is _update_record -> attributes_for_update -> _update_row, and an empty attribute list skips the SQL and sets @_trigger_update_callback. delete skips callbacks; destroy runs them.

Connection acquisition order for that insert: establish_connection (usually from the railtie reading database.yml) -> connection_handler.establish_connection -> later with_connection -> ConnectionPool#lease_connection -> checkout on first use for the thread. ActiveRecord.disconnect_all! closes every pool via PoolConfig.disconnect_all!.

credentials:edit order: load_environment_config!, load_generators, maybe retarget content_path and key_path to config/credentials/<env>.yml.enc, ensure_encryption_key_has_been_added (EncryptionKeyFileGenerator#add_key_file), ensure_credentials_have_been_added (CredentialsGenerator#invoke_all), then credentials.change yields a tempfile to system_editor, which is system(*Shellwords.split(editor), path). InvalidMessage and MissingKeyError are rescued and printed.

Action Cable open order on the server connection object: handle_open calls connect (empty by default; apps override it to identify the current user), then subscribe_to_internal_channel, then send_welcome_message. Authorization::UnauthorizedError closes with disconnect reason unauthorized and reconnect: false. Incoming frames go handle_channel_command -> subscriptions.execute_command. Close is unsubscribe_from_all, unsubscribe_from_internal_channel, disconnect.

Job order: SomeJob.perform_later -> job_or_instantiate -> job.enqueue. QueueAdapter::ClassMethods#queue_adapter lazily assigns :async, and queue_adapter= Symbol/String calls ActiveJob::QueueAdapters.lookup(name).new then check_adapter if the adapter defines it. A custom object is accepted only when it responds to enqueue and enqueue_at.

testing_signals.summary: The framework tests itself with Minitest, one test/ tree per component, and a shared runner in tools/test.rb. Active Record and Active Job are matrixed by adapter at the Rake layer. Browser-level coverage uses Capybara and Selenium and is declared for the framework tests, not for a sample app. GitHub Actions in this repo does not run that matrix; release docs point at Buildkite. JavaScript for Action Cable is a separate QUnit suite.

claims.claim: The root Gemfile pins minitest ~> 6.0, minitest-mock, and, in the :test group, minitest-retry, plus stackprof and debug on MRI. capybara >= 3.39 and selenium-webdriver >= 4.20.0 are top-level dependencies used by system tests. brakeman and bundler-audit are test dependencies because generated apps include them.

tools/test.rb expects COMPONENT_ROOT, prepends that component's test directory, requires bundler/setup and rails/test_unit/runner, extends ActiveSupport::TestCase with Rails::LineFiltering, and calls Rails::TestUnit::Runner.parse_options then Runner.run. Each component's bin/test is the documented entry; the repo-root bin/test only chdirs into the first path segment and execs that component's bin/test.

Rails::TestUnit::Runner knows test folders models, helpers, channels, controllers, mailers, integration, jobs, and mailboxes, and parses --environment / -e itself before Minitest sees ARGV. AGENTS.md documents bin/test FILE, bin/test -i /name/, and bin/test FILE:line, and states the runner is parallel across processes.

Root rake test runs every framework in Releaser::FRAMEWORKS. rake activerecord:<adapter>:test and :integration cover mysql2, trilogy, postgresql, sqlite3, and sqlite3_mem. rake activejob:<adapter>:test and :integration cover async, inline, queue_classic (omitted on JRuby), resque, sneakers, backburner, and test.

Action Cable's package.json pretest/test scripts sit on @web/test-runner and qunit, with mock-socket. The package also has a lint script via eslint. actioncable/test/javascript holds the JS tests; Ruby tests live under actioncable/test/channel, connection, server, and subscription_adapter.
guides/ has its own Rakefile, rails_guides.rb, and guides/test. CONTRIBUTING.md points bug reporters at executable templates in guides/bug_report_templates rather than at the main suite.

rails-new-docker.yml, on push and pull_request, runs railties/exe/rails new dev/devrails --dev with BUNDLE_WITHOUT=db:job:cable:storage, builds that app's Dockerfile with podman, runs it with SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY=1 and DATABASE_URL=sqlite3:storage/production.sqlite3, then executes .github/workflows/scripts/test-container.rb.

rail_inspector.yml runs only when tools/rail_inspector changes, and its job is cd tools/rail_inspector && bundle exec rake. release.yml runs only on a published GitHub release and does not run the test suite before rake push.

AGENTS.md requires configuration tests to use Object#with (for example ActionView::Base.with or ActionController::Base.with) after requiring active_support/core_ext/object/with, instead of manual save/restore of class attributes.

There is no in-repo workflow that invokes rake test or the Active Record adapter matrix. A green GitHub Actions run on a normal pull request therefore does not mean the component suites passed; RELEASING_RAILS.md treats Buildkite as that signal.

Optional queue backends are require: false in the :job group (resque, resque-scheduler, queue_classic, sneakers, backburner). Adapter tests for those gems cannot run unless the group is installed, so a default bundle that excludes :job does not exercise them.

HealthController is documented as not reflecting database or Redis health, and its own tests, if any, cannot prove dependency checks that the action does not perform. The controller rescues Exception and only renders up or down.

risk_map.summary: The dangerous paths are the ones that eval, shell out, decrypt secrets, or accept network input before an app's own auth. CSRF and host authorization changed meaning across load_defaults versions, so an edit that looks local can change every newly generated app. Several public framework routes (health, storage, mailbox ingress) are safe only when the app understands their actual guarantees. The release webhook and the local .Gemfile hook are smaller but real trust boundaries.

claims.claim: RunnerCommand evals stdin or an arbitrary string in TOPLEVEL_BINDING after boot_application! and Rails.application.load_runner. That is an intentional RCE surface for anyone who can invoke bin/rails runner.

Credentials editing shells out with system(*Shellwords.split(ENV['VISUAL'] or ENV['EDITOR']), tempfile). Shellwords reduces word-splitting surprises, but the editor string is still an executable chosen by the environment, and a forking editor that does not wait will cause an immediate re-encrypt of an unedited file.

EncryptedFile follows ENV then key file, uses AES-128-GCM, and rejects keys whose length is not expected_key_length. Missing keys raise MissingKeyError naming both the key path and the env var. Invalid ciphertext surfaces as MessageEncryptor::InvalidMessage, which credentials diff and edit rescue and sometimes print the raw encrypted file.

If SECRET_KEY_BASE and credentials are both empty in a local environment, secret_key_base generates and stores a secret in tmp/local_secret.txt. SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY forces that path so assets:precompile can run without production secrets. A dummy secret shipped into a real environment would make cookie and message forgeries trivial.

HostAuthorization exists to stop DNS rebinding. It returns 403 via a default response_app when the host is not permitted, and logs the blocked host at error. ALLOWED_HOSTS_IN_DEVELOPMENT is .localhost, .test, 0.0.0.0/0, and ::/0. config.host_authorization exclude can opt a path out.

load_defaults 8.2 sets forgery_protection_verification_strategy to :header_only, default_protect_from_forgery_with to :exception, and removes X-XSS-Protection and X-Download-Options from the default security headers. Apps that stay on an older load_defaults keep the previous token-based behavior. protect_from_forgery without an explicit with: warns when the default is still :null_session.

sanitize_sql_for_conditions returns a String argument unchanged, so callers who pass an already-interpolated SQL fragment get no quoting. The safe form is the array or named-bind form. This is the classic injection footgun at the framework boundary.

Rails::HealthController#show returns 200 whenever rendering succeeds. The class comment states it does not check the database or Redis, and that pointing a load balancer at it can restart pods for the wrong reason if an app later adds those checks carelessly.

Action Mailbox mounts POSTs at /rails/action_mailbox/{postmark,relay,sendgrid,mandrill}/inbound_emails and /rails/action_mailbox/mailgun/inbound_emails/mime on the application routes, plus a conductor that can create and incinerate emails. Those ingress controllers are the authentication boundary for inbound mail; the route file itself does not show a shared secret check.

Active Storage exposes signed_id blob and representation URLs and a disk service PUT /disk/:encoded_token plus direct upload creation. Confidentiality of stored files depends on signed-id expiry and the service, not on a session.

Rakefile task publish_docs POSTs to http://api.rubyonrails.org:8080/rails-master-hook with Net::HTTP and no credentials in the request. The comment says a GitHub webhook is what normally triggers doc publishing, and that humans should not run the task.
The root Gemfile instance_evals ./.Gemfile when that file exists, so a local untracked file executes during every bundle install of the framework.

load_defaults is a single case ladder from 5.0 through 8.2 where each version calls the previous one. Changing an assignment inside when 8.2, or inserting a version in the wrong place, changes defaults for every app that generated config.load_defaults at that version. The generator writes that call into config/application.rb.

load_defaults 8.0 sets Regexp.timeout ||= 1 when the Ruby supports it, which can raise on previously legal long matches. 8.1 turns YJIT off when Rails.env.local? and on otherwise. Both are process-wide, not per-request.

Railtie initializers share one ordered list with the application. A before/after name that does not match, or a railtie loaded after initialize!, silently misses the boot. rails/all.rb's require order is the supported composition order, and Releaser::FRAMEWORKS comments that Action Mailbox must follow Active Record.

extension_points.summary: Rails is extended by subclassing Railtie or Engine, by dropping files that match command and generator globs, and by registering adapters. The frameworks that ship in this repo are themselves just those plugins. New queue adapters are explicitly not an accepted extension; password algorithms, storage services, database protocol names, and middleware are.

claims.claim: Rails::Railtie is the extension base. Subclasses are loaded when the gem is required if Rails::Railtie is defined. The initializer macro accepts before and after. Railties can also set config.app_generators, config.to_prepare, rake_tasks, generators, and a server block that runs when the Rails server starts.

Rails::Engine subclasses Railtie and is what makes a gem load app/ models, controllers, helpers, config/routes.rb, config/locales, and lib/tasks. Rails::Application is an engine. Isolated engines are how Action Cable, Active Storage, Action Mailbox, and Action Text are mounted.

Rails::Command.find_by_namespace searches load paths for rails/commands and commands, files named *_command.rb, and namespaces with an optional rails: prefix. Adding a command is a new file matching that glob plus a class inheriting Rails::Command::Base, not a hand-edited registry hash.

Rails::Generators uses the same pattern for *_generator.rb under rails/generators and generators, with fallbacks when the first lookup misses. invoke is the entry for generate, destroy, and update. after_generate callbacks see files recorded by add_generated_file.

ActiveJob::QueueAdapters.lookup(name) does const_get of the camelized name plus Adapter. A non-symbol adapter is accepted by queue_adapter= when it implements enqueue and enqueue_at. The same file says pull requests for new adapters are not accepted.

Active Job argument types are extended with serializer classes under activejob/lib/active_job/serializers (date, time, duration, range, symbol, BigDecimal, ActionController::Parameters, module, and GlobalID via the documented Identification interface).

A new Active Storage backend subclasses Service, implements upload, download, download_chunk, and compose, and is selected when Configurator#resolve require's active_storage/service/<underscore>_service and constantizes <Name>Service. MirrorService is the built-in example of build receiving the configurator so it can construct children.

ActiveRecord.protocol_adapters is an ActiveSupport::InheritableOptions hash used only to map DATABASE_URL protocols onto adapter names. The documented extension is ActiveRecord.protocol_adapters.mysql = "mysql2" or a custom protocol string pointing at an external adapter.

Password hashing is a registry: ActiveModel::SecurePassword.register_algorithm(name, algorithm_class). :bcrypt and :argon2 are registered at load. has_secure_password algorithm: :name calls lookup_algorithm and instantiates the class; an unknown symbol raises ArgumentError.

Middleware is inserted either in DefaultMiddlewareStack#build_stack or from a railtie initializer via app.middleware.use. Session stores are resolved through ActionDispatch::Session.resolve_store when config.session_store is a Symbol. :disabled skips session middleware.

Versioned behavior is the case statement in Application::Configuration#load_defaults. The in-file comment is the extension procedure: add an accessor preserving old behavior, branch on the flag, set the new default only in the next version arm, mirror it in new_framework_defaults, and update the configuring guide. Unknown versions raise.

Action Cable subscription adapters for Redis and PostgreSQL are listed in Zeitwerk::Loader.do_not_eager_load so they load only when configured. Connection#connect and #disconnect are the empty hooks an app overrides for authentication and presence.

Engines draw routes by reopening Rails.application.routes.draw, which is how Action Mailbox and Active Storage install their endpoints without the app editing config/routes.rb. Development-only framework routes are appended later by Finisher#add_internal_routes.

agent_handoff.summary: Edit one component at a time and treat Railties configuration and the generator templates as a second component whenever a default changes. The safe test loop is that component's bin/test, plus an adapter rake task if the change touches SQL or jobs. Read the load_defaults comment before adding a flag. Do not add Active Support core extensions or new Active Job adapters. Assume GitHub Actions will not prove the change is green.

claims.claim: Read first: AGENTS.md, README.md, the component README, rails.gemspec, railties/lib/rails/all.rb, and the load_defaults method in railties/lib/rails/application/configuration.rb. For a request bug, continue into default_middleware_stack.rb, route_set.rb, and the controller metal. For a persistence bug, continue into persistence.rb and connection_handling.rb.

Components are meant to stay independently usable. A change that requires another framework must be guarded the way bcrypt and argon2 are (require: false) or the way rails/all.rb rescues a missing railtie. Releaser::FRAMEWORKS order is the dependency order used by packaging.

Run tests from the component directory: bin/test path/to_test.rb, bin/test path:line, or bin/test -i /method_name/. From the repo root the equivalents are rake <framework>:test, rake test, and rake smoke. Active Record SQL changes need bundle exec rake test:sqlite3 at minimum and the other adapters when the SQL differs. Active Job adapter changes need the matching test:<adapter> task.

Toggle framework configuration in tests with Object#with after requiring active_support/core_ext/object/with. AGENTS.md forbids the manual save/restore pattern around class attributes such as ActionView::Base.remove_hidden_field_autocomplete.

Every Ruby file starts with # frozen_string_literal: true. Bugfixes and features need a CHANGELOG.md entry at the top of that component. Assertions should prefer assert_not and, in view tests, assert_dom_equal. Style is bundle exec rubocop against the repo .rubocop.yml.

A new config flag is not done until load_defaults sets it in the newest version arm (currently 8.2), the upgrade initializer template under railties generators repeats it commented out, and guides/source/configuring.md mentions it. The steps are written at the top of load_defaults. Editing an older when arm changes behavior for apps that have not upgraded their load_defaults target.

CONTRIBUTING.md says Active Support core-extension changes are generally rejected and should be proposed to Ruby instead, and that cosmetic-only patches are rejected. Active Job's queue_adapters.rb says new adapter pull requests are not accepted.

Security reports must not be opened as GitHub issues. .github/security.md and CONTRIBUTING.md both redirect to https://rubyonrails.org/security. Do not add exploit details to a public changelog while following that policy.

The test runner is parallel. Tests that leak global configuration, routes, or Active Record connections across examples will flake even when they pass alone. Prefer the with helper and the existing test helper in that component (abstract_unit.rb or test_helper.rb) over process-global mutation.

Generated-app behavior is owned by railties/lib/rails/generators, especially templates under rails/app/templates, not by the root Gemfile. The root Gemfile is the framework's own development bundle. Changing one without the other leaves rails new and the CI docker smoke (BUNDLE_WITHOUT=db:job:cable:storage) disagreeing.

JavaScript changes in Action Cable need the npm scripts in actioncable/package.json (build, lint, test) in addition to the Ruby tests under actioncable/test. The root package.json only declares workspaces; it has no test script.

Current development line is 8.2.0.alpha. Changelog entries, npm package versions, and gemspecs are expected to stay on that version until tools/releaser's update_versions task rewrites them. Do not hand-bump a single gemspec.
