readmePreview: This document serves as both a quick start guide to Redis and a detailed resource for building it from source.

overview.summary: This is the Redis Open Source server (`src/version.h` reports 8.9.241, branch `unstable`) — a single-process, event-loop-driven in-memory data structure server written in C99/gnu11, plus its CLI, benchmark, sentinel, and RDB/AOF checking tools. Beyond upstream Redis it carries a substantial in-tree feature layer: a new `OBJ_ARRAY` sparse-array type (`src/t_array.c`, `src/sparsearray.c`), key eviction protection (`src/bless.c`), CuckooHeavyKeeper hot-key tracking (`src/chk.c`, `src/hotkeys.c`), atomic cluster slot migration (`src/cluster_asm.c`), zstd replication/client compression (`src/client_comp.c`), and multi-threaded IO (`src/iothread.c`). It also ships a bespoke top-level Makefile + `scripts/` orchestration layer that clones, builds, deploys, and tests four external Redis modules (RediSearch, RedisJSON, RedisBloom, RedisTimeSeries) pinned by `modules/modules.yaml`, which upstream Redis does not have.

system_map.summary: The runtime is one `redis-server` binary whose `main()` in `src/server.c` initializes config, ACL, the module system and connection types, then hands control to the `ae` event loop (`aeMain`). The same binary multiplexes into sentinel, `redis-check-rdb` and `redis-check-aof` modes by argv[0] inspection. Storage is entirely in-process (`kvstore`/`dict`/`listpack`/`quicklist`/`rax`/`ebuckets`), persisted by RDB snapshot and/or AOF manifest, and replicated over a custom PSYNC protocol. Build is GNU Make: `src/Makefile` compiles the core and vendored `deps/`, while the top-level `Makefile` delegates to `scripts/*.sh` for the module-bundle workflow. Deployment shape is a bare binary + `redis.conf` (or the generated `redis-full.conf`), with an Ubuntu 24.04 build image in `docker/Dockerfile.noble`.

claims.claim: `main()` in src/server.c is the single entrypoint for redis-server, redis-sentinel, redis-check-rdb and redis-check-aof: it calls `checkForSentinelMode()` on argv, then dispatches to `redis_check_rdb_main()` / `redis_check_aof_main()` when `strstr(exec_name, "redis-check-rdb"/"redis-check-aof")` matches, before any config parsing.

Startup order in `main()` is fixed and dependency-driven: `initServerConfig()` → `ACLInit()` (commented 'must be initialized ASAP because the basic networking code and client creation depends on it') → `moduleInitModulesSystem()` → `connTypeInitialize()` → `keyMetaInit()`.

The event loop is created in `initServer()` via `aeCreateEventLoop(server.maxclients+CONFIG_FDSET_INCR)`, and per-DB storage is allocated as three parallel structures — `kvstoreCreate()` for `db->keys`, `db->expires`, plus `blessedKvstoreCreate()` for `db->blessed_keys` and `estoreCreate()` for `db->subexpires`.
`main()` ends with `aeMain(server.el)` after `redisSetCpuAffinity(server.server_cpulist)` and `setOOMScoreAdj(-1)`; everything after that point is event-loop driven.

The core links 130+ objects listed in `REDIS_SERVER_OBJ` in src/Makefile, including the non-upstream modules `bless.o t_array.o sparsearray.o chk.o hotkeys.o gcra.o vector.o fwtree.o estore.o client_comp.o cluster_asm.o iothread.o keymeta.o`.

Vendored third-party code lives in `deps/` and is built as separate targets: `DEPENDENCY_TARGETS=hiredis linenoise lua hdr_histogram fpconv xxhash tre` — note `tre` (regex) is a dependency of the new array type, which includes `../deps/tre/local_includes/tre.h`.

The top-level Makefile is not upstream's: it includes `modules/manifest.mk`, defines a `GOALS_WITH_ARGS` positional-argument capture mechanism, and routes `build`/`clean`/`test`/`deploy`/`bootstrap`/`run`/`tarball` to `scripts/*.sh` rather than recursing into `src/`.

`modules/modules.yaml` is the single source of truth pinning four external modules to immutable refs: redisbloom v8.11.81, redisearch v8.10.1 (with `build_env: LTO=1 REDISEARCH_GENERATE_HEADERS=0 INLINE_LSE_ATOMICS=0`), redisjson v8.10.0, redistimeseries v8.10.0.

Test entrypoints are four shell wrappers that locate tclsh 8.5–9.0 and invoke `tests/test_helper.tcl`: `./runtest`, `./runtest-moduleapi` (which first runs `$MAKE -C tests/modules` then names 48 `--single unit/moduleapi/*` suites), `./runtest-cluster`, `./runtest-sentinel`.

`make -C src test` depends on building redis-server, redis-check-aof, redis-cli, redis-benchmark and `module_tests` before shelling out to `(cd ..; ./runtest)`; `test-modules`, `test-sentinel`, `test-cluster` are separate targets.

External integrations are network protocols rather than SDKs: the cluster bus (`src/cluster_legacy.c`), the PSYNC replication protocol (`src/replication.c`), TLS via OpenSSL gated on `BUILD_TLS=yes|module` (`src/tls.c`), and optional zstd compression gated on `-DUSE_COMPRESSION=1` detected via pkg-config.

The deployment artifact set is defined by `scripts/deploy.sh` / `scripts/uninstall.sh`: core binaries and symlinks into `$(PREFIX)/bin` (default `/usr/local`) and module `.so` files into `$(PREFIX)/lib/redis/modules`, with `loadmodule` paths rewritten into a generated `redis-full.conf`.

`docker/Dockerfile.noble` is the only container definition — an Ubuntu 24.04 multi-arch build environment (amd64+arm64) that installs Redis prereqs and then runs `modules/docker-install-bundled-module-deps.sh` to execute each bundled module's `.install/install_script.sh`. It is a build image, not a runtime image.
Memory allocator selection is a build-time runtime boundary: `MALLOC` defaults to `jemalloc` on Linux and `libc` elsewhere, and is forcibly downgraded to `libc` whenever `SANITIZER` is set.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface is the RESP command set — 464 JSON command specs under `src/commands/` compiled into the 13k-line `src/commands.def`. Alongside the classic types (string/list/set/zset/hash/stream/HLL/geo/bitmap) this tree adds a first-class array type (AR* commands), key-blessing (BLESS), hot-key tracking (HOTKEYS), INCREX, hash-field expiration (HEXPIRE family), and a compiled-out GCRA rate limiter. Administrative surface spans ACL, CLIENT, CLUSTER (including atomic slot migration), CONFIG, FUNCTION, DEBUG, and the Sentinel command set. Client-side tooling ships as `redis-cli` (with a full cluster manager and ~60 flags), `redis-benchmark`, and the two check tools.

claims.claim: 464 command specification JSON files under `src/commands/` are the declarative source of the command table; `utils/generate-command-code.py` compiles them into `src/commands.def` (13,236 lines) via the `$(COMMANDS_DEF_FILENAME).def` Make rule.

A new `OBJ_ARRAY` (type 7) sparse-array data type is exposed via 18 commands — ARSET, ARGET, ARDEL, ARDELRANGE, ARGETRANGE, ARGREP, ARINFO, ARINSERT, ARLASTITEMS, ARLEN, ARMGET, ARMSET, ARNEXT, AROP, ARRING, ARSCAN, ARSEEK, ARCOUNT — implemented in `src/t_array.c` over `src/sparsearray.c`.

BLESS marks keys as never-evictable: the NO-EVICT bit lives in the kvBits byte after each kvobj, persists through RDB and AOF, and is exposed as BLESS SET/GET/CLEAR/SCAN plus an `blessed_keys` INFO counter backed by a per-DB `db->blessed_keys` index.

HOTKEYS START/STOP/GET/RESET/HELP expose a CuckooHeavyKeeper top-K sketch (`src/chk.c`, based on the Ngo & Papatriantafilou paper plus a min-heap borrowed from RedisBloom's TopK) that can be scoped to specific cluster slot ranges via a `slotRangeArray`.
INCREX is a new string command returning a two-element reply (`{value, applied}`) that creates a missing key at 0 before incrementing, with an optional increment argument.

Hash-field expiration ships as eight commands — HEXPIRE, HEXPIREAT, HPEXPIRE, HPEXPIREAT, HEXPIRETIME, HPEXPIRETIME, HGETEX, HGETDEL — backed by the `ebuckets` radix-of-buckets expiry structure and the per-DB `estore` subexpires store.

A GCRA (Generic Cell Rate Algorithm) leaky-bucket rate limiter exists as `src/gcra.c` with an `OBJ_GCRA` object type and a 4-arg `GCRA key max_burst tokens_per_period period` command, ported from redis-cell — but it is compiled out by default behind `#ifdef ENABLE_GCRA`.

Atomic slot migration is a user-facing cluster feature driven by `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT <slots>` run on the destination node, handled by `clusterMigrationCommand()`, with an eight-step protocol documented in the file header.

Lua scripting is offered in two forms: ephemeral EVAL/EVALSHA/SCRIPT via `evalGenericCommand()` and `luaCreateFunction()` in `src/eval.c`, and persistent FUNCTION libraries via a pluggable engine registry in `src/functions.c` whose only registered engine is `LUA_ENGINE_NAME` from `src/function_lua.c`.

`redis-cli` is a large multi-mode tool (11,561 lines) exposing analysis modes `--bigkeys --memkeys --hotkeys --keystats-samples --scan --latency --latency-dist --latency-history --intrinsic-latency --lru-test --rdb --functions-rdb --pipe --replica --eval --ldb`, RESP3/JSON output modes, and TLS flags (`--tls --cert --key --cacert --cacertdir --insecure`).

`redis-cli --cluster` embeds a full cluster manager dispatch table of `clusterManagerCommandProc` functions — create, add-node, del-node, info, check, fix, reshard, rebalance — with ~25 `--cluster-*` option flags.

Sentinel is a distinct operating mode of the same binary: `initSentinelConfig()` + `initSentinel()` run before config parsing so the config file populates monitored-master state, and `sentinelIsRunning()` replaces the normal ready-to-serve path in `main()`.

Multi-threaded IO is a runtime feature with its own event loops per thread: `initThreadedIO()` is called from `InitServerLast()`, and `readQueryFromClient()` branches on `server.io_threads_num > 1` and atomically tracks `c->pending_read` and per-thread `IOThreads[c->running_tid].io_reads_processed`.

Client/replication payload compression is a user-visible option: `clientCompressionProcessPendingData()` runs in `beforeSleep()`, clients carry a `compression_state` and `CLIENT_IO_COMPRESSION_ENABLED` io_flag, and `setReplCompression(server.repl_compression)` is forced off at init when the build lacks zstd.

`modules/vector-sets/` is an in-tree module (deliberately absent from modules.yaml) implementing HNSW vector search with its own `commands.json`, `hnsw.c`, an expression filter language in `expr.c`, and a word2vec helper `w2v.c`.

data_flow.summary: Input arrives on a connection abstraction (`connection.h` over socket/unix/TLS), is read into a per-client or thread-reusable query buffer by `readQueryFromClient()`, parsed into `pendingCommand` structs by `processInlineBuffer()`/`processMultibulkBuffer()`, dispatched by `processCommand()` and executed by `call()`. Command handlers mutate the authoritative state owner — `server.db[j]` kvstores — and any side effects are queued through `alsoPropagate()`. At the end of the execution unit `propagateNow()` fans out to exactly three sinks: the AOF buffer, the replica stream, and the atomic-slot-migration client. Replies accumulate in per-client output buffers and are flushed in `beforeSleep()` by `handleClientsWithPendingWrites()`, strictly after `flushAppendOnlyFile()` so `appendfsync=always` is honoured before acknowledgement.

claims.claim: The input boundary is `readQueryFromClient(connection *conn)`, which recovers the client via `connGetPrivateData(conn)` and reads `PROTO_IOBUF_LEN` bytes, except when a multibulk argument exceeds `PROTO_MBULK_BIG_ARG`, in which case it sizes the read to exactly the remaining bulk length to enable zero-copy object creation.

Query buffers are pooled per IO thread: a client with no private `querybuf` borrows `thread_reusable_qb` and sets `CLIENT_IO_REUSABLE_QUERYBUFFER`; if `thread_reusable_qb_used` is already set (nested execution via `processEventsWhileBlocked()`) the client allocates a private buffer instead.

`processInputBuffer()` parses ahead up to `server.lookahead` commands into `c->pending_cmds`, but clamps the lookahead to 1 for unauthenticated clients because AUTH changes the handling of succeeding commands.

Request type is inferred from the first byte: `'*'` selects `PROTO_REQ_MULTIBULK` → `processMultibulkBuffer()`, anything else selects `PROTO_REQ_INLINE` → `processInlineBuffer()`; an unknown `reqtype` triggers `serverPanic("Unknown request type")`.

`processCommand()` resolves argv to a `struct redisCommand` through a three-tier lookup: an already-set `c->lookedcmd`, then `isCommandReusable(c->lastcmd, ...)` reusing the previous command, then a full `lookupCommand(c->argv, c->argc)`.

The command table itself is populated once at startup by `populateCommandTable()` walking the generated `extern struct redisCommand redisCommandTable[]` from commands.def, so adding a command is a data change in `src/commands/*.json` followed by codegen.

Module command filters get first look at every non-reprocessed command: `processCommand()` calls `moduleCallCommandFilters(c)` and `reqresAppendRequest(c)` before command lookup, meaning a module can rewrite argv before the core ever resolves the command name.

`call()` records `dirty = server.dirty` and `old_master_repl_offset = server.master_repl_offset` before invoking the proc, and clears `CLIENT_FORCE_AOF|CLIENT_FORCE_REPL|CLIENT_PREVENT_PROP` so the handler must opt back into propagation.

`server.allowed_propagate_targets` is a global mask narrowed for the duration of each `call()` so that nested `RM_Call`/Lua `redis.set_repl()` restrictions from an outer call cannot be escaped by an inner one — this is what makes effect-command rewriting (SPOP→SREM) honour selective replication.

`propagateNow()` is the single fan-out point to the three output sinks: `feedAppendOnlyFile()` when `server.aof_state != AOF_OFF && target & PROPAGATE_AOF`, then `replicationFeedSlaves(server.slaves, ...)` and `asmFeedMigrationClient(argv, argc)` when `target & PROPAGATE_REPL`.

`propagateNow()` asserts that propagation never happens while replica actions are paused — `serverAssert(!(isPausedActions(PAUSE_ACTION_REPLICA) && !server.client_pause_in_transaction))` — because a dataset change during a replica pause could be lost on failover.

Output ordering in `beforeSleep()` is load-bearing and commented as such: `connTypeProcessPendingData()` and `clientCompressionProcessPendingData()` must run before `flushAppendOnlyFile(0)`, which must run before `handleClientsWithPendingWrites()` and `sendPendingClientsToIOThreads()` so `appendfsync=always` is satisfied before the reply is sent.

Blocked-client resumption is sequenced before AOF flushing: `blockedBeforeSleep()` is called with the comment 'must be done before flushAppendOnlyFile, in case of appendfsync=always, since the unblocked clients may write data'.

Client-side caching invalidation is a distinct output boundary flushed per-iteration: `beforeSleep()` asserts `server.tracking_pending_keys` and `server.pending_push_messages` are empty, then calls `trackingBroadcastInvalidationMessages(NULL)` for BCAST-mode clients.

On startup the persistence-to-memory direction is owned by `loadDataFromDisk()`, which honours a `preload-file` config prefixed `aof:/` or `rdb:/` (dispatching to `loadPreLoadAOFFile`/`loadPreLoadManifestFile`/`rdbLoad`), else falls back to `loadAppendOnlyFiles(server.aof_manifest)` when AOF is on, else `rdbLoad(server.rdb_filename, ...)`.

behavior_traces.summary: Three flows dominate. Startup: `main()` → config → subsystem init → `initServer()` → `InitServerLast()` → `loadDataFromDisk()` → AOF reconciliation → `aeMain()`. Command execution: socket readable → `readQueryFromClient()` → `processInputBuffer()` → `processCommandAndResetClient()` → `processCommand()` → `call()` → handler → `alsoPropagate()` → `propagatePendingCommands()` → `propagateNow()`. Replica bootstrap: `replicaofCommand()` → `replicationSetMaster()` → `connectWithMaster()` → `syncWithMaster()` handshake → `slaveTryPartialResynchronization()` → full sync via `readSyncBulkPayload()`, with the master side running `syncCommand()` → `startBgsaveForReplication()` → `rdbSaveToSlavesSockets()`.

claims.claim: STARTUP step 1 — `main()` seeds entropy from `time(NULL)^getpid()^tv.tv_usec` into `srand`/`srandom`/`init_genrand64`, calls `crc64_init()`, captures `umask(server.umask = umask(0777))` early to avoid a thread race, and seeds the dict hash with 16 bytes from `getRandomBytes()` — this is what makes hash-flooding attacks impractical.

STARTUP step 2 — argv parsing in `main()` conceptually appends every `--opt value` pair onto the config file text as newline-separated directives, with documented precedence 'File, stdin, explicit options -- last config is the one that matters', plus special-cases for bare `--save` and `--sentinel`.

STARTUP step 3 — `initServer()` installs `SIG_IGN` for SIGHUP/SIGPIPE, runs `setupSignalHandlers()`, `ThreadsManager_init()`, `makeThreadKillable()`, then `hashTemplatesInit()`, `createSharedObjects()`, `adjustOpenFilesLimit()` and `monotonicInit(monotonicLogCallback)` before creating the event loop.

STARTUP step 4 — `initServer()` decides memory accounting once and irreversibly: `server.memory_tracking_enabled = server.key_memory_histograms || clusterSlotStatsEnabled(CLUSTER_SLOT_STATS_MEM)`, documented as disable-able at runtime but never re-enable-able to avoid a full slot re-scan.

STARTUP step 5 — `InitServerLast()` starts the background subsystems last: `bioInit()`, `initThreadedIO()`, `set_jemalloc_bg_thread()`, and records `server.initial_memory_usage = zmalloc_used_memory()` as the baseline for memory reporting.

STARTUP step 6 — the load sequence in `main()` is `aofLoadManifestFromDisk()` → `loadDataFromDisk()` → `aofSetupAfterPreloadFile()` → `aofOpenIfNeededOnServerStart()` → `aofDelHistoryFiles()` → `applyAppendOnlyConfig()`, the last of which exists specifically to apply an `appendonly` config change that arrived while loading.

STARTUP step 7 — in cluster mode `main()` hard-asserts `verifyClusterConfigWithData() == C_OK` after load, then logs 'Ready to accept connections' per non-NULL `server.listeners[j]`, notifies systemd with `READY=1` when `supervised_mode == SUPERVISED_SYSTEMD`, and finally calls `warnAboutInsecureConfig()`.

COMMAND step 1 — `processCommand()` first postpones the client via `blockPostponeClient(c)` if a module is in a blocked yield that excludes `BUSY_MODULE_YIELD_CLIENTS`, then runs `commandCheckExistence()` and `commandCheckArity()`, rejecting via `rejectCommandSds()`.

COMMAND step 2 — commands literally named `host:` or `post` are intercepted before any other handling and routed to `securityWarningCommand(c)` returning `C_ERR`, a cross-protocol-scripting (HTTP-to-Redis) defence.

COMMAND step 3 — commands carrying `CMD_INTERNAL` are made to look nonexistent (`cmd = NULL`) unless the client has `CLIENT_INTERNAL` or `mustObeyClient(c)` is true, so masters and AOF replay are implicitly trusted while ordinary clients cannot even discover them.

COMMAND step 4 — `CMD_PROTECTED` commands are gated by `allowProtectedAction(server.enable_debug_cmd, c)` for `debugCommand` and `server.enable_module_cmd` for `moduleCommand`, with an error naming `enable-debug-command`/`enable-module-command`.

COMMAND step 5 — `call()` sets `CLIENT_EXECUTING_COMMAND` to suppress mid-reply client-side-caching pushes, calls `enterExecutionUnit(1, call_timer)`, and skips slowlog/stat updates entirely when `isAOFLoadingContext()` is true.

COMMAND step 6 — `call()` avoids a `gettimeofday` per command when a hardware monotonic clock is available: it only calls `updateCachedTime(0)` after 10µs of monotonic drift or 25 accumulated calls (`server.accum_call_count_since_ustime > 25`).

REPLICATION (replica side) — `replicaofCommand()` → `replicationSetMaster(ip, port)` → `connectWithMaster()` installs `syncWithMaster()` as the connection handler, which performs the PING/AUTH/REPLCONF handshake then calls `slaveTryPartialResynchronization(conn, read_reply)`; on `+FULLRESYNC` the handler becomes `readSyncBulkPayload()`.

REPLICATION (master side) — `syncCommand()` handles PSYNC/SYNC and, when no partial resync is possible, calls `startBgsaveForReplication(mincapa, req)` which selects between `rdbSaveBackground()` (disk-backed) and `rdbSaveToSlavesSockets()` (diskless) based on `repl-diskless-sync`.

ATOMIC SLOT MIGRATION — the documented eight-step flow is: destination runs `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT`, source forks and ships a slot snapshot as RESTORE commands over an RDB channel, streams incremental writes over a main channel, pauses writes at catch-up, destination drains and takes ownership, config propagates over the cluster bus, then the source trims migrated keys via `asmTriggerBackgroundTrim()` on a BIO thread.

NESTED EVENT LOOP — when `ProcessingEventsWhileBlocked` is set, `beforeSleep()` takes a short-circuit path running only `connTypeProcessPendingData`, `clientCompressionProcessPendingData`, `flushAppendOnlyFile(0)`, `handleClientsWithPendingWrites`, `freeClientsInAsyncFreeQueue`, `processClientsOfAllIOThreads` and `sendPendingClientsToIOThreads`, counting them into `server.events_processed_while_blocked` and returning early.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is a Tcl integration suite: `tests/test_helper.tcl` globs `tests/{unit,unit/type,unit/moduleapi,unit/cluster,integration}/*.tcl` into `::all_tests` and runs them against real spawned `redis-server` processes on ports from 21111. There are no C-level unit test files, but the binary embeds a `REDIS_TEST` mode invoked as `redis-server test <name>|all` for data-structure self-tests. Module API coverage is unusually deep — 48 C test modules under `tests/modules/` paired with 48 `unit/moduleapi/*.tcl` suites. CI runs eight build matrices plus an ASAN build and a commands.def drift check, with lcov/Codecov, CodeQL, Coverity, and a reply-schema linter on separate workflows.

claims.claim: Test discovery is directory-glob based, not a manifest: `test_helper.tcl` iterates `set test_dirs {unit unit/type unit/moduleapi unit/cluster integration}` and lsorts `*.tcl` into `::all_tests`, so a new `.tcl` file in those dirs is picked up automatically.

The harness is a client/server fan-out: `test_server_main`, `accept_test_clients`, `read_from_test_client` and `signal_idle_client` distribute test files across parallel Tcl clients, with `run_solo` for tests that must not run concurrently.

Support libraries sourced by every suite live in `tests/support/`: `server.tcl` (start_server), `util.tcl`, `cluster_util.tcl`, `aofmanifest.tcl`, `redis.tcl` (the Tcl RESP client), `response_transformers.tcl` (RESP2/RESP3 normalisation), and `cli.tcl`.

Module API is the most thoroughly covered subsystem: `runtest-moduleapi` enumerates 48 suites explicitly by `--single`, and `tests/modules/` holds 48 matching C test modules built by `$MAKE -C tests/modules` before the run.

The C code carries an embedded self-test harness rather than a separate unit-test binary: `main()` under `#ifdef REDIS_TEST` accepts `redis-server test <name>|all` with flags `--accurate --large-memory --valgrind --verbose`, iterates a `redisTests[]` table, and prints a pass/fail summary.

Cluster coverage includes 23 dedicated suites under `tests/unit/cluster/`, notably `atomic-slot-migration.tcl`, `internal-secret.tcl`, `packet-validation.tcl`, `tls-peer-impersonation.tcl` and `cluster-bus-port-protected-mode.tcl` — the security-sensitive cluster paths are explicitly exercised.

Integration coverage focuses on durability and replication edge cases: `aof-multi-part.tcl`, `aof-race.tcl`, `corrupt-dump-fuzzer.tcl`, `corrupt-dump.tcl`, `psync2*.tcl` (four files), `replication-rdbchannel.tcl`, `replication-iothreads.tcl`, `failover.tcl`, `shutdown.tcl`.
The primary CI job `test-ubuntu-latest` builds with `make REDIS_CFLAGS='-Werror' BUILD_TLS=yes` and runs `./runtest --verbose --tags -slow --dump-logs` — meaning slow-tagged tests do not gate PRs.

CI enforces codegen freshness: the `validate commands.def up to date` step touches `src/commands/ping.json`, runs `make commands.def`, and fails if `git diff` is non-empty — a hand-edited commands.def will break the build.

A dedicated `test-sanitizer-address` job builds `SANITIZER=address REDIS_CFLAGS='-Werror -DDEBUG_ASSERTIONS -DREDIS_TEST' BUILD_TLS=module` and reruns the suite, so debug assertions and the embedded C tests are compiled in on that path only.

The build matrix covers portability rather than behaviour: `build-debian-old` (debian:buster container), `build-macos-latest`, `build-32bit` (via gcc-multilib), `build-libc-malloc`, `build-centos-jemalloc` (centos:stream9) and `build-old-chain-jemalloc` — all compile-only, no test step.

Coverage is reported but non-gating: `codecov.yml` sets both `patch` and `project` statuses to `informational: true`, and the workflow runs `make lcov` and uploads `./src/redis.info`, gated on `github.repository == 'redis/redis'` so forks skip it.

Static analysis runs on separate cadences: CodeQL on every PR plus a weekly `cron: '0 0 * * 0'`, and Coverity daily (`cron: '0 0 * * *'`) with a comment noting the sub-500k-LOC quota of 21 builds/week.

Command JSON specs have their own path-filtered lint gate: `reply-schemas-linter.yml` triggers only on changes to `src/commands/*.json` and runs `node ./utils/reply_schema_linter.js` after `npm install ajv`.
Heavy/long-running coverage is deferred to `daily.yml`, which runs nightly and on PRs targeting release branches matching `'[0-9].[0-9]'` — so a PR into `unstable` never exercises it.

The GCRA rate-limiter test file is entirely inert: `tests/unit/gcra.tcl` wraps its body in `if 0 { ... }`, matching the fact that `src/gcra.c` is compiled out unless `-DENABLE_GCRA` is passed — so that feature has zero effective coverage.

risk_map.summary: The dominant risk class is memory-safety in hand-written C parsing code reachable pre-authentication: the RESP parser, the cluster bus packet decoder, and the RDB/DUMP loader all consume untrusted bytes. Authentication is layered and easy to misconfigure — protected-mode, ACL, an auto-generated cluster internal secret, and module-supplied auth callbacks. A second class is coupling risk: the propagation invariants in `call()`/`propagateNow()`, the ordering contract inside `beforeSleep()`, and the object-type registration checklist all fail silently or assert if a contributor misses a step. Finally, there is genuinely dead code — GCRA is compiled out and its test file is `if 0`'d — and a large `DEBUG` surface with 50+ subcommands guarded only by a config flag.

claims.claim: The RESP parser is the pre-auth attack surface: `processMultibulkBuffer()` and `processInlineBuffer()` parse attacker-controlled bytes into `pendingCommand` structs before any AUTH check, and `readQueryFromClient()` performs manual pointer arithmetic (`(size_t)(c->bulklen+2)-(sdslen(c->querybuf)-c->qb_pos)`) to size big-argument reads.

The cluster internal secret is auto-generated with `getRandomHexChars(server.cluster->internal_secret, CLUSTER_INTERNALSECRETLEN)` and converged across nodes by a lexicographic `memcmp(...) > 0` rule in the PING extension handler — meaning any node that can join the bus can influence the shared secret used to authenticate internal connections.

Internal-secret password comparison correctly uses `time_independent_strcmp()`, but it is one of several parallel auth paths (`checkPasswordBasedAuth`, `ACLAuthenticateUser`, module auth callbacks) that must all stay consistent — a change to one does not automatically cover the others.

`moduleLoad()` calls `dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL)` on an operator-supplied path, giving any successfully loaded module full in-process code execution; the only guard is that `MODULE` carries `CMD_PROTECTED` and is gated by `server.enable_module_cmd`.
`warnAboutInsecureConfig()` only logs — it never refuses to start. A server with `DefaultUser` NOPASS, `protected-mode no` and a `0.0.0.0`/`::` bind emits a WARNING and then serves traffic.

`redis-server --test-memory <mb>` and `--check-system` run arbitrary memory-stressing code (`memtest()`, `syscheck()`) directly from `main()` before any config or privilege handling, and `--test-memory` with a non-numeric argument silently becomes `atoi(...) == 0`.

`src/debug.c` dispatches roughly 52 `DEBUG` subcommands via a chain of `strcasecmp(c->argv[1]->ptr, ...)` comparisons; the entire surface is protected only by the `enable-debug-command` config and `allowProtectedAction()`, and several subcommands (JMAP, SEGFAULT, SET-ACTIVE-EXPIRE, QUICKLIST-PACKED-THRESHOLD) can corrupt or crash a live server.

Adding a new object type is a documented multi-file checklist with no compiler enforcement — the `server.h` comment requires coordinated edits to `rdb.c` (save/load, possibly RDB_VERSION), `aof.c` (rewrite), `db.c` (`obj_type_name`, `copyCommand`), `debug.c` (`xorObjectDigest`, `serverLogObjectDebugInfo`) and `defrag.c` (`defragKey`). Missing one produces silent data or defrag corruption, not a build error.

GCRA is dead code in the shipped build: `src/gcra.c` is entirely inside `#ifdef ENABLE_GCRA`, `OBJ_GCRA`/`OBJ_TYPE_MAX 9` are conditional in `server.h`, the guard appears in `rdb.h`, `redismodule.h` and `acl.c`, and `tests/unit/gcra.tcl` disables its whole body with `if 0 {`. Building with `-DENABLE_GCRA` would activate untested code and change `OBJ_TYPE_MAX`, which is an RDB-visible constant.

`beforeSleep()` encodes at least four ordering invariants in comments rather than in code structure (TLS pending data before AOF flush; `clusterBeforeSleep()` before `blockedBeforeSleep()`; `blockedBeforeSleep()` before `flushAppendOnlyFile`; AOF flush before `handleClientsWithPendingWrites`). Reordering any of them breaks `appendfsync=always` durability guarantees without failing a test deterministically.

`propagateNow()` contains two assertions that convert logic errors into crashes rather than data loss: `debugServerAssert(duration != PROP_DURATION_UNKNOWN)` and the replica-pause assert. Both are reachable from any new command that queues propagation incorrectly.

The query-buffer pooling scheme (`thread_reusable_qb` / `thread_reusable_qb_used` / `CLIENT_IO_REUSABLE_QUERYBUFFER`) is shared mutable state whose correctness depends on nested-execution detection; the code comment notes the private-buffer fallback exists only for `processEventsWhileBlocked()` re-entry.

`src/module.c` is 16,117 lines — the single largest blast-radius file. It owns command registration, `RM_Call`, command filters, keyspace hooks, data-type serialization and `dlopen`, so nearly every subsystem change can break the stable module ABI in `src/redismodule.h`.

Atomic slot migration carries its own trim-correctness risk: `ASM_DEBUG_TRIM_DEFAULT` auto-selects between background BIO-thread deletion and main-thread active deletion 'based on module subscriptions and client tracking', so keyspace notifications fire in one mode and not the other.

`make` recipes shell out to scripts that perform network operations without review gates: `scripts/modules-update.sh` and `modules/common.mk` clone from GitHub URLs in `modules.yaml`, and `common.mk` resolves ref kind by probing the remote with `git ls-remote` at recipe time — so a `branch:` pin silently follows a moving target.

CI does not run the slow test tag on PRs (`./runtest --verbose --tags -slow`), and the heavy `daily.yml` matrix only triggers on PRs to release branches matching `'[0-9].[0-9]'` — so changes merged to `unstable` get comparatively thin pre-merge validation.

Sentinel mode initializes before config parsing and before the RDB/AOF check dispatch, and `sentinel.c` is 5,000+ lines sharing `server.c` globals with the normal server path — a startup-order change in `main()` can break sentinel in ways the default `./runtest` (which excludes sentinel) will not catch.

extension_points.summary: Redis has four first-class extension mechanisms. New commands are added declaratively: drop a JSON spec in `src/commands/`, implement the proc, and regenerate `src/commands.def`. New configuration parameters are appended to the `static_configs[]` table in `src/config.c` using the `create*Config` macro family. New runtime behaviour is added out-of-process via the module API (`RM_CreateCommand`/`RM_CreateSubcommand` plus data types, filters, and hooks). New scripting languages plug into `functionsRegisterEngine()`. On top of these, this tree adds a fifth: `modules/modules.yaml` as a declarative registry for bundled external modules.

claims.claim: Command registration is codegen-driven: `src/commands/*.json` is the input, `utils/generate-command-code.py` is the generator, and `src/Makefile`'s rule `$(COMMANDS_DEF_FILENAME).def: commands/*.json ../utils/generate-command-code.py` regenerates `src/commands.def`. CI fails if the checked-in file drifts.

The generator maps declarative JSON to C enums via `ARG_TYPES` (string/integer/double/key/pattern/unix-time/pure-token/oneof/block) and `GROUPS`, which already contains the newer `COMMAND_GROUP_ARRAY` and `COMMAND_GROUP_RATE_LIMIT` — adding a command group means editing this table.

The runtime command registry is `redisCommandTable[]` from commands.def, loaded once by `populateCommandTable()` into dicts consulted by `lookupCommandLogic()`, `lookupCommandBySds()` and `lookupCommandByCString()` — module commands are inserted into the same dicts.

Configuration is a single append-only table: `standardConfig static_configs[]` in src/config.c, populated by 119 `createBoolConfig`/`createStringConfig`/`createEnumConfig`/`createSDSConfig`/etc. calls, each taking a flags mask (`MODIFIABLE_CONFIG`, `IMMUTABLE_CONFIG`, `DEBUG_CONFIG`, `HIDDEN_CONFIG`, `SENSITIVE_CONFIG`) plus optional validate and apply callbacks.

Config apply-callbacks are the hook for cross-subsystem side effects — e.g. `updateClusterFlags` on `cluster-replica-no-failover`, `updateJemallocBgThread` on `jemalloc-bg-thread`, `updateAppendonly` on `appendonly`, `updateRequirePass` on `requirepass`, and `applyClusterBusPortProtectedMode`.

The module command API is `RM_CreateCommand(ctx, name, cmdfunc, strflags, firstkey, lastkey, keystep)` with `RM_CreateSubcommand(parent, ...)` for containers — the canonical way third-party code adds commands without touching the core tables.

Modules can intercept every command before dispatch by registering a command filter, invoked as `moduleCallCommandFilters(c)` at the top of `processCommand()`; `src/module.c` documents a flag to prevent a module's own `RM_Call()` from re-entering its filter.

Server lifecycle hooks are exposed as module server events — `beforeSleep()` fires `moduleFireServerEvent(REDISMODULE_EVENT_EVENTLOOP, REDISMODULE_SUBEVENT_EVENTLOOP_BEFORE_SLEEP, NULL)` once per loop iteration when `moduleCount()` is non-zero.

Scripting languages are pluggable through `functionsRegisterEngine(const char *engine_name, engine *engine)`, which stores into a module-level `static dict *engines`; `FUNCTION STATS` reflects the registry back to clients, and the only current registration is `LUA_ENGINE_NAME` from `luaEngineInitEngine` in function_lua.c.

Keyspace notification is a central hook point via `notifyKeyspaceEvent(type, event, key, dbid)` and the newer `notifyKeyspaceEventWithSubkeys(...)` — new data types must call these to participate in keyspace events and client-side-cache invalidation.

Connection types are a runtime-registered abstraction: `connTypeInitialize()` in `main()` sets up `server.listeners[j]` for `j < CONN_TYPE_MAX`, with implementations in `src/socket.c`, `src/unix.c` and `src/tls.c` behind `src/connection.h` — TLS can even be built as a loadable module with `BUILD_TLS=module`.

Bundled external modules are added declaratively by appending an entry to `modules/modules.yaml` with `name`/`repo`/`ref`/`target_module`/`loadmodule` and optional `build_env` — no new Makefile is needed, because `modules/common.mk` derives `MODULE_NAME` from `$(notdir $(CURDIR))` and reads the rest from the manifest.

All YAML parsing has exactly one implementation: `scripts/lib/manifest.sh`, which is dual-mode — sourced as a shell library (`manifest_modules`, `manifest_field`, `manifest_ref`, `resolve_modules`) and invoked as a CLI by `modules/manifest.mk`. Extending the manifest format means editing that one file.

New top-level Make goals that take positional module names plug into the `GOALS_WITH_ARGS := <goal>:<VAR>` list in the root Makefile; the dispatch and no-op `.PHONY` targets are generated automatically by the `_capture_goal_args` define.

New Tcl test suites require no registration — dropping a `.tcl` file into `tests/unit/`, `tests/unit/type/`, `tests/unit/cluster/` or `tests/integration/` is enough, since `test_helper.tcl` globs those directories. The exception is `tests/unit/moduleapi/`, where `runtest-moduleapi` lists each suite explicitly with `--single`.

The embedded C test harness is extended through the `redisTests[]` table consumed by `getTestProcByName()` in `main()`, letting a data-structure file register a `redisTestProc` runnable as `redis-server test <name>`.

agent_handoff.summary: Read `src/server.h` (the 4,976-line master header that every `.c` file includes) and `src/server.c` before touching anything — nearly all global state hangs off the `server` struct declared there. Never hand-edit `src/commands.def`; edit the JSON spec and regenerate. Prefer adding config via the `static_configs[]` table and features via the module API over touching the dispatch path. Build with `make REDIS_CFLAGS='-Werror'` to match CI, and validate with `./runtest --tags -slow` plus `./runtest-moduleapi` if you touched `src/module.c`. Be aware this tree's root `Makefile` is not upstream's: plain `make` runs `scripts/build.sh`, which builds `src/` and then every cloned external module.

claims.claim: Read first, in order: `src/server.h` (all struct/constant/prototype definitions), `src/server.c` (`main`, `initServer`, `processCommand`, `call`, `beforeSleep`, `serverCron`), `src/networking.c` (client lifecycle and RESP parsing), and `src/config.c` (`static_configs[]`).

Never edit `src/commands.def` by hand. Edit `src/commands/<cmd>.json`, run `make commands.def` (which invokes `utils/generate-command-code.py`), and commit both — CI's `validate commands.def up to date` step diffs the regenerated output and fails on drift.

Match CI's build flags locally: `make REDIS_CFLAGS='-Werror' BUILD_TLS=yes`. Use `REDIS_CFLAGS`/`REDIS_LDFLAGS` rather than `CFLAGS`/`LDFLAGS` — the src/Makefile header notes that plain CFLAGS propagate into the `deps/` builds (jemalloc, Lua, hiredis) too.

Test commands to run: `make -C src test` (= `./runtest`) for the default suite, `./runtest --tags -slow --dump-logs` to match CI exactly, `./runtest --single unit/type/hash` to scope, `make -C src test-modules`, `test-cluster`, `test-sentinel` for the other three harnesses.

Trap — building Redis alone is `make -C src all`, not `make`. The root `Makefile`'s default goal is `build`, which runs `scripts/build.sh` and will additionally try to build every module cloned under `modules/*/src`. Use `make build redis` or `make build core` to skip modules.

Trap — on macOS you must use `gmake` (GNU Make ≥ 4.x), not Apple's `/usr/bin/make` 3.81. The root Makefile explicitly `export MAKE`s so recipe shells inherit the right binary, precisely because non-interactive recipe shells otherwise PATH-resolve to make 3.81.

Trap — adding a new object type requires coordinated edits to `rdb.c`, `aof.c`, `db.c` (`obj_type_name`, `copyCommand`), `debug.c` (`xorObjectDigest`, `serverLogObjectDebugInfo`) and `defrag.c` (`defragKey`), per the checklist comment in server.h. Nothing enforces this at compile time.

Trap — `redis.conf` is the tracked, hand-edited core config with no markers; `redis-full.conf` is untracked and regenerated by `scripts/sync-redis-conf.sh` on every `make modules-update`. Never hand-add `loadmodule` lines to `redis.conf`.

Safe edit boundary — prefer adding behaviour through the module API (`RM_CreateCommand`, module data types, command filters, server-event hooks) or a new `static_configs[]` entry over modifying `processCommand()`/`call()`, which carry assertions and propagation invariants.

Do not touch `deps/` — it is vendored third-party source (jemalloc, lua, hiredis, linenoise, hdr_histogram, fpconv, xxhash, tre) built by separate targets listed in `DEPENDENCY_TARGETS`. Changes there are lost on dependency refresh.

Style convention — the codebase is C99/gnu11 compiled with `-pedantic -Wall -W -Wstrict-prototypes -Werror=deprecated-declarations`, and falls back to `-std=c99` (also setting `SKIP_VEC_SETS=yes`) when the compiler lacks C11 `_Atomic`. New code must build under both.

Licensing convention — every new source file carries the Redis tri-license header (RSALv2 / SSPLv1 / AGPLv3); contributions are governed by the Software Grant and CLA reproduced in full in CONTRIBUTING.md.

Security convention — do not report vulnerabilities through normal issues; SECURITY.md directs reports to the Redis Vulnerability Disclosure Program or GitHub's 'Report a Vulnerability', and notes that 32-bit, non-Linux and outdated-toolchain findings may be ruled out of scope.

When adding or changing a command's reply, update the reply schema in its `src/commands/*.json` — `.github/workflows/reply-schemas-linter.yml` triggers on changes to those files and validates them with ajv via `utils/reply_schema_linter.js`.

For debugging a failing Tcl test, `./runtest --dump-logs` plus `tests/support/util.tcl`'s helpers and the `s <field>` / `S <index> <field>` INFO accessors in test_helper.tcl are the standard tools; servers spawn on ports starting at `::baseport 21111`.

Bumping a bundled module is a one-line change: edit `ref:` in `modules/modules.yaml` then run `make modules-update <name>`. Ref kind is resolved dynamically against the remote in the order tag → branch → commit, and an unmatched ref errors out with 'unknown ref kind'.

readmePreview: Requests Requests is a simple, yet elegant, HTTP library.

overview.summary: Requests is the PSF-maintained Python HTTP client library (`v2.34.2`, `src/requests/__version__.py`) that wraps urllib3 in a human-friendly API: `requests.get(...)` returns a `Response` with `.text`, `.json()`, `.cookies`, and `.raise_for_status()`. It is a pure-library distribution — no CLI, no server, no database — whose entire user surface is the seven module-level verb functions in `api.py` plus the `Session` object that persists cookies, auth, proxies, and a urllib3 connection pool across calls. What is distinctive in this commit is how much of the codebase is now type-machinery and hardening rather than new features: a private `_types.py` with `TypedDict` kwargs unpacking, pyright in `strict` mode over `src/requests/`, a pinned/hash-locked GitHub Actions setup audited by zizmor, and an explicit anti-LLM contribution policy. The architecture is deliberately layered so that the transport is swappable: `Session.mount(prefix, adapter)` is the single extension seam that every custom TLS, retry, or mock-transport integration in the ecosystem hangs off.

system_map.summary: There is no application entrypoint — the package root `src/requests/__init__.py` is the runtime boundary, and it does dependency-compatibility checking, optional pyOpenSSL SNI injection, and re-export of the public API before anything else runs. Beneath it sit four layers: the stateless verb wrappers (`api.py`), the stateful `Session` (`sessions.py`), the request/response value objects (`models.py`), and the urllib3-backed transport (`adapters.py`). Cross-cutting support lives in `utils.py` (proxies, netrc, header validation, length probing), `cookies.py` (a `CookieJar`/`MutableMapping` hybrid), `structures.py` (`CaseInsensitiveDict`, `LookupDict`), and `exceptions.py`. There is no storage layer: the only persistent state is the in-memory `RequestsCookieJar` on a `Session` and urllib3's connection pools. Build is setuptools via `pyproject.toml`; test/lint/typecheck/publish are four separate GitHub Actions workflows, and distribution is a Trusted-Publishing PyPI upload on `v*` tags.

claims.claim: The package root is the de-facto entrypoint: importing `requests` runs `check_compatibility()` to assert urllib3 >= 1.21.1 and chardet 3.0.2–8.0.0 / charset_normalizer 2.0.0–4.0.0, emitting `RequestsDependencyWarning` on mismatch rather than failing the import.

Import also attempts `pyopenssl.inject_into_urllib3()` when `ssl.HAS_SNI` is falsy and then version-checks `cryptography` via `_check_cryptography()`, warning if below 1.3.4 — a side effect that mutates urllib3 globally at import time.

The public API surface is fixed by the `__all__` tuple in `__init__.py`: 7 verb functions (`get/post/put/patch/delete/head/options`) plus `request`, the `Session`/`Request`/`PreparedRequest`/`Response` types, `codes`, and 9 exception classes.

`api.request()` is stateless by construction — it opens `sessions.Session()` in a `with` block for every call specifically to close sockets and avoid `ResourceWarning`, meaning module-level calls get zero connection reuse.

`Session.__init__` establishes all mutable session state (headers from `default_headers()`, empty proxies/params/hooks, `verify=True`, `max_redirects=DEFAULT_REDIRECT_LIMIT` of 30, `trust_env=True`) and mounts an `HTTPAdapter` for both `https://` and `http://`.

The transport boundary is `HTTPAdapter.send()`, which calls `conn.urlopen(..., redirect=False, preload_content=False, decode_content=False, retries=self.max_retries)` — requests deliberately disables urllib3's own redirect and decode handling and reimplements both.

The only external integrations are the four hard runtime dependencies declared in `pyproject.toml`: `charset_normalizer>=2,<4`, `idna>=2.5,<4`, `urllib3>=1.26,<3`, `certifi>=2023.5.7`; SOCKS and chardet are optional extras.

The CA bundle boundary is `certs.where()`, a one-line re-export of `certifi.where` that the module docstring explicitly names as the seam distro packagers should patch; it is captured once at import into `utils.DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH`.

Build/test commands live in the `Makefile`: `make init` installs `requirements-dev.txt`, `make test` runs `pytest tests`, `make ci` adds `--junitxml=report.xml`, and `make coverage` runs pytest-cov against `src/requests`.

pytest is configured with `addopts = "--doctest-modules"` and `testpaths = ["tests"]`, so the docstring examples in `api.py`, `sessions.py`, and `status_codes.py` are executed as tests alongside the suite.

Deployment is PyPI-only via `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, which builds with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` pinned to the commit time for reproducibility and publishes through `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` with `attestations: true` and `id-token: write` (Trusted Publishing, no stored API token).

Five CI workflows gate the repo: `run-tests.yml` (matrix of Python 3.10–3.15-dev plus 3.14t free-threaded and pypy-3.11, across ubuntu/macOS/windows), `lint.yml` (pre-commit), `typecheck.yml` (pyright), `codeql-analysis.yml`, and `zizmor.yml` for Actions-security scanning.
`packages.py` is a compatibility shim that aliases `sys.modules['requests.packages.urllib3.*']` to the real urllib3/idna/chardet modules so pre-2.16 imports still resolve to identical module objects.
Docs are a separate Sphinx build deployed to Read the Docs with the `dirhtml` builder on Python 3.12, producing PDF and ePub alongside HTML; `make docs` builds them locally.

feature_catalog.summary: Every user-facing feature is a Python API, not a route or command. The catalog splits into: the seven HTTP verb helpers and their `Session` methods; request-construction features (params, form/JSON/multipart/streamed bodies, file uploads, IDNA hostnames); response-consumption features (`.text` with charset auto-detection, `.json()` with UTF-BOM sniffing, `.iter_content`/`.iter_lines` streaming, `.links` header parsing, `.raise_for_status`); and connection features (pooling, redirects, cookie persistence, proxy resolution including SOCKS, TLS verification and mTLS client certs, netrc auth, digest auth). Two auxiliary surfaces exist: `python -m requests.help` prints a JSON environment report for bug filing, and `python -m requests.certs` prints the CA bundle path.

claims.claim: Seven verb helpers are exposed at module level and mirrored as `Session` methods; `head()` uniquely defaults `allow_redirects` to `False` at both levels while `get`/`options` default it to `True`.

Request bodies support four distinct shapes decided in `prepare_body`: JSON via `complexjson.dumps(json, allow_nan=False)` → `application/json`; multipart via `_encode_files`; form-encoding via `_encode_params` → `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`; and streamed iterables/file objects that set `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` when length is unknown.
Multipart uploads accept 2-, 3-, and 4-tuples (`filename, fileobj`, `+content_type`, `+custom_headers`) and are assembled into urllib3 `RequestField` objects by `encode_multipart_formdata`.
Streaming bodies and file uploads are mutually exclusive — combining them raises `NotImplementedError("Streamed bodies and files are mutually exclusive.")`.

Internationalised domains are supported by `_get_idna_encoded_host()`, which applies `idna.encode(host, uts46=True)` for any non-ASCII host and raises `InvalidURL("URL has an invalid label.")` on failure.

`Response.text` decodes using the header-declared charset, falling back to `apparent_encoding` (charset_normalizer or chardet), and finally to `utf-8` with `errors="replace"` if no detection library is installed.
`Response.json()` sniffs UTF-8/16/32 via `guess_json_utf()` when no encoding is declared and the body exceeds 3 bytes, and normalises every decode failure into `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError`.

Streaming download is offered by `iter_content(chunk_size, decode_unicode)` and the line-oriented `iter_lines(delimiter=...)`; re-iterating a consumed non-streamed response raises `StreamConsumedError`.
Pagination via RFC 5988 is supported by `Response.links`, which parses the `Link` header through `parse_header_links()` and keys results by `rel` (falling back to `url`).

`requests.codes` is a `LookupDict` supporting attribute and item access with multiple aliases per code — including the joke aliases `codes['\\o/']` and `codes['✓']` for 200 — generated by `_init()` which also appends the full table to the module docstring.
Three auth handlers ship: `HTTPBasicAuth`, `HTTPProxyAuth` (same header under `Proxy-Authorization`), and `HTTPDigestAuth` supporting MD5, MD5-SESS, SHA, SHA-256 and SHA-512 with `qop=auth`.
`.netrc` credentials are honoured automatically when `trust_env` is true, checked at `$NETRC` if set otherwise `~/.netrc` and `~/_netrc`, and re-applied on cross-host redirects by `rebuild_auth`.

SOCKS proxy support is optional: `proxy_manager_for()` routes `socks*` proxies to `SOCKSProxyManager`, and a stub raising `InvalidSchema("Missing dependencies for SOCKS support.")` is installed when PySocks is absent.

`python -m requests.help` (i.e. `help.main()`) prints a sorted, indented JSON bug-report blob covering platform, interpreter implementation, system OpenSSL version, urllib3, chardet/charset_normalizer, pyOpenSSL, cryptography, idna and requests versions.

Sessions are picklable: `__getstate__`/`__setstate__` serialise the 12 attributes listed in `Session.__attrs__`, while `HTTPAdapter.__setstate__` rebuilds the unpicklable `PoolManager` by re-calling `init_poolmanager`.

data_flow.summary: Input arrives as loosely-typed Python kwargs at `api.request()` or `Session.request()`, is funnelled into a `Request` value object, then normalised into a fully-serialised `PreparedRequest` (bytes body, `CaseInsensitiveDict` headers, percent-encoded URL string) by `Session.prepare_request()`. Session-level and environment-level settings are merged in at two distinct points — `merge_setting`/`merge_hooks` during preparation, and `merge_environment_settings` for proxies/verify/cert/stream just before send. The `PreparedRequest` crosses the adapter boundary into urllib3, and the urllib3 response crosses back through `HTTPAdapter.build_response()`, which is the sole constructor of `Response` objects. State ownership is clean: `Session` owns cookies, adapters and defaults; `PreparedRequest` owns the wire representation; `Response` owns `_content`/`_content_consumed` and lazily pulls bytes off `raw`. Output boundaries are the `Response` accessors and the environment mutations in `should_bypass_proxies` (via `set_environ`) and `extract_zipped_paths` (via `tempfile.mkstemp`).

claims.claim: Settings precedence is implemented by `merge_setting(request_setting, session_setting)`: non-Mapping request values win outright, Mappings are merged with request keys overriding, and any key explicitly set to `None` is deleted from the merged result — that is how callers suppress a session default header.
Hooks need special merging because `{'response': []}` would otherwise wipe session hooks; `merge_hooks` short-circuits when either side has an empty response list.

Cookies flow through a three-way merge in `prepare_request`: `merge_cookies(merge_cookies(RequestsCookieJar(), self.cookies), request.cookies)`, so per-request cookies layer over session cookies into a fresh jar rather than mutating the session's.

`PreparedRequest.prepare()` runs a fixed six-step pipeline — method, url, headers, cookies, body, auth — then hooks; the ordering comment states auth must be last so schemes like OAuth can sign a fully-formed request and still register hooks.

`prepare_auth` mutates the prepared request by `self.__dict__.update(r.__dict__)` from whatever the auth callable returns, then recomputes Content-Length — so an auth handler can legitimately rewrite body and headers.

Credentials embedded in the URL are extracted into auth during preparation: `prepare_auth` calls `get_auth_from_url(self.url)` when no explicit auth was supplied, and `prepare_url` reassembles netloc with the `auth@` prefix preserved.

Environment enters the flow at `merge_environment_settings`, which (only when `trust_env`) seeds proxies from `getproxies()` and overrides `verify` from `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` or `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` — explicitly to be cURL-compatible.

Proxy selection is layered: `resolve_proxies` consults `should_bypass_proxies` (NO_PROXY, CIDR matching, platform `proxy_bypass`), then `select_proxy` picks by the key precedence `scheme://host` → `scheme` → `all://host` → `all`.

Body length determination flows through `super_len()`, which probes `__len__`, `.len`, `fileno()`+`os.fstat`, and `seek/tell`, subtracting the current file position so partially-read files report the remaining bytes.
Header values are validated at the input boundary by `check_header_validity`, which regex-matches against `HEADER_VALIDATORS` to reject CR/LF and leading-whitespace — the CRLF-injection guard.

The response side is constructed exclusively in `HTTPAdapter.build_response()`, which lifts status, `CaseInsensitiveDict` headers, encoding from `get_encoding_from_headers`, `raw`, reason, url, extracts server cookies into `response.cookies`, and back-links `request` and `connection`.
Cookies persist onto the Session after the fact: `Session.send` calls `extract_cookies_to_jar(self.cookies, request, r.raw)` for the final response and separately for every entry in `r.history`.

Response bytes are pulled lazily: `content` joins `iter_content(CONTENT_CHUNK_SIZE)` (10 KiB) once and caches into `_content`, flipping `_content_consumed`; `Session.send` forces this by touching `r.content` whenever `stream` is falsy.

urllib3 exceptions are translated into the requests hierarchy at exactly one place — the `try/except` ladder in `HTTPAdapter.send` mapping `MaxRetryError` reasons to `ConnectTimeout`/`RetryError`/`ProxyError`/`SSLError` and `ProtocolError`/`OSError` to `ConnectionError`.

`should_bypass_proxies` temporarily mutates process environment via the `set_environ('no_proxy', ...)` context manager before calling the stdlib `proxy_bypass`, restoring the prior value in a `finally` block.

behavior_traces.summary: Three flows carry most of the library's behaviour: the one-shot `requests.get()` path, the redirect-following loop inside `Session.send`, and the digest-auth 401 retry. All three converge on `Session.send` → `HTTPAdapter.send` → `build_response`. The redirect loop is a generator (`resolve_redirects`) that is fully drained inside `send`, which is why history arrives pre-assembled on the returned `Response`. The digest flow is unusual in that it re-enters the transport from a response hook (`r.connection.send(prep)`), bypassing `Session.send` entirely.

claims.claim: Import trace: `requests/__init__.py` runs `check_compatibility` → optional `pyopenssl.inject_into_urllib3` → `warnings.simplefilter('ignore', DependencyWarning)` → re-exports → `logging.getLogger(__name__).addHandler(NullHandler())` → `simplefilter('default', FileModeWarning, append=True)`.

One-shot GET trace: `api.get()` → `api.request()` opens `Session()` in a `with` → `Session.request()` → builds `Request` → `Session.prepare_request()` → `merge_environment_settings()` → `Session.send()` → returns, and `__exit__` calls `Session.close()` closing every adapter.

Preparation trace: `prepare_request` → `PreparedRequest.prepare()` → `prepare_method` (uppercases) → `prepare_url` (IDNA + `requote_uri(urlunparse(...))`) → `prepare_headers` (`check_header_validity` per header) → `prepare_cookies` (sets `Cookie` header once) → `prepare_body` → `prepare_auth` → `prepare_hooks`.

Send trace: `Session.send` defaults stream/verify/cert, rejects a bare `Request` with `ValueError("You can only send PreparedRequests.")`, resolves the adapter by longest matching prefix via `get_adapter`, times the call with `preferred_clock` into `r.elapsed`, then dispatches the `response` hook.

Adapter trace: `HTTPAdapter.send` → `get_connection_with_tls_context` → `cert_verify` (sets `conn.ca_certs`/`cert_file`, raising `OSError` if any path is missing) → `request_url` (full URL for proxied HTTP, path-only otherwise) → `add_headers` (no-op hook) → `conn.urlopen(...)` → `build_response`.

Redirect trace: `Session.send` calls `resolve_redirects(r, request)` and drains the generator into `history`; the generator per hop consumes `resp.content`, checks `len(resp.history) >= self.max_redirects` raising `TooManyRedirects`, calls `resp.close()`, normalises the Location, and copies the request.

On a non-307/308 redirect the loop strips `Content-Length`, `Content-Type` and `Transfer-Encoding` and blanks `prepared_request.body`, then always pops the `Cookie` header before re-deriving it from the jar.
Method rewriting per hop is `rebuild_method`: 303 → GET (unless HEAD), 302 → GET (unless HEAD, 'what browsers do, despite standards'), and 301 on a POST → GET.

Auth rewriting per hop is `rebuild_auth` → `should_strip_auth`, which drops `Authorization` on any hostname change but deliberately preserves it for http:80 → https:443 on the same host for backwards compatibility.

Body rewind trace: a redirect with `_body_position` set and a length header triggers `rewind_body(prepared_request)`; a prior failed `tell()` stores a sentinel `object()` so the rewind raises `UnrewindableBodyError` instead of hanging the connection.

Non-following trace: when `allow_redirects=False`, `Session.send` primes `r._next` by taking one item from `resolve_redirects(..., yield_requests=True)` inside a `try/except StopIteration`, which is what backs `Response.next`.

Digest trace: `HTTPDigestAuth.__call__` registers `handle_401` and `handle_redirect` as response hooks and records `r.body.tell()`; on a 4xx `handle_401` parses `www-authenticate`, consumes and closes the response, copies the request, builds the `Authorization` header and re-sends via `r.connection.send(prep, **kwargs)`, appending the original to `_r.history`.

Digest state is per-thread: `init_per_thread_state()` lazily populates `threading.local()` with `last_nonce`, `nonce_count`, `chal`, `pos` and `num_401_calls`, and the retry is capped at `num_401_calls < 2`.

Streaming-read trace: `iter_content` builds a generator that prefers `self.raw.stream(chunk_size, decode_content=True)`, translating `ProtocolError`→`ChunkedEncodingError`, `DecodeError`→`ContentDecodingError`, `ReadTimeoutError`→`ConnectionError` and urllib3 `SSLError`→`requests.SSLError`, then sets `_content_consumed`.
Teardown trace: `Session.close()` iterates adapters calling `HTTPAdapter.close()`, which does `poolmanager.clear()` and clears every cached proxy manager.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is pytest-only, concentrated in one 108 KB file: `tests/test_requests.py` holds 237 of the ~347 test functions, with `tests/test_utils.py` (64) and `tests/test_lowlevel.py` (13) next. Integration tests run against a real local `httpbin` via the `pytest-httpbin` fixture (wrapped by `conftest.prepare_url` to guarantee a trailing slash), while wire-level behaviour uses a hand-rolled socket `Server` thread in `tests/testserver/server.py`. TLS behaviour is covered by checked-in fixture certificates (`tests/certs/{valid,expired,mtls}`) plus a `trustme`-generated no-SAN server fixture. Doctests in the library modules are executed by `--doctest-modules`. Gaps: `adapters.py` — the single most security-relevant module — has a one-test dedicated file, and there is no coverage threshold enforced anywhere.

claims.claim: The framework is pytest with `minversion = 6.2`, `testpaths = ["tests"]`, and `--doctest-modules` plus `NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE ELLIPSIS` optionflags, so module docstring examples are part of the suite.

Test distribution is extremely lopsided: `tests/test_requests.py` defines 237 `test_` functions across 7 classes (`TestRequests`, `TestCaseInsensitiveDict`, `TestMorselToCookieExpires`, `TestMorselToCookieMaxAge`, `TestTimeout`, `RedirectSession`, `TestPreparingURLs`), versus 64 in `test_utils.py` and 13 in `test_lowlevel.py`.

An autouse fixture `clean_proxy_environ` monkeypatches away `http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `no_proxy`, `ftp_proxy` and `all_proxy` (both cases) for every test, so proxy tests must set env vars explicitly.
Integration coverage runs against a live httpbin server through the `httpbin`/`httpbin_secure` fixtures, pinned via `pytest-httpbin==2.1.0` and `httpbin~=0.10.0` in the `test` dependency group.

Wire-level tests use a purpose-built threaded socket server with `text_response_server` / `basic_response_server` helpers, exercising chunked upload, conflicting Content-Length, RFC 1808 non-ASCII redirects and fragment handling.
Digest auth is covered at the socket level by three dedicated tests: `test_digestauth_401_count_reset_on_redirect`, `test_digestauth_401_only_sent_once`, and `test_digestauth_only_on_4xx`.

TLS paths are tested with committed fixture certs — expired server cert, valid server cert, and an mTLS client cert — including `test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings` verifying pool-key separation.
A `nosan_server` fixture mints a CA and a commonName-only (no subjectAltName) certificate at runtime using `trustme`, backing the SNI/SAN warning tests.
`test_response_iter_lines_reentrant` is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` and documents a known defect: `Response.iter_lines()` is not reentrant-safe, matching the docstring note on the method itself.

Behaviour differences between urllib3 1.x and 2.x are handled by skips keyed on `is_urllib3_1`, e.g. `test_content_length_for_string_data_counts_bytes` skips on 1.x because it encodes strings as latin-1 rather than utf-8.
`adapters.py` has a single dedicated regression test (`test_request_url_handles_leading_path_separators`); the rest of the adapter is exercised only indirectly through `test_requests.py`.
CI runs `make ci` (`pytest tests --junitxml=report.xml`) across 8 Python versions × 3 OSes, plus two special jobs: `no_chardet` uninstalls both detection libraries, and `urllib3` pins `urllib3<2`.

Typechecking is enforced in CI as a separate gate: pyright in `strict` mode over `include = ["src/requests"]`, run on Python 3.10 and 3.14 — note `tests/` is deliberately outside the typechecked surface.

Coverage is available locally via `make coverage` with a `.coveragerc` whose only directive omits `requests/packages/*` — a stale path given the package now lives under `src/requests/`; no minimum threshold is configured and no workflow uploads coverage.
Lint runs as its own workflow executing pre-commit (`ruff-check --fix`, `ruff-format`, plus whitespace/merge-conflict hooks), with `tests/test_lowlevel.py` explicitly excluded from `ruff-format`.

risk_map.summary: As a library in ~4M dependent repos, the blast radius of any change here is close to maximal, and the highest-risk surfaces are the ones that decide whether credentials cross a trust boundary: `should_strip_auth`, `rebuild_proxies`, `prepare_url`, and `cert_verify`. Several behaviours are knowingly non-ideal and preserved for backwards compatibility — the http→https auth-retention carve-out, `_basic_auth_str` accepting non-strings, and `LookupDict.__getitem__` silently returning `None`. Environment trust is on by default (`trust_env=True`), so `.netrc`, `$NETRC`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`/`CURL_CA_BUNDLE` and `*_proxy` variables all influence behaviour implicitly. Filesystem and process-global side effects exist in `extract_zipped_paths`, `atomic_open`, `set_environ`, and the import-time `pyopenssl.inject_into_urllib3()`.

claims.claim: `should_strip_auth` intentionally keeps the `Authorization` header across an http:80 → https:443 redirect on the same host; the comment states this is not RFC 7235 behaviour and is retained only for backwards compatibility.

`rebuild_proxies` reconstructs `Proxy-Authorization` from proxy URL credentials but skips it when the target scheme starts with `https`, explicitly to avoid leaking the header into a TLS tunnel — a subtle invariant easy to break in a refactor.

Any URL containing a colon whose scheme does not start with `http` bypasses all URL preparation and is assigned verbatim to `self.url`, so `mailto:`/`data:`-style inputs skip IDNA, requoting and host validation entirely.

`verify=False` disables certificate and hostname validation at the urllib3 level (`cert_reqs = 'CERT_NONE'`, ca_certs cleared); the Session docstring is explicit that this exposes callers to MitM and is for testing only.
`trust_env=True` by default means an attacker-controlled or accidentally-set `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`/`CURL_CA_BUNDLE` silently replaces the trust store for every request on the session.

`get_netrc_auth` reads credentials from a path taken from the `$NETRC` environment variable without restriction, and swallows `NetrcParseError`/`OSError` unless `raise_errors=True` — failures to read credentials are silent by default.

`extract_zipped_paths` performs file IO outside the repo root: it walks a path upward looking for a zip archive, then extracts a member into a `tempfile.mkstemp()` file that is never cleaned up, returning that path to the caller.

`_basic_auth_str` still accepts non-string usernames/passwords, coercing them with a `DeprecationWarning` promising removal in 3.0.0; the source comment preserves it precisely because callers depend on it.

Digest auth uses MD5 by default when the server omits an `algorithm` directive; MD5/SHA-1 usage is flagged `usedforsecurity=False` to appease FIPS builds but the weak-hash negotiation is server-driven.

`handle_401` re-sends the authenticated request directly through `r.connection.send(prep, **kwargs)`, bypassing `Session.send` — so session-level cookie extraction, hooks, and redirect resolution do not run for that hop.

`prepare_auth` blanket-applies `self.__dict__.update(r.__dict__)` from a user-supplied callable, meaning a third-party auth class can overwrite any attribute of the PreparedRequest including `url` and `hooks`.
`LookupDict.__getitem__` deliberately falls through to `None` for unknown keys, so a typo'd `requests.codes['okey']` silently yields `None` instead of raising — a footgun with no test-enforced guard.

`HTTPAdapter.get_connection` is live deprecated code retained for subclass compatibility; it emits a `DeprecationWarning` and, unlike `get_connection_with_tls_context`, does not incorporate verify/cert into the pool key.

`compat.py` is largely legacy: it still exports `is_py2`, `is_py3`, `basestring`, `numeric_types` and `integer_types` for a Python 2 that the project no longer supports (`requires-python = ">=3.10"`), and shadows the builtin `str`/`bytes` names.
`packages.py` mutates the global `sys.modules` table at import time to alias urllib3/idna/chardet under `requests.packages.*` — a process-wide side effect purely for pre-2.16 backwards compatibility.
`.coveragerc` omits `requests/packages/*`, a path that no longer exists since the move to `src/` layout, so the omit rule is dead configuration.
Release-critical files are protected by CODEOWNERS requiring lead-maintainer review: `.github/workflows/`, `src/requests/__version__.py`, `HISTORY.md` and `pyproject.toml`.

extension_points.summary: There is one primary extension seam and several secondary ones. The primary is the Transport Adapter: `Session.mount(prefix, adapter)` keeps `self.adapters` sorted by descending prefix length and `get_adapter` picks the longest matching prefix, so any URL prefix can be routed to a `BaseAdapter` subclass — this is how retry policies, custom TLS contexts, and test doubles are injected. Secondary seams are the response hook system, the `AuthBase` callable protocol, the `SessionRedirectMixin` methods documented as overridable, and the packager-facing `certs.where()`. Nearly every private-looking `HTTPAdapter` method carries a docstring saying it exists specifically for subclass overrides.

claims.claim: `Session.mount(prefix, adapter)` is the registry: it inserts into the `self.adapters` OrderedDict then re-pops every shorter key so adapters stay in descending prefix-length order.

`Session.get_adapter(url)` resolves by case-insensitive `startswith` over that ordered map, raising `InvalidSchema(f"No connection adapters were found for {url!r}")` when nothing matches — so registering a new scheme is purely a mount call.
`BaseAdapter` defines the minimal contract — `send(request, stream, timeout, verify, cert, proxies)` and `close()` — that any replacement transport must implement.

Eight `HTTPAdapter` methods are documented as subclass-override points rather than user API: `init_poolmanager`, `proxy_manager_for`, `cert_verify`, `build_response`, `get_connection_with_tls_context`, `request_url`, `add_headers`, and `proxy_headers`.

`HTTPAdapter.add_headers()` is an intentional empty hook — 'As of v2.0 this does nothing by default, but is left for overriding by users that subclass' — and is called on every send with the full kwargs.
`init_poolmanager(**pool_kwargs)` forwards arbitrary kwargs to `urllib3.PoolManager`, which is the documented way to inject a custom `ssl_context` or TLS version.

The hook registry is the `HOOKS = ['response']` list in `hooks.py`, with `default_hooks()` building `{event: []}` and `dispatch_hook()` chaining callables so each non-None return replaces the data for the next hook.

Hooks can be attached per-request (`hooks=` kwarg), per-session (`Session.hooks`), or programmatically via `RequestHooksMixin.register_hook` / `deregister_hook`, which both `Request` and `PreparedRequest` inherit.
Custom auth plugs in via `AuthBase`, whose `__call__(self, r) -> PreparedRequest` raises `NotImplementedError` by default; `prepare_auth` treats any non-2-tuple auth value as such a callable.

`SessionRedirectMixin` is a separately-inheritable class exposing `get_redirect_target`, `should_strip_auth`, `resolve_redirects`, `rebuild_auth`, `rebuild_proxies` and `rebuild_method` — the tests subclass it directly as `RedirectSession` to exercise redirect logic without a network.
`get_redirect_target`'s docstring explicitly invites a custom mixin that caches the redirect location on the response as a private attribute, acknowledging the method is called redundantly per hop.
`certs.where()` is the packager extension point: the module docstring instructs distributors to change its definition to return a separately packaged CA bundle.

Character-detection backends are pluggable at import: `_resolve_char_detection()` tries `chardet` then `charset_normalizer`, and `Response.apparent_encoding` degrades to a plain `utf-8` assumption if neither is installed.
The status-code table is data-driven: adding a code means adding an entry to the `_codes` dict, and `_init()` generates both lowercase and uppercase attributes plus the docstring table automatically.
Custom HTTP verbs need no new code — `Session.request(method, ...)` uppercases whatever string it is given, which is the documented 'Custom Verbs' capability.
Optional extras are declared as installable feature flags in `pyproject.toml`: `socks` (PySocks), `use_chardet_on_py3` (chardet), and a now-empty `security` extra kept for compatibility.

agent_handoff.summary: Treat this repo as a stability-first, extremely high-blast-radius library: the maintainers protect version, changelog, workflows and pyproject behind CODEOWNERS, and the project has a written policy banning unsupervised agentic contributions. Read `sessions.py`, `models.py` and `adapters.py` before touching anything; almost every non-obvious branch in them encodes a specific GitHub issue number that you should look up before 'simplifying' it. Local loop is `make init` then `make test`; before pushing, run `pre-commit run --all-files` and `pyright src/requests/`, since lint and typecheck are separate required CI gates. The biggest trap is that `tests/` is excluded from pyright but `src/requests/` is checked in `strict` mode, so type annotations in library code must be complete and the codebase is dense with deliberate `# type: ignore` comments carrying explanatory reasons — preserve them.

claims.claim: `.github/AI_POLICY.md` states 'Absolutely no unsupervised agentic tools' and requires a human copyright owner per contribution with no LLM bots in `Co-authored-by:` — do not open PRs against this upstream without explicit human sponsorship.

Read first, in order: `src/requests/api.py` (surface), `src/requests/sessions.py` (orchestration), `src/requests/models.py` (value objects), `src/requests/adapters.py` (transport). These four contain the whole request lifecycle.
Local setup and test: `make init` installs `requirements-dev.txt` (editable `.[socks]`, pytest, pytest-httpbin, httpbin, trustme); `make test` runs `pytest tests`; `make ci` matches CI exactly.
Two additional gates must pass before merge: `pre-commit run --all-files` (ruff-check --fix and ruff-format) and `python -m pyright src/requests/` under `typeCheckingMode = "strict"`.

Style is enforced by ruff with rule sets E/W/F/I/UP/T10 targeting py310, ignoring E203/E501/UP031, with per-file `E402,F401` exemptions for `src/requests/__init__.py` and `src/requests/compat.py` — do not 'clean up' those unused imports, they are the public re-export surface.

`src/requests/_types.py` is explicitly documented as not part of the public API; it hosts the `RequestKwargs`/`GetKwargs`/`PostKwargs`/`DataKwargs` TypedDicts consumed via `Unpack` in `api.py` and `sessions.py`, so adding a request kwarg means editing both the runtime signature and the TypedDict.

`_types.is_prepared()` is a typing-only narrowing helper that returns `True` unconditionally at runtime; the many `assert _is_prepared(request)` lines are type assertions, not validation — do not convert them into runtime checks.

Safe edit boundary: new transport behaviour belongs in an `HTTPAdapter` subclass or the documented override methods, not in `Session.send`, because `Session.send` is also reached by `resolve_redirects` and any change there multiplies across every redirect hop.

Trap: `prepare_cookies` can only meaningfully run once per PreparedRequest — cookielib will not regenerate the header if `Cookie` already exists, which is why `resolve_redirects` pops the header before re-preparing.

Trap: branch comments cite issue numbers as the rationale (e.g. #1084 for the 307/308 carve-out, #3490 for the purged headers, #1704 for POST-301→GET, #3772 for digest-only-on-4xx, #5229 for the `fileno` AttributeError). Look these up before changing the branch.

Trap: `compat.py` rebinds `str` and `bytes` to the builtins and exports `basestring = (str, bytes)`; modules importing from it (`auth.py`, `utils.py`, `adapters.py`) rely on these shadows, so removing them is a wide breaking change.
Tests requiring network-like behaviour need the local httpbin fixture; use the `httpbin` fixture (which yields a URL-joining callable, not a string) rather than hardcoding `https://httpbin.org`.
New doctests are load-bearing: because `--doctest-modules` is on, any `>>>` example added to a library docstring will be executed by `make test` and must actually pass.

Version bumps live in `src/requests/__version__.py` (both `__version__` and the hex `__build__`), are resolved dynamically by setuptools, and are CODEOWNERS-gated — never bump as part of a feature PR.
Compatibility floor is Python 3.10 enforced in three places — `requires-python`, the `setup.py` guard that prints an error and exits 1, and ruff's `target-version = "py310"` — so no 3.11+ syntax.

Behaviour must hold across both urllib3 major versions and with no charset library at all; CI has dedicated `urllib3 1.x` and `No Character Detection` jobs, and `compat.is_urllib3_1` exists for version-conditional code.
