readmePreview: ripgrep (rg) ------------ ripgrep is a line-oriented search tool that recursively searches the current directory for a regex pattern.

overview.summary: ripgrep is a line-oriented recursive search tool (`rg`) written in Rust that walks a directory tree while respecting `.gitignore`/`.ignore` rules, matches each file with either Rust's `regex` crate or PCRE2, and prints results through one of three printers (standard/summary/JSON). The repository is a Cargo workspace: a thin binary crate at `crates/core` glues together ten reusable library crates (`grep-matcher`, `grep-regex`, `grep-pcre2`, `grep-searcher`, `grep-printer`, `grep-cli`, `ignore`, `globset`, plus the experimental `grep-index`), each published independently on crates.io. What is distinctive is the amount of engineering in the boring parts: a hand-rolled CLI parser over a 246KB table of `&dyn Flag` trait objects that also generates the man page, `--help` text and four shells' completions from the same source of truth; a directory walker that reimplements gitignore precedence with a parallel work-stealing traversal; and a searcher that chooses between memory maps, a reusable line buffer, and multi-line slice scanning per file. An unstable `unstable-index` feature adds a redb+fst ngram index behind `-X/--index` and `--x-crud`.

system_map.summary: The workspace root `Cargo.toml` declares the `ripgrep` package producing one binary `rg` from `crates/core/main.rs`, and lists ten workspace members under `crates/`. `crates/core` is not published as a library — it is pure glue plus the CLI definition, as its README states. Dependencies flow strictly downward: core → `grep` facade → `grep-searcher`/`grep-printer`/`grep-regex`/`grep-pcre2`/`grep-cli`/`grep-matcher`, with `ignore` and `globset` used for traversal and glob filtering. There is no network, database or server component in the default build; the only external integrations are subprocesses (decompressors, `--pre` preprocessor, hostname binary) and, under `unstable-index`, a redb embedded database on disk. Deployment is static binaries cross-compiled for ~14 targets by a tag-triggered GitHub Actions release workflow, plus a Debian package described by `[package.metadata.deb]`.

claims.claim: The single binary target `rg` is declared in the root manifest with `path = "crates/core/main.rs"`, and `autotests = false` with one explicit `[[test]] name = "integration", path = "tests/tests.rs"`.

`fn main() -> ExitCode` calls `run(flags::parse())` and dispatches on `args.mode()` into seven arms: indexed search, single-threaded `search`, `search_parallel`, `index::write`, `files`/`files_parallel`, `types`, and `generate`.

The workspace has ten members — `globset`, `grep`, `cli`, `index`, `matcher`, `pcre2`, `printer`, `regex`, `searcher`, `ignore` — sharing `edition = "2024"` and `rust-version = "1.96"` via `[workspace.package]`.
`crates/grep` is a pure facade that re-exports the constituent crates as `grep::cli`, `grep::matcher`, `grep::printer`, `grep::regex`, `grep::searcher` and (feature-gated) `grep::pcre2`.

The published crate names differ from directory names: `crates/matcher` is `grep-matcher` v0.1.9, `crates/printer` is `grep-printer` v0.3.1, `crates/searcher` is `grep-searcher` v0.1.17, `crates/regex` is `grep-regex` v0.1.14.

There is no persistent storage in the default build; the only storage layer is the optional `grep-index` crate, which opens a redb `Database`/`ReadOnlyDatabase` at a file named `index.db` inside a discovered `.ripgrep` directory.

`grep-index` is marked `publish = false`, version `0.0.1`, and is wired in only through the `unstable-index` Cargo feature (`dep:grep-index`), which the root manifest itself warns "may have very serious bugs".

Index code is compiled behind a `#[path]` module swap: `crates/core/index/mod.rs` selects `disabled.rs` (which `bail!`s "indexing not enabled in this build") or `enabled.rs` based on the `unstable-index` feature.

`build.rs` embeds the short git hash as `RIPGREP_BUILD_GIT_HASH` by shelling out to `git rev-parse --short=10 HEAD`, and on `windows`+`msvc` embeds `pkg/windows/Manifest.xml` via `/MANIFEST:EMBED` linker args to enable long paths.

Build/test commands are `cargo build --release` (optionally `--features pcre2`) and `cargo test --all`; CI additionally runs `cargo test --workspace --features unstable-index` and `cargo fmt --all --check`.
On musl 64-bit targets the binary swaps in jemalloc as the `#[global_allocator]` because musl's allocator measurably slows ripgrep down; this is the only allocator override.

Release shape: a `release-lto` profile (fat LTO, `panic = "abort"`, `codegen-units = 1`, symbols stripped) plus `.cargo/config.toml` forcing `+crt-static` for MSVC and musl targets so shipped binaries are statically linked.

The release workflow triggers only on `[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+` tags, verifies the tag matches the `version = "..."` line in `Cargo.toml`, and fans out over ~14 targets including aarch64/armv7/s390x/powerpc64 Linux, macOS x86_64+arm64 and four Windows targets.

Packaging metadata installs `rg`, licenses, CHANGELOG/README/FAQ, plus a generated man page and bash/fish/zsh completions from `deployment/deb/` — artifacts that do not exist in the repo and must be produced by `ci/build-deb`.

feature_catalog.summary: ripgrep's user surface is a single command with a very large flag set: `FLAGS` in `crates/core/flags/defs.rs` is a static slice of `&dyn Flag` trait objects, each carrying short/long/negated/alias names, a documentation category, short and long (mdoc) help text, a completion type, and an `update` method that mutates `LowArgs`. Beyond plain search, the binary has distinct top-level modes — `--files`, `--type-list`, `--generate`, `-h/--help`/`-V/--version` special modes, and the experimental index modes. Output modes (`--count`, `--count-matches`, `-l/--files-with-matches`, `--files-without-match`, `--json`) select among three printers. Filtering features include gitignore semantics, `-t/--type` file types, `-g/--glob` overrides, hidden-file handling and `--max-filesize`. Provider-style integrations are the pluggable regex engine (`--engine auto|default|pcre2`), decompression (`-z`), arbitrary preprocessors (`--pre`), and terminal hyperlinks.

claims.claim: `Mode` enumerates the five top-level behaviors — `Search(SearchMode)`, `Index(IndexMode)`, `Files`, `Types`, `Generate(GenerateMode)` — with `Mode::Search(SearchMode::Standard)` as the default.

`SearchMode` has six variants (`Standard`, `FilesWithMatches`, `FilesWithoutMatch`, `Count`, `CountMatches`, `JSON`) and `HiArgs::printer` maps them onto `Printer::Standard`, `Printer::JSON` or `Printer::Summary` with a `SummaryKind`.

`--generate` emits ancillary artifacts: `GenerateMode::Man` produces roff, and `CompleteBash`/`CompleteZsh`/`CompleteFish`/`CompletePowerShell` produce shell completions, all rendered from the same `FLAGS` table.

`-h` and `--help` render different documents (`generate_short` vs `generate_long`) from `template.short.help` / `template.long.help`, interpolating per-category placeholders like `!!filter!!` and `!!output-modes!!`.
`--type-list` is implemented by `types()` in main, which iterates `args.types().definitions()` and prints `name: glob, glob` lines, exiting 1 if there are no definitions.
ripgrep ships a large built-in file-type table, `DEFAULT_TYPES`, mapping type names to glob lists (e.g. `ada` → `*.adb`,`*.ads`), extensible per-invocation via `--type-add`.

Three regex engine choices are supported: `EngineChoice::Default` (Rust regex), `PCRE2`, and `Auto`, where `Auto` tries Rust first and falls back to PCRE2, reporting both errors side by side if both fail.

`-z/--search-zip` transparently decompresses by file extension using external binaries: gzip, bzip2, xz (also for `.lzma`), lz4, brotli, zstd and `uncompress`, keyed by globs like `*.gz`, `*.tgz`, `*.zst`, `*.Z`.
`--pre` runs an arbitrary user program per file with the path as argv[1] and the file on stdin, optionally restricted by `--pre-glob` via `preprocessor_globs`.

Hyperlink support is a first-class feature with named aliases (e.g. `"vscode".parse::<HyperlinkFormat>()`) and interpolation variables including `{host}` and a `{wslprefix}` derived from `WSL_DISTRO_NAME`.

Sorting is user-selectable across four criteria — `path`, `modified`, `accessed`, `created` — with reverse variants; `HiArgs::sort` special-cases ascending path sort to be done during traversal instead of by buffering.

The experimental indexing surface consists of `--x-crud` (create/update/remove index entries), `--x-index-force` and `--x-index-path`, all in the `Category::Indexing` group, which renders as "Indexing is not supported in this build of ripgrep." when the feature is off.
`--stats` produces either a human block (matches / matched lines / files searched / bytes printed / seconds) or, in JSON mode, an extra `{"type":"summary"}` record with `elapsed_total`.

`ignore` exposes a second public feature beyond traversal: `IncrementalIgnore`, built via `WalkBuilder::build_matchers()`, which checks individual paths against hierarchical ignore files without re-walking the tree.

data_flow.summary: Input enters at three boundaries: `std::env::args_os()`, an optional rc file named by `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`, and stdin (patterns via `-f -`, or the haystack itself). The parser folds all of these into a flat, dumb `LowArgs` struct through `Flag::update`, then `HiArgs::from_low_args` performs all the "expensive" derivations — compiling globs, building the type matcher, resolving the CWD and hostname, choosing thread count and mmap strategy. `HiArgs` is the single state owner for the rest of the process; every downstream object (`ignore::WalkBuilder`, `grep::searcher::Searcher`, the matcher, the printer, the `SearchWorker`) is constructed from it by a dedicated accessor. Bytes then flow file → `Searcher` → `Sink` → printer → `termcolor` writer, either directly to stdout (single-threaded) or into per-thread `termcolor::Buffer`s flushed by a `BufferWriter` (parallel). Exit status is a fourth output channel, driven by a match flag plus a global `ERRORED` atomic.

claims.claim: Config args are read from the file named by `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`, one shell argument per line with `#` comments and blank lines skipped, then **prepended** to `std::env::args_os().skip(1)` and the whole CLI is re-parsed from scratch.
`--no-config` short-circuits before the config file is read, and `-h`/`-V` short-circuit even earlier via `ParseResult::Special`, so help output never depends on the config file or the CWD.

Each flag writes into `LowArgs` — a flat struct of ~60 public(crate) fields — via `Flag::update(FlagValue, &mut LowArgs)`, and by convention `update` only validates, deferring side effects (e.g. resolving `--hostname-bin`) to the high-level stage.

Patterns are drained from `LowArgs` by `Patterns::from_low_args`, which promotes the first positional to a pattern only when neither `-e` nor `-f` was given, reads `-f -` through `grep::cli::patterns_from_stdin()`, and de-duplicates patterns to avoid pathological regex compile costs.

`Paths::from_low_args` runs after patterns so all remaining positionals are paths; with none given it uses `grep::cli::is_readable_stdin()` as a heuristic to choose between searching `./` and searching `-` (stdin), and errors if stdin would be consumed twice.
`State` tracks one-shot derived facts across the low→high conversion, notably `stdin_consumed`, which is what makes the double-stdin error and the CWD heuristic consistent.
Thread count is derived once in `from_low_args`: forced to 1 when `--sort` is set or only one file is searched, else `--threads`, else `available_parallelism()` capped at 12.
Memory-map policy is decided from the path set: `MmapMode::Auto` only enables mmap when ≤10 paths are given and all of them are files; otherwise `MmapChoice::never()`.

Traversal output is `Result<ignore::DirEntry, ignore::Error>`, converted by `HaystackBuilder::build_from_result` into `Option<Haystack>`; errors are reported through `err_message!` and non-file, non-explicit entries are dropped with a debug log.
`SearchWorker::search` selects among four data sources per haystack in priority order: stdin lock, preprocessor subprocess, decompression subprocess, then direct `search_path`.

Search results reach printers only through the `Sink` trait (`matched`, `context`, `context_break`, `binary_data`, `begin`, `finish`); `search_path`/`search_reader` build a `sink_with_path` per printer variant and harvest `has_match()` and `stats()` from it.

In parallel mode each worker owns a cloned `SearchWorker` writing into its own `termcolor::Buffer`; the buffer is cleared before each file and printed atomically via `bufwtr.print(...)` to avoid interleaving.
In `--files` parallel mode output is funneled through an `mpsc::channel::<Haystack>` to a single dedicated printing thread, deliberately in place of a mutex.
Exit status is computed from two independent channels: the boolean `matched` returned by the mode function and the process-global `ERRORED` atomic flipped by `err_message!`, yielding 0/1/2.

behavior_traces.summary: Three flows dominate: startup/arg-parsing, a default recursive search, and the file-listing path. All of them funnel through `flags::parse()` → `HiArgs` and then diverge on `Mode`. The parallel search path is notable because parallelism lives entirely in the directory walker — `search_parallel` just hands a closure to `WalkParallel::run` and never manages threads itself. The indexed path currently degrades gracefully: `index::read` opens the index and then falls straight through to the ordinary exhaustive search.

claims.claim: Startup order: `main` → `flags::parse()` → `parse_low()` which first calls `Logger::init()`, then `Parser::new().parse(env::args_os().skip(1), &mut low)`, then `set_log_levels(&low)` so `--trace` is live before config parsing.

If a config file yields arguments, the parser discards the first `LowArgs`, builds a fresh `LowArgs::default()`, re-parses `config_args ++ argv`, and re-runs `set_log_levels` because logging flags may have changed.

`Parser::new()` returns a `&'static Parser` memoized in a `OnceLock`, so the flag-name trie (`FlagMap` over short names, long names, aliases and negations) is built exactly once per process even though `lookup()` calls it repeatedly.
`HiArgs::from_low_args` begins by asserting `low.special == None` ("special mode demands short-circuiting"), which encodes the invariant that help/version never reach high-level conversion.

Default search trace: `run` → `search(args, mode)` → `args.walk_builder()?.build()` → `haystack_builder.build_from_result` → `args.sort(...)` → `args.search_worker(args.matcher()?, args.searcher()?, args.printer(mode, args.stdout()))` → loop `searcher.search(&haystack)`.

Inside one file's search: `SearchWorker::search` sets binary detection (explicit vs implicit) on the `Searcher`, then `search_path` dispatches on the `PatternMatcher` enum to the generic `search_path(m, searcher, printer, path)`, which calls `p.sink_with_path(&matcher, path)` and `searcher.search_path`.

`Searcher::search_path` → `search_file_maybe_path` first tries `self.config.mmap.open(file, path)` and searches the resulting slice; only if mmap is unavailable does it fall back to the incremental reader path.
The searcher has three internal strategies implemented in `glue.rs`: `ReadByLine` (streaming reader), `SliceByLine` (whole-slice, e.g. mmap) and `MultiLine` (when `--multiline` is on).

Parallel search trace: `search_parallel` creates a `BufferWriter`, an `AtomicBool` matched/searched pair and an optional `Mutex<Stats>`, then `args.walk_builder()?.build_parallel().run(|| Box::new(move |result| ...))` clones a `SearchWorker` per thread.

Early exit under `-q/--quiet` is implemented twice: the sequential loop `break`s when `matched && args.quit_after_match()`, and the parallel closure returns `WalkState::Quit`, which aborts the whole traversal.

Broken pipe is handled at three levels: inside the search loop (`break`), inside `bufwtr.print` (`WalkState::Quit`), and finally in `main`, which walks `err.chain()` for an `io::Error` of kind `BrokenPipe` and returns exit code 0.

Preprocessor trace: `search_preprocessor` builds `Command::new(bin).arg(path).stdin(Stdio::from(File::open(path)?))`, wraps it in a `CommandReader`, searches the reader, then calls `rdr.close()` so a non-zero exit code surfaces stderr as a Rust error.

Indexed search currently does no index-based pruning: `index::read` calls `args.index_read()?`, discards the handle into `let _index`, and then delegates to the ordinary `search`/`search_parallel` ("Do an exhaustive search for now").

Index discovery trace: `IndexDiscovery::discover` checks `RIPGREP_INDEX_PATH` first, then walks `cwd.ancestors()` looking for a `.ripgrep` directory containing `index.db`, returning `None` when nothing is found.

Man page generation trace: `generate()` groups `FLAGS` by `doc_category()` into a `BTreeMap`, renders each flag's roff via `generate_flag`, then substitutes `!!VERSION!!` and per-category `!!name!!` placeholders in `template.rg.1`.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is two-tier and unusually thorough for a CLI. Integration tests live in `tests/` behind a single `[[test]] integration` target and drive the real `rg` binary in a temp directory via a `Dir`/`TestCommand` harness; the `rgtest!` macro automatically runs every test twice — once with the default engine and once with PCRE2 — when the `pcre2` feature is on. Unit tests live inline in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` blocks, heavily concentrated in `crates/core/flags/defs.rs` (116 `#[test]`s, mostly per-flag parse assertions) and `crates/printer/src/standard.rs` (74). CI runs the suite on 18 build configurations including cross-compiled big-endian (s390x, powerpc64) and 32-bit targets, plus rustfmt, `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`, a wasm32-wasip1 build check, and a cargo-fuzz compile check. There is no coverage measurement and no benchmark job; `benchsuite/` is a separate Python/shell harness not run by CI.

claims.claim: The integration suite is one binary: `tests/tests.rs` declares modules `binary`, `feature`, `json`, `misc`, `multiline`, `regression`, plus `index` gated on `#[cfg(feature = "unstable-index")]`.
Test volume by area: `regression.rs` has 110 `rgtest!` cases, `misc.rs` 95, `feature.rs` 82, `binary.rs` 29, `json.rs` 9, `multiline.rs` 8 — regression tests are the single largest group.

`rgtest!` runs each test body twice when built with the `pcre2` feature — once via `util::setup` and once via `util::setup_pcre2` — which is why CI skips PCRE2 tests under cross/qemu to avoid doubling runtime.
`Dir::new` locates the `rg` binary relative to `env::current_exe()` and creates an isolated temp working directory keyed by a global atomic counter, so tests can create real files and symlinks.
`TestCommand::env` exists specifically so tests can exercise environment-driven behavior such as `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`.
Decompression is covered by committed fixture files: `tests/data/` contains `sherlock.{gz,bz2,xz,lz4,lzma,br,zst,Z}` matching the glob table in `default_decompression_commands`.
`cmd_exists` lets tests skip gracefully when an external decompression binary isn't installed on the runner, by probing `program --help`.

Index tests are split into `tests/index/basic.rs` (UX happy paths) and `tests/index/disallowed.rs`, the latter asserting that `-X` combined with `--files-without-match`, `--text` or `-Eutf16` errors out.
`crates/core/flags/defs.rs` carries 116 `#[test]` functions — largely `parse_low_raw([...])` assertions per flag — making the flag table the most densely unit-tested file in the repo.

Structural invariants of the flag table are enforced by tests: `shorts_no_duplicates`, `longs_no_duplicates`, `shorts_all_ascii_alphanumeric` and `longs_all_ascii_alphanumeric` (which also validates aliases and negations).
CI runs two informational tests with `--nocapture`: `flags::defs::tests::available_shorts` (prints unused short-flag letters) and grep-cli's `print_hostname`.
Shell completion correctness is tested outside cargo by the `ci/test-complete` script, which is skipped on Windows and on cross-compiled targets.
The CI matrix pins the MSRV build to Rust 1.96.0 and includes big-endian (s390x, powerpc64), 32-bit (i686, armv7) and Windows-on-ARM runners, so endianness and pointer-width bugs are caught.

Fuzzing is compile-checked only: the `fuzz_testing` CI job installs `cargo-fuzz` and runs `cargo check` in `fuzz/`; the sole target is `fuzz_glob` against the `globset` crate's `arbitrary` feature — the searcher and printer are not fuzzed.
Documentation is gated in CI: `cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace` runs with `RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings`, so a broken intra-doc link fails the build.

risk_map.summary: ripgrep has a small but real attack surface for a search tool: it executes external programs (decompressors, `--pre`, `--hostname-bin`), reads a config file from an environment-variable-named path whose contents become command-line flags, and memory-maps files it does not control. The codebase acknowledges most of these explicitly in comments — the mmap `unsafe` block calls its own reasoning "suspect", and `resolve_binary` exists specifically to stop Windows CWD-relative program resolution. The most fragile coupling is the 246KB `defs.rs` flag table, where a single flag touches parsing, help text, man page and four completion generators. The experimental index path is the least-finished area: `grep-index` opens with `#![allow(warnings)]`, its literal module is self-described as a prototype, and `index::read` doesn't actually use the index yet.

claims.claim: Arbitrary code execution is by design in three places — `--pre` (`Command::new(bin).arg(path)`), `-z` decompressors, and `--hostname-bin` — all spawned with the user's environment inherited.

`resolve_binary` is a deliberate Windows security mitigation: without it, `Command::new` hands relative paths to `CreateProcess`, which searches the CWD, so `rg -z` in an untrusted tree could run an attacker-planted `gzip.exe`. On non-Windows it is a no-op returning the path unchanged.

`RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` turns a file's contents into command-line arguments that are prepended to argv, so anything that can set that env var or write that file can inject flags including `--pre` — a full code-execution vector with no allowlist or validation.

The memory-map `unsafe` block carries an explicit hazard note: a file truncated concurrently with the search can raise SIGBUS and abort the process, and the author writes "This reasoning should be treated as suspect."

File IO is unbounded outside the repo root by nature — `walk_builder` starts at user-supplied paths with `follow_links(self.follow)` and `same_file_system(self.one_file_system)`, so `-L` on a hostile tree can be walked out of the intended subtree.
Index discovery reads `RIPGREP_INDEX_PATH` and otherwise walks every ancestor of the CWD looking for `.ripgrep`, a lookup the code itself flags as "subject to TOCTOU problems".
`crates/index/src/lib.rs` opens with `#![allow(warnings)]`, suppressing all compiler lints for the entire index crate — including dead code and unused results.

`crates/index/src/literal.rs` is self-described as "currently a prototype ... hastily written in order to bootstrap ngram extraction", so the ngram query construction (`GramQuery::And/Or/Literal`) is not production-hardened.
Indexed search is effectively dead weight today: `index::read` binds the opened index to `let _index` and runs a full exhaustive search anyway, so `-X` costs index-open time for zero pruning benefit.

`crates/core/flags/defs.rs` is 246KB — larger than the next two biggest files combined — and each flag must stay consistent across `Flag::update`, `doc_short`, `doc_long`, `doc_category` and `completion_type`, making it the highest blast-radius file for CLI changes.

`FlagValue::unwrap_switch`/`unwrap_value` panic via `unreachable!` on mismatch; this is intentional (a bug indicator) but means an `is_switch()`/`update()` inconsistency in a new flag is a runtime panic rather than a compile error.

Error reporting is global mutable state: three `AtomicBool`s (`MESSAGES`, `IGNORE_MESSAGES`, `ERRORED`) set once at startup and read at exit, so any code path that prints an error without going through `err_message!` silently fails to change the exit code.

`eprintln_locked!` calls `std::process::exit(0)`/`exit(2)` directly on write failure, bypassing destructors and any in-flight buffered output — an abrupt-termination path inside a macro used throughout the binary.

Sorting and parallelism are coupled by an assertion rather than the type system: `walk_builder` contains `assert_eq!(1, self.threads, "sorting implies single threaded")`, so a future change to the thread heuristic would panic at runtime.
The `FLAGS` slice order is load-bearing for generated documentation ("The order of these flags matter ... This is why the deprecated flags are last"), an invariant no test enforces.
`is_readable_stdin()` is documented as a heuristic with a "terrible failure mode": exec-process APIs that open an unused stdin pipe make `rg foo` appear to hang while it waits on stdin.

extension_points.summary: ripgrep's extension seams are almost all static tables and traits rather than runtime plugin systems. Adding a flag means adding one unit struct implementing `Flag` and one entry in the `FLAGS` slice; everything downstream (parser trie, `-h`, `--help`, man page, four shell completions) derives from that. Adding a file type means one line in `DEFAULT_TYPES`. Adding a decompressor means one `add(glob, ARGS, &mut cmds)` line. At the library level, `Matcher` and `Sink` are the two real trait-based extension points: any regex engine implementing `grep_matcher::Matcher` can be plugged into the searcher, and any output format implementing `grep_searcher::Sink` can consume results. The `ParallelVisitorBuilder` trait in `ignore` lets external callers drive the parallel walker with their own per-thread state.

claims.claim: The primary extension point is the `Flag` trait plus the `FLAGS: &[&dyn Flag]` slice; the module doc states the `defs` module "provides a single global slice of `&dyn Flag` values corresponding to all of the flags in ripgrep" used via dynamic dispatch.
One `Flag` impl can expose four user-visible names — short, long, `name_negated()` and an arbitrary `aliases()` list — as with `-E`/`--encoding`/`--no-encoding` sharing a single implementation.

`Category` (Input, Search, Filter, Output, OutputModes, Indexing, Logging, OtherBehaviors) is the grouping key for generated docs; `Category::as_str` returns the template variable name interpolated into help and man templates.
`CompletionType` (Other, Filename, Executable, Filetype, Encoding) is the hook a new flag uses to tell all four shell completion generators what to complete.

Four completion generators are registered in `flags::mod` as `generate_complete_bash/zsh/fish/powershell` and surfaced through `GenerateMode`; adding a shell means adding a module under `flags/complete/` and a `GenerateMode` variant.

`grep_searcher::Sink` is the output extension trait — implement `matched`, `context`, `context_break`, `binary_data`, `begin`, `finish` — and the crate ships a `sinks` submodule of closure-based conveniences (e.g. `UTF8`) for quick use.
`grep_matcher::Matcher` is the regex-engine extension trait; `grep-regex` and `grep-pcre2` are two implementations, and `PatternMatcher` in core is the enum that selects between them at runtime.

Printers are extended by adding a `Printer<W>` enum variant plus a `printer_*` builder in `HiArgs`; each variant only needs `get_mut()` and a `sink_with_path` method for `search_path`/`search_reader` to work.

New file types plug into `DEFAULT_TYPES`, a `&[(&[&str], &[&str])]` table of (names, globs) that the doc comment explicitly invites PRs against; users extend it per-invocation with `TypesBuilder::add`/`add_def`.

New decompressors plug into `default_decompression_commands()` via a single `add(glob, ARGS_X, &mut cmds)` call; unavailable binaries are silently skipped after `resolve_binary` fails with a debug log.
`ignore::ParallelVisitorBuilder` and `WalkParallel::visit` let external code supply per-thread visitors with owned state, as an alternative to the closure-based `run`.
`WalkBuilder::filter_entry` and `add_custom_ignore_filename` are the per-caller filtering hooks; ripgrep itself uses the latter to register `.rgignore`.
`HyperlinkFormat` implements `FromStr` with named aliases (`HyperlinkAlias`), so new editor URL schemes are added by extending the alias table rather than the printer.
`IndexDiscovery` is configurable rather than hard-wired: `env_name()`, `dir_name()`, `cwd()` and `create()` builders let embedders relocate the index away from `RIPGREP_INDEX_PATH`/`.ripgrep`.
The `grep` facade crate is the intended embedding point for third parties, re-exporting the whole stack under one dependency, with a worked `simplegrep` example.

agent_handoff.summary: Read `crates/core/main.rs`, `crates/core/flags/mod.rs` and `crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs` first — they define the whole control flow and the low→high argument split that every other decision hangs off. Formatting is enforced (`rustfmt.toml`: `max_width = 79`, `use_small_heuristics = "max"`, edition 2024) and CI fails on `cargo fmt --all --check`, so run rustfmt before proposing a diff. Most changes that touch the CLI require edits in three coordinated places: the `Flag` impl, the `FLAGS` slice, and the corresponding `LowArgs`/`HiArgs` fields. Note the repository's `AI_POLICY.md`: autonomous agents are explicitly barred from contributing upstream, and AI-written comments to maintainers may be hidden — treat this repo as read/analyze-friendly but do not open PRs or issues on it autonomously.

claims.claim: `AI_POLICY.md` states "Autonomous agents are not allowed to be used for contributing to this project" and that PRs appearing in violation will be closed, possibly without notice; `CONTRIBUTING.md` says contributions not following it will be closed.

Read first, in order: `crates/core/main.rs` (dispatch), `crates/core/flags/mod.rs` (the `Flag` trait and `Category`), `crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs` (`from_low_args` and every builder accessor), `crates/core/search.rs` (`SearchWorker`).

The core crate's own README warns it is not a library and is "glue code that brings the grep-matcher, grep-regex, grep-searcher and grep-printer crates together" — behavior changes usually belong in a `crates/*` library, not in core.
Formatting convention is strict and narrow: `max_width = 79`, `use_small_heuristics = "max"`, `edition = "2024"`; the `rustfmt` CI job runs `cargo fmt --all --check`.

Adding a flag requires: a unit struct implementing `Flag` (with `doc_long` in mdoc format), an entry in `FLAGS` at the right position for doc ordering, a field in `LowArgs`, and usually a matching field/accessor in `HiArgs`.

Per-flag tests use `parse_low_raw([...])`, a `#[cfg(test)]`-only helper that runs the parser once with no logging and no config file — the right tool for asserting flag parsing without touching the environment.
By convention `Flag::update` must only validate, never act: the trait docs use `--hostname-bin` as the example of work that must be deferred so it happens once, later.

Tests to run: `cargo test --all` for the full suite, `cargo test --features pcre2` to double-run integration tests under PCRE2, `cargo test --workspace --features unstable-index` for index tests, and `ci/test-complete` for zsh completions.

Integration tests create real files in a temp dir and run the built `rg` binary — they are not hermetic against the host, and `cmd_exists` gating means missing `gzip`/`xz` silently reduces coverage rather than failing.

Trap: `Flag::name_long` must be ≥2 ASCII alphanumeric/`-` characters and short flags must be unique ASCII alphanumeric or `.`; violating either fails `longs_all_ascii_alphanumeric`/`shorts_no_duplicates` rather than failing to compile.

Trap: changing thread-count derivation can trip `assert_eq!(1, self.threads, "sorting implies single threaded")` in `walk_builder`, because `--sort` and parallelism are mutually exclusive by construction.

Trap: in parallel mode the printer must not own the file separator — `printer_standard` only calls `separator_search` when `self.threads == 1`, because the `BufferWriter` owns separator logic otherwise.

Safe edit boundary: the `ignore`, `globset`, `grep-cli`, `grep-matcher`, `grep-printer`, `grep-regex` and `grep-searcher` crates are published to crates.io with independent versions and `#![deny(missing_docs)]`, so any new public item needs a doc comment or `cargo doc -D warnings` fails.

Release hygiene: `RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md` and the `#:version` marker comments next to each crate version are the mechanism for coordinated version bumps; the release workflow hard-fails if the git tag doesn't match `Cargo.toml`.
User-facing documentation that needs updating alongside behavior changes lives in `GUIDE.md` (usage guide), `FAQ.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` (90KB, maintained per release), not in generated help alone.

readmePreview: Ruff Docs | Playground An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust.

overview.summary: Ruff 0.16.8 is Astral's Rust monorepo for a Python linter/formatter and the ty type checker. The user-facing `ruff` binary lints and formats Python (and notebooks) from the CLI, a stdio language server, or WASM; `ty` type-checks projects with a Salsa database and an optional uv integration. The PyPI package is a thin launcher around the native binary, not a Python implementation of the linter.

system_map.summary: The Cargo workspace (edition 2024, rust-version 1.96, toolchain channel 1.98.0) builds two binaries, `ruff` and `ty`, plus libraries they share: the Python parser and AST, diagnostics, and workspace settings. Ruff's check and format paths are parallel file walks over hierarchical TOML config with an on-disk `.ruff_cache`. ty is a separate CLI and language server on a Salsa 0.28 `ProjectDatabase`, with typeshed vendored under `crates/ty_vendored`. Release artifacts are a scratch Docker image, cargo-dist installers, PyPI (maturin bin binding), WASM playgrounds, and crate publishes, all driven from GitHub Actions.

claims.claim: The workspace members are `crates/*`, package version 0.16.8, Rust edition 2024, minimum rust-version 1.96, license MIT, and the shared dependency set includes both `ruff_*` crates and `ty_*` crates plus salsa 0.28.2.
The developer toolchain pin is Rust 1.98.0 in rust-toolchain.toml, which the Dockerfile copies before `rustup target add` and `cargo zigbuild --bin ruff --release`.

`ruff` starts at `crates/ruff/src/main.rs`: it expands `@file` args with `argfile`, parses `Args` with clap, and calls `ruff::run`. Windows uses mimalloc; other supported arches use jemalloc. Broken-pipe errors exit 0; other failures print `ruff failed` and return `ExitStatus::Error` (code 2).

`ty` starts at `crates/ty/src/main.rs` and calls `ty::run`. `ty::run` sets up Rayon, expands `@file` arguments, and dispatches `Cli` to check, server, version, shell completion, or explain. Exit statuses are Success 0, Failure 1, Error 2, InternalError 101, and Interrupted 130.

PyPI packaging uses maturin with `bindings = "bin"`, `manifest-path = "crates/ruff/Cargo.toml"`, and `python-source = "python"`. `python/ruff/__main__.py` execs (or on Windows `subprocess.run`s) the native binary located by `find_ruff_bin`, which searches sysconfig script directories rather than embedding the linter in Python.

Shared front-end: `ruff_python_parser::parse` builds a `Parsed<Mod>` via `Parser::new`, and both the linter (`lint_only`) and the formatter (`format_module_source`) consume that parse. The linter crate documents its public API as completely unstable.

Ruff settings come from `ruff_workspace`. `project_files_in_path` normalizes paths, walks ancestors for `pyproject.toml` when hierarchical discovery is on, and walks the tree with the `ignore` crate's `WalkBuilder` (gitignore on, hidden files included, at most 12 threads).

Lint/format caches live in `.ruff_cache` (`ruff_cache::CACHE_DIR_NAME`). `Cache::open` stores one rkyv file per package at `cache_dir/VERSION/<settings key>` and drops entries if the package root does not match.

ty's persistent state is a Salsa `ProjectDatabase` created by `ProjectDatabase::fallible`. `check` and `check_with_reporter` delegate to `Project::check`. One-shot CLI checks call `disable_lru` and may `freeze` inputs; `run_check` then `mem::forget`s the database after optional `TY_MEMORY_REPORT` dumps.

Language servers are separate crates speaking stdio LSP: `ruff server` calls `ruff_server::run` (worker threads capped at 4); `ty server` calls `ty_server::run_server` with an `OsSystem` fallback and the same thread cap.

Release shape is cargo-dist 0.31.0 (`dist = false` on the workspace, local artifact jobs `./build-binaries`, `./build-docker`, `./build-wasm`; publish jobs PyPI, wasm, and crates). Installers are shell and PowerShell for a long target list, hosted at `https://releases.astral.sh/github/ruff/releases/download/{tag}`. The Docker image is `FROM scratch` with `ENTRYPOINT ["/ruff"]` and `WORKDIR /io`.

In-browser entry points are `ruff_wasm` (`Workspace::new` deserializes `Options` into `Settings`) and the npm workspaces `ruff`, `ty`, and `shared` under `playground/`, built with Vite, React, Tailwind, and wasm-pack. Sharing uses a Cloudflare Worker in `playground/api`.

feature_catalog.summary: Ruff's clap `Command` enum is the product surface: lint, format, an LSP server, rule and config help, cache cleaning, shell completions, and an import graph. The linter reimplements a large set of Flake8-family plugins as native rules under `ruff_linter::rules`, selected by code or category. ty exposes check (with fix and ignore insertion), a language server, and `explain rule`. Both tools have WASM playgrounds; Ruff also formats notebooks and can watch the filesystem.

claims.claim: `ruff check` (`CheckCommand`) accepts paths or `-` for stdin, `--fix` / `--fix-only` / `--diff` / `--unsafe-fixes`, `--watch`, `--ignore-noqa`, `--add-noqa` and `--add-ignore`, `--select` / rule selectors, `--target-version`, `--preview`, and `--output-format` from `RUFF_OUTPUT_FORMAT` plus `--output-file` from `RUFF_OUTPUT_FILE`. `--show-settings` and `--show-files` short-circuit before linting.

Default fix behavior generates fixes but does not write them. `--diff` selects `FixMode::Diff`; `--fix` or `--fix-only` selects `FixMode::Apply`; otherwise `FixMode::Generate`. Applicability stays automatic unless `--unsafe-fixes` is set. `--add-noqa` / `--add-ignore` refuse newlines in the reason and are incompatible with `--fix`.

`ruff format` (`FormatCommand`) writes files by default. `--diff` selects `FormatMode::Diff` and `--check` selects `FormatMode::Check`. `--range` is rejected when the resolved path set contains more than one file. Stdin is handled by `commands::format_stdin::format_stdin` instead of `commands::format::format`.

Formatting itself is `format_module_source`: parse with `ParseOptions` from the source type, build `TriviaRanges`, `format_module_ast`, then `print`. Parse, format, and print failures become `FormatModuleError` and map to `DiagnosticId::InternalError`.

`ruff server` is the editor integration. Request handlers registered in `ruff_server` are code action, code-action resolve, document diagnostic, execute command, format, format range, hover, and shutdown. Notifications include didOpen/didChange/didClose for text documents and notebooks, configuration, watched files, and workspace changes. Code-action kinds include `source.fixAll.ruff` and `source.organizeImports.ruff` (plus notebook variants).

Other Ruff subcommands: `rule` (one rule or `--all`), `config` (one option or the catalog), `linter` (upstream linter list), `clean`, hidden `generate-shell-completion`, `version`, and `analyze graph` (`AnalyzeGraphCommand`: direction, string-import detection, `--python` venv, type-checking imports, preview, target version).

Native lint plugins are the `Linter` enum in `registry.rs` (prefixes such as AIR, E/W via pycodestyle, F, S, B, I, UP, PL, RUF) and matching modules under `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/` (`airflow` through `tryceratops`, including `pyflakes`, `pylint`, `pyupgrade`, `isort`, `flake8_bugbear`, `ruff`). `code_to_rule` is the `#[ruff_macros::map_codes]` table that maps `(Linter, code)` to a rule struct.

`ty` subcommands are `check`, `server`, `version`, hidden `generate-shell-completion`, and `explain rule`. `ty check` takes paths, `--project`, `--config-file`, `--fix`, `--add-ignore`, `--watch`, `--exit-zero`, color, verbosity, and progress flags. Fix mode is `FixMode::ApplyFixes` or `FixMode::AddIgnore`; plain runs are `MainLoopMode::Check`.

ty diagnostics come from `ty_python_semantic::check_file`: I/O errors, parse errors, unsupported-syntax errors (with an inferred-version hint), then `check_types`. Lints are `LintMetadata` values created with `declare_lint!` (kebab-case name, summary, docs, default `Level` of ignore/warn/error, status) and stored in `default_lint_registry`.

The Ruff WASM API exposes `Workspace` with `version`, a constructor from JS `Options`, and `defaultSettings`. The playground README describes two SPAs (Ruff at play.ruff.rs and a ty playground) using Monaco, Vite, and localStorage, plus a Worker KV share store.

Notebooks are first-class inputs: watch mode treats `.py`, `.pyi`, `.pyw`, and `.ipynb` as source and `.toml` as configuration, and `lint_path` lints `pyproject.toml` / `ruff.toml` when a TOML rule is enabled via `lint_fix_toml` / `lint_toml`.

`cargo dev` (`crates/ruff_dev`) is the maintainer CLI: `generate-all`, JSON schemas, rules tables, options docs, ty CLI/env/schema docs, `print-ast` / `print-cst` / `print-tokens`, formatter stability (`format-dev`), and `repeat` for profiling `ruff check`.

data_flow.summary: Ruff and ty both start from OS arguments and project files, never from a network service in the CLI. Ruff turns paths into per-file source text, a parse, noqa/suppression directives, and diagnostics, then either prints them, writes fixes, or stores a negative cache entry. ty loads project metadata into a Salsa database, type-checks files in parallel, and optionally rewrites source. The only intentional subprocess is uv, and only when `TY_UV` enables it. The playground is the network boundary: the browser runs WASM locally and optionally POSTs source to Workers KV.

claims.claim: Input boundary for both CLIs is `wild::args_os` expanded by `argfile::expand_args_from` (prefix `@`) before clap parsing. Ruff also honors `FORCE_COLOR` via `colored_override` and `RUFF_OUTPUT_FORMAT` / `RUFF_OUTPUT_FILE`.

`ruff check` calls `resolve::resolve` for the root config, then `project_files_in_path`. Enabled rules decide whether `.py` and pyproject/ruff TOML files stay in the set. Package roots come from `resolver.package_roots`, and per-file `LinterSettings` come from `resolver.resolve(path)`.

Per-file lint transform in `diagnostics::lint_path`: cache lookup by relative path plus `FileCacheKey` (mtime and permission mode); on miss, `SourceKind::from_path`; then `lint_fix` (apply or diff) or `lint_only`. `lint_only` parses, builds `Locator`, `Stylist`, and `Indexer`, extracts noqa directives and `Suppressions`, and calls `check_path`.

`check_path` is phased: token rules, filesystem rules, logical-line rules, then (only if the parse is valid) `check_ast` plus import sorting and docstring line collection, then physical-line rules. AST checking is `checkers::ast::check_ast`. Diagnostics are sorted with `Diagnostic::ruff_start_ordering` before return.

Output boundary for a check: `Printer` writes violations to stdout, or to `RUFF_OUTPUT_FILE` (parent directories created, color forced off) unless `--watch`. `--fix` writes transformed source with `File::create`; `--diff` writes a unified diff to stdout. Watch mode uses `notify::recommended_watcher` and re-resolves config when a `.toml` changes.

Cache write path: after the parallel fold, `caches.persist()` runs `Cache::persist`, which rkyv-serializes `PackageCache` to a temp file in the cache directory and renames it into place. Windows `PermissionDenied` on that rename is warned, not failed. A cache hit with noqa enabled returns empty diagnostics and skips re-lint.

ty input flow: cwd from `current_directory`, optional `--project` directory, absolute check paths, `OsSystem`, and `UseUv::from_system`. Metadata is `ProjectMetadata::from_config_file` or `discover_with_uv`, then `apply_configuration_files` and `set_override_options`. A single PEP 723 script file forces `UseUv::Scripts` even when uv is otherwise on.

ty check execution: `MainLoop::main_loop` synchronizes script environments, then on `CheckWorkspace` clones the database and Rayon-spawns `db.check_with_reporter`. `Project::check` reports settings and file-set diagnostics, then `into_par_iter` calls salsa `check_file_impl`, which calls `ty_python_semantic::check_file` unless script settings are invalid. Results are discarded if the revision moved.

ty fix output: `FixMode::ApplyFixes` calls `fix_all_diagnostics` with `Applicability::Safe` only; `FixMode::AddIgnore` calls `suppress_all_diagnostics`. `--exit-zero` forces `ExitStatus::Success` after a non-internal result. `TY_MEMORY_REPORT=short|full|json` dumps Salsa memory on the summary stream.

When uv is enabled, `Uv::execute` runs `Command::new(executable)` with args `workspace metadata --quiet`. Workspace targets add `--active`; script targets add `--sync --script <path>` and optional `--python`. The executable is `UV` if set, otherwise `system.which("uv")`.

Playground data flow: the SPA keeps editor state in localStorage and runs Ruff or ty as WASM. Share URLs hit the Worker: GET `/{id}` reads Workers KV namespace `PLAYGROUND`; POST reads the raw body, stores it under `crypto.randomUUID()`, and returns the id. Production CORS allows `https://play.ruff.rs` plus `playknot.ruff.rs`, `types.ruff.rs`, and `play.ty.dev`.

behavior_traces.summary: Three user-visible pipelines dominate: process startup for each binary, `ruff check` from arguments to printed diagnostics and cache, and `ty check` from project discovery through a cancellable Salsa main loop. Format and the Ruff language server are the same file pipeline entered from different adapters. Watch modes re-enter those pipelines on filesystem events instead of exiting.

claims.claim: Ruff startup order: `main` enables Windows virtual terminal, expands args, `Args::parse_from`, `run`. `run` applies color, `ruff_db::set_program_version`, installs a panic hook that points at the GitHub issue URL, skips logging for `Command::Server`, then matches `Command` to `check`, `format`, `server`, `analyze_graph`, or the help commands.

`ruff check` order: `CheckCommand::partition` -> `resolve::resolve` -> optional `show_settings` / `show_files` -> compute `FixMode` -> if suppression flags, `commands::add_noqa::add_noqa` and return -> else build `Printer` -> if `--watch`, `recommended_watcher` and an initial `commands::check::check` -> otherwise the same `check` once.

`commands::check::check` order: `project_files_in_path` -> retain Python and ruff/pyproject TOML -> `package_roots` -> `PackageCacheMap::init` if cache enabled -> `paths.par_iter` calling `lint_path` -> `catch_unwind` around `diagnostics::lint_path` -> fold/reduce diagnostics -> `sort_by(Diagnostic::ruff_start_ordering)` -> `caches.persist`. A panic becomes `create_panic_diagnostic` instead of aborting the process.

`diagnostics::lint_path` order for Python: `FileCacheKey::from_path` and `cache.get` -> `settings.extension.get_source_type` -> `SourceKind::from_path` -> `lint_fix` or `lint_only` -> on `FixMode::Apply`, `transformed.write` to `File::create(path)`; on `Diff`, write `source_kind.diff` to stdout. TOML files branch earlier into `lint_fix_toml` / `lint_toml`.

`lint_only` order: `settings.resolve_target_version` -> `ParseSource::into_parsed` -> `Locator::new` -> `Stylist::from_tokens` -> `Indexer::from_tokens` -> `directives::extract_directives` -> `Suppressions::from_tokens` -> `check_path`. `lint_fix` repeats that loop up to 100 iterations, tracking `FixTable`.

`ruff format` order: `FormatCommand::partition` -> `resolve::resolve` -> `resolve_default_files` -> `project_files_in_path` -> `package_roots` -> optional `PackageCacheMap::init` -> parallel per-path format. Each file reaches `format_module_source` -> `parse` -> `format_module_ast` -> `Printed`.

ty startup and check order: `main` -> `run` -> `setup_rayon` -> `Cli::parse_from` -> `run_check` -> `setup_tracing` -> resolve cwd/project/paths -> `UseUv::from_system` -> `ProjectMetadata::{from_config_file|discover_with_uv}` -> `ProjectDatabase::fallible` -> `MainLoop::new` -> `ctrlc::set_handler` -> `watch` or `run`.

ty main-loop order: `synchronize_scripts` -> `request_check` -> biased select on uv sync wakeups, watcher messages, and check requests. `CheckWorkspace` defers while `has_pending_synchronizations`, else spawns `check_with_reporter` + `into_sorted_diagnostics`. `CheckCompleted` either `write_diagnostics` or `fix_all_diagnostics` / `suppress_all_diagnostics`. Ctrl+C calls `CancellationTokenSource::stop`.

Per-file ty order inside `check_file_impl`: if the file is a script without valid settings, return script settings diagnostics; else `ty_python_semantic::check_file`; then append script settings diagnostics and a dependency-metadata diagnostic. `check_file` itself loads `source_text`, returns `IOErrorDiagnostic` on read error, extends parse and unsupported-syntax diagnostics, extends `check_types`, and sorts by `rendering_sort_key`.

Ruff LSP diagnostic order: `publish_diagnostics_for_document` calls `generate_diagnostics`, which no-ops unless `client_settings().lint()`, otherwise `crate::lint::check` on the document snapshot, then `Client::send_notification` of `PublishDiagnosticsNotification` per URI with the document version. Server boot is `ConnectionInitializer::stdio` then `Server::new(...).run` and `io_threads.join`.

Cache persistence order on a dirty cache: `Cache::persist` -> `save` merges changes -> `tempfile_in(parent)` -> `rkyv::to_bytes` of `PackageCache` -> `write_all` -> `NamedTempFile::persist`. No-change caches return before opening a temp file.

testing_signals.summary: Tests are Rust-native: cargo-nextest in CI, insta snapshots, and ty Markdown fixtures executed by `datatest-stable`. Parser, linter, and formatter crates carry large snapshot and fixture trees; the Ruff CLI has integration tests under `crates/ruff/tests`. CI path-filters which jobs run, and additionally dogfoods `ty check` on in-repo Python. Fuzz targets cover parse, fix, and format idempotency. Playground Worker code and file-watching tests are the obvious gaps.

claims.claim: Linux CI job `cargo test (linux)` runs `uv run --locked --only-dev cargo insta test --all-features --unreferenced reject --test-runner nextest --disable-nextest-doctest`, then `cargo test --doc --all-features`. It is skipped when the PR has label `no-test` or `determine_changes` says no code changed (except on main).

The same job dogfoods ty: `cargo run -p ty check` on `python/py-fuzzer`, `scripts/ty_benchmark`, and `scripts/*.py` (the last with `TY_UV=scripts` and `UV_LOCKED=true`). A prior step runs `cargo test -p ty_python_semantic --test mdtest` with `MDTEST_GITHUB_ANNOTATIONS_FORMAT=1` and ignores its exit code so annotations cannot fail the job.

CI also runs `cargo fmt`, `shellcheck`, `cargo clippy` (including a wasm clippy job), `cargo hawk` at HAWK_VERSION 0.1.13, and a `cargo publish` dry-run. `determine_changes` sets outputs `parser`, `linter`, `formatter`, `ty`, `playground`, `fuzz`, `py-fuzzer`, `benchmarks`, and `release` from path filters. Workflow permissions are `contents: read`.

ty semantic tests are Markdown files. `crates/ty_python_semantic/tests/mdtest.rs` registers `mdtest` and `lint_doc` via datatest-stable; each fixture runs on a one-thread Rayon pool. `lint_doc` looks the filename stem up in `default_lint_registry` and passes it as `default_error_rule`. Fixtures live under `./resources/mdtest` and `./resources/lint_docs`.

Ruff CLI coverage includes `crates/ruff/tests` (integration and CLI snapshot tests) and a unit test `unreadable_files` in `commands/check.rs` that creates mode-0o000 files and snapshots E902 / invalid-pyproject diagnostics with insta. Rule crates keep insta snapshots beside rules (for example `rules/pyflakes` and `rules/pylint`).

Parser tests are fixture-driven: `crates/ruff_python_parser/resources` holds hundreds of `.py` fixtures and `crates/ruff_python_parser/tests` holds matching snapshots. Formatter tests similarly pair `resources/test` fixtures with `tests` snapshots. The parser fuzz target `ruff_parse_simple` and idempotency target `ruff_parse_idempotency` sit outside the workspace.

Fuzz package `ruff-fuzz` (separate `[workspace]`, cargo-fuzz, libfuzzer-sys) builds bins `ty_check_invalid_syntax`, `ruff_parse_simple`, `ruff_fix_validity`, `ruff_formatter_validity`, `ruff_parse_idempotency`, and `ruff_formatter_idempotency`. It depends on the linter, parser, formatter, and ty semantic crates with the semantic `testing` feature.

AGENTS.md requires `INSTA_FORCE_PASS=1 INSTA_UPDATE=always MDTEST_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo nextest run` (or `cargo test` if nextest is missing), forbids hand-editing snapshot bodies, and says file-watcher tests do not work in the sandbox. Clippy gate is `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.

`pyproject.toml` defines a `ruff-lsp-test` dependency group (pytest, pygls 1.x, lsprotocol) separate from the Rust LSP crates, and a `ty-ecosystem` group on `ecosystem-analyzer`. Those are integration/ecosystem harnesses, not the in-crate nextest suites.

The playground Worker (`playground/api/src/index.ts`) has no test module beside it, and `playground/package.json` scripts are `dev:wasm`, oxlint, `tsc`, and prettier rather than a behavioral test runner. WASM API tests exist as `crates/ruff_wasm/tests/api.rs` and `crates/ty_wasm/tests/api.rs`, which is a different layer.
An ignored `linter_quick_test` in `ruff_linter` is an ad-hoc debug entry point (`#[ignore]`) that runs one rule through `test_contents`. It is not part of normal CI coverage.

risk_map.summary: The repository's own threat model treats project source and config as attacker-controlled and forbids analysis from executing that code. The sharp edges that do cross a process or network boundary are ty's uv subprocess, fix/format writes, cache files, stdio LSP, and the unauthenticated playground share API. Internally, the rule table in `codes.rs`, Salsa cancellation, and the unstable linter API are the maintenance blast radii.

claims.claim: The CLI threat model states analysis must not execute user-supplied code; `--isolated` must ignore config files; reading files reached via imports, config extensions, or symlinks is expected; fixes, format, ignore insertion, and cache cleanup may change only the operation's selected targets; `ruff format --check` must not write source.

ty's uv integration is off unless `TY_UV` is `1`, `true` (`UseUv::On`), or `scripts` (`UseUv::Scripts`). When on, `Uv::execute` runs the `UV` env var or `PATH`'s `uv`. Script metadata uses `workspace metadata --sync --script`, which the threat model says may install dependencies.

`--fix` and format `Write` mode replace file contents via `File::create` and a full write of the transformed source. A failed fix falls back to `lint_only` on the original. `--add-noqa` also rewrites files. These are the intentional mutation paths.

Cache files are written outside the source tree only in the sense that `.ruff_cache` (or `cache-dir`) sits in the project and is excluded from linting by default. Persistence is atomic rename, but a mismatched package root silently clears `package.files`, and unreadable cache files are replaced with an empty cache after a warning.

The playground share Worker stores the entire POST body in KV with a random UUID and no authentication, size check, or content-type check in `fetch`. GET returns the stored text to any caller who has the id. Production CORS is an allowlist, not an auth scheme. Dev mode sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

Both language servers read editor documents over stdio and trust the client connection. Ruff publishes diagnostics from in-memory snapshots (`snapshot.query()`), so a hostile document is linted with the server's filesystem rights. ty's server additionally requires a Unicode cwd and keeps an `OsSystem` fallback for files not in the index.

Python launcher risk is local binary lookup: `find_ruff_bin` returns the first `ruff` executable on a fixed list of script directories and `__main__` `execvp`s it. A planted binary earlier in that search list would run with the user's privileges. On Windows the launcher uses `subprocess.run` and maps `KeyboardInterrupt` to exit 2.

Lint panics are isolated per file with `catch_unwind` and reported as diagnostics, but `Cache::open` and the Windows color setup still use `unwrap`/`assert` on paths that are not panic-isolated (`SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.elapsed().unwrap()`, `set_virtual_terminal` assert). ty's check thread uses `salsa::Cancelled::catch` and drops stale revisions.

`codes.rs` `code_to_rule` is a single macro-expanded match from every rule code to a rule type. A new rule that is not added there is unreachable from `--select` and noqa codes. `Rule::from_code` searches `Linter::all_rules` by noqa suffix.

ty one-shot checks `freeze` the database and then `std::mem::forget(db)` so destructors do not run. `system_mut` documents that it cancels other handles and can deadlock if the refcount is not 1. Watch mode, fix modes, and memory reports must not freeze.

The linter library is explicitly unstable. WASM, the CLI, and the language server all call into `check_path` / settings types, so a signature change in `ruff_linter` fans out across `crates/ruff`, `ruff_server`, and `ruff_wasm`.

Docker build fetches rustup with `curl | sh` and compiles a musl binary. That is a release-supply-chain path, not a runtime path for users of the scratch image. cargo-dist comments that CI customizes cargo-dist install specifically to avoid `curl | sh` for the dist tool itself.

Debug Ruff builds warn when the cache is left on, because `--no-cache` is what developers expect while iterating. Shipping a debug binary to users would both warn and serve potentially stale-looking cache behavior relative to source edits.

extension_points.summary: New Ruff rules plug into a plugin module, the `Linter` enum, and the `code_to_rule` table, usually scaffolded by `scripts/add_rule.py`. New ty lints plug into `declare_lint!` plus `LintRegistryBuilder::register_lint`. User-facing commands, LSP methods, TOML options, and WASM settings are each a closed table that must be updated and then regenerated into docs and JSON schema. Checker phases and `FormatNodeRule` are the extension points inside an existing rule or syntax node.

claims.claim: `scripts/add_rule.py` scaffolds a rule (`--name`, `--prefix`, `--code`, `--linter`, `--category`). The implementation then lives under `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/<plugin>/` and must be referenced from `code_to_rule` in `codes.rs`. Plugin modules are declared in `rules/mod.rs`.

`Linter` is a `RuleNamespace` enum. `#[derive(RuleNamespace)]` in `ruff_macros` generates the prefix and rule-iteration impls. `Rule::from_code` parses a code into that namespace and matches the noqa suffix.

Rule structs use `#[derive(ViolationMetadata)]` (`ruff_macros::derive_violation_metadata`). `Violation` and `AlwaysFixableViolation` are the public traits re-exported from `ruff_linter`. Test-only rules are compiled in under `feature = "test-rules"` inside `check_path`.

ty lints are not in the Ruff `Rule` enum. `declare_lint!` builds a `LintMetadata` static; `register_lints` in `ty_python_semantic` calls `types::register_lints` and then registers ignore-comment lints. `LintRegistryBuilder::register_lint` panics on a duplicate name. Aliases go through `register_alias`.

CLI extension is the clap `Command` enum in `crates/ruff/src/args.rs` and the match in `ruff::run`. ty's parallel table is `crates/ty/src/args.rs` `Command` and the match in `ty::run`. Hidden shell-completion variants call `clap_complete_command`.

Ruff LSP methods are one module per request under `server/api/requests/` and one per notification under `server/api/notifications/`, re-exported from `requests.rs` and `notifications.rs`. Adding a method means a new handler type plus registration in those modules, not a dynamic plugin loader.

Configuration options use `#[derive(OptionsMetadata)]` and `CombineOptions` from `ruff_macros`. `ruff config` prints that metadata. `cargo dev generate-all` / `generate-json-schema` / `generate-options` / `generate-ty-schema` regenerate `ruff.schema.json`, `ty.schema.json`, and docs. CLI overrides arrive as `ConfigurationTransformer` implementations passed into `resolve_root_settings`.

Lint passes are selected by `rule.lint_source()` inside `check_path`: tokens, filesystem, logical lines, AST, imports, physical lines, and TOML. A rule that needs a new pass has to extend that match of sources, not only the rule body. AST work enters through `check_ast`.

Formatter node coverage is the `FormatNodeRule<N>` trait (`fmt` handles comments and source-map positions; `fmt_fields` is implemented per node). `format_module_ast` is the stable entry for callers that already have a `Parsed<Mod>`.

WASM settings are whatever `Options` / `Configuration::from_options` accepts. `Workspace::new` is the JS constructor; `defaultSettings` re-serializes defaults including `DEFAULT_SELECTORS`. There is no runtime plugin registry in the WASM crate.

File discovery can be customized per invocation by implementing `ConfigurationTransformer` and passing it to `project_files_in_path` / `resolve_scoped_settings`. The CLI's `ConfigArguments` is that transformer for `--config` key/value overrides and `--isolated`.

agent_handoff.summary: Read the CLI dispatch and the crate you are changing before editing; Ruff and ty share a parser but not a rule registry. Semantic changes need a focused test, snapshot updates via the environment variables rather than hand edits, and `cargo dev generate-all` when options, rules, or CLI help change. ty code must keep `db` in the Salsa parameter position and must not touch another file's AST from an untracked query. Do not drop Python repros inside this checkout, and do not expect file-watcher tests to pass in a sandbox.

claims.claim: Start with `AGENTS.md` (test commands, mdtest style, Salsa rules, `db` parameter order, prek) and `crates/ruff/src/lib.rs` plus `args.rs` for Ruff CLI work, or `crates/ty/src/lib.rs` for ty CLI work. Rule work starts at `codes.rs` `code_to_rule` and the plugin module; ty lint work starts at `declare_lint!` and `register_lints`.

Safe Ruff lint edit: add or change a rule under `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/<plugin>/`, register it in `code_to_rule`, add a fixture and insta snapshot, and leave unrelated plugins alone. The public `ruff_linter` API is documented as unstable, so do not churn signatures to make a single rule compile.

Tests to run for a linter change: `cargo nextest run -p ruff_linter` (or the narrower test binary) with `INSTA_FORCE_PASS=1 INSTA_UPDATE=always MDTEST_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, then review snapshot diffs. For ty semantic changes, run `cargo nextest run -p ty_python_semantic --test mdtest`. Full CI uses `cargo insta test --all-features --unreferenced reject --test-runner nextest`.

Never edit `.snap` files or inline snapshot bodies by hand. After option, CLI, rule, or environment-variable definition changes, run `cargo dev generate-all` so `ruff.schema.json`, `ty.schema.json`, and generated docs stay aligned. Finish with `uv run --only-dev --locked prek run --files <each changed path>`.

ty parameter convention: `db` is the first argument of free functions and comes immediately after `self` on methods. Methods that read `.node()` should be `#[salsa::tracked]`. `check_file_impl` is already a tracked query; do not call raw AST helpers from module A while checking module B.

Ad-hoc Python repros must be created outside the checkout. The root `pyproject.toml` sets `requires-python = ">=3.7"` and `tool.ruff.target-version = "py38"`, so ty discovered from this tree infers an old Python version. ty preview for 3.15 is still warned unless preview is enabled.

Do not use `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `unwrap`, or `expect` for conditions the type system can encode. Existing exceptions include the Windows VT assert in `main` and cache timestamp truncation; do not add more. Lint-path failures should become diagnostics the way `catch_unwind` already does.
ty PR titles should start with `[ty]`. LSP-only changes use the `server` label when you can set labels. Avoid competing with an open PR; `CONTRIBUTING.md` is the duplicate-work check.

File-watcher tests do not work in the sandbox. Ruff watch mode is `recommended_watcher` in `ruff::check`; ty watch mode is `watch::directory_watcher` plus `ProjectWatcher`. Skip those locally unless the change is specifically about watching.

Cache keys include the crate version string, so behavior changes that should invalidate user caches need a version bump or an explicit settings-key change. Do not hand-delete logic that compares `package.package_root` or the atomic rename; both exist because of real corruption bugs.

Formatter and parser changes have their own fixture trees and fuzz targets (`ruff_formatter_idempotency`, `ruff_parse_idempotency`). A parser change that still snap-passes can fail idempotency fuzz; run the crate tests, not only a single rule snapshot.

Security-sensitive edits (subprocess, LSP trust, playground KV, cache paths, fix application) should be checked against `agents/references/cli-threat-model.md`, `language-server-threat-model.md`, `playground-threat-model.md`, or `repository-threat-model.md` as appropriate. uv must stay default-off.
