qaReadiness.summary: Repo has some Synthetic QA building blocks, but CodeVetter should ask for the missing runner/script/spec pieces before claiming runtime coverage.

readmePreview: A utility-first CSS framework for rapidly building custom user interfaces.

overview.summary: This is the Tailwind CSS v4 monorepo: a CSS-first utility framework whose compiler is a TypeScript AST pipeline (`packages/tailwindcss`) paired with a Rust candidate scanner compiled to a NAPI/WASM native addon (`crates/oxide` → `@tailwindcss/oxide`). Configuration moved out of `tailwind.config.js` and into CSS at-rules — `@theme`, `@utility`, `@custom-variant`, `@source`, `@plugin`, `@config`, `@apply` — with a dedicated `compat/` layer that replays legacy v3 JS configs and plugins onto the new design system. It ships as a fan of thin integration packages (CLI, PostCSS, Vite, webpack, Turbopack, browser CDN build, Bun-compiled standalone binary) that all wrap the same `compile()` + `Scanner` pair, plus an AST-driven `@tailwindcss/upgrade` codemod tool for v3→v4 migration. It targets web developers and build-tool authors; what's distinctive is the split-language architecture and the aggressive incremental-rebuild caching that appears in every integration.

system_map.summary: The repo is a pnpm workspace (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`) orchestrated by Turborepo (`turbo.json`) layered over a Cargo workspace (`Cargo.toml`, `members = ["crates/*"]`). The compiler core lives in `packages/tailwindcss` and is pure TypeScript with no filesystem access — all IO is injected via `loadModule`/`loadStylesheet` callbacks. `@tailwindcss/node` is the Node IO adapter (enhanced-resolve + jiti + Lightning CSS), and `@tailwindcss/oxide` is the Rust scanner bridged through napi-rs. Six consumer packages (cli, postcss, vite, webpack, turbopack, browser, standalone) sit on top, and `@tailwindcss/upgrade` is a separate codemod CLI. There is no server or database; the storage layer is the filesystem plus in-memory LRU caches.

claims.claim: `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.ts` exports the three public compiler entrypoints — `compile(css, opts)` (string→string), `compileAst(ast, opts)` (AST→AST, used by the PostCSS plugin), and `__unstable__loadDesignSystem` (used by IntelliSense and the upgrade tool) — plus a default export that throws a hard error if someone wires `tailwindcss` directly into PostCSS.

The core compiler takes zero filesystem dependencies: `CompileOptions` declares `loadModule` and `loadStylesheet` callbacks that default to `throwOnLoadModule`/`throwOnLoadStylesheet`, which is what makes the same code run in Node, Bun, and the browser CDN build.

`@tailwindcss/node` is the Node runtime boundary: it wires `enhanced-resolve` resolvers (separate `cssResolver` with `mainFields: ['style']`, `esmResolver`, and `cjsResolver` fallback), `jiti` for `.ts` plugin/config files, and `Module.registerHooks({ resolve: resolveSync })` so ESM config reloads work in watch mode.

`crates/node/src/lib.rs` is the napi-rs bridge exposing the `Scanner` class (`scan()`, `scanFiles()`, `getCandidatesWithPositions()`, and `files`/`scannedFiles`/`globs`/`normalizedSources` getters) plus the `ChangedContent`, `GlobEntry`, and `SourceEntry` object shapes consumed by every JS integration.

The Cargo workspace has four crates: `tailwindcss-oxide` (the scanner/extractor), `tailwind-oxide` (`crates/node`, the NAPI shim), `classification-macros` (a `ClassifyBytes` proc-macro deriving byte-class lookup tables for the extractor state machines), and a vendored fork of BurntSushi's `ignore` crate pinned to edition 2024.

Build is `pnpm build` → `turbo build --filter=!./playgrounds/*`, followed by a `postbuild` hook that runs `scripts/pack-packages.mjs` to `pnpm pack` every non-private workspace into `dist/*.tgz` — the integration tests then install those tarballs.

Test commands are split three ways: `pnpm test` runs `cargo test && vitest run`, `pnpm test:integrations` runs `vitest --root=./integrations`, and `pnpm test:ui` runs Playwright in both `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/browser`.

`turbo.json` gives `@tailwindcss/oxide#build` explicit `inputs` covering `../oxide/src/**/*` and `../Cargo.toml`, so touching Rust source correctly busts the Turbo cache for the native addon; it also passes `RUSTUP_HOME` through via `globalPassThroughEnv`.

Deployment shape is npm publishing with provenance: `@tailwindcss/oxide` fans out into 12 platform-specific optionalDependencies (`napi.targets` includes `wasm32-wasip1-threads`), and `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds each target in a matrix then publishes with `id-token: write` for npm trusted publishing.

`@tailwindcss/standalone` is built by Bun (`bun ./scripts/build.ts`) into seven single-file executables (linux/macos/windows × arm64/x64, glibc and musl), each SHA-256 checksummed; it is marked `private: true` so `pack-packages.mjs` skips it.

Lightning CSS is the only output post-processor: `optimize()` in `@tailwindcss/node` runs `transform()` twice (so nesting-flattened adjacent rules get merged), pins browser targets to Safari/iOS 16.4, Firefox 128, Chrome 111, and uses `errorRecovery: true` with a warning filter for framework pseudo-classes like `::ng-deep` and `::v-deep`.
pnpm patches three dependencies — `@napi-rs/cli`, `@parcel/watcher`, and `lightningcss` — specifically so Bun can statically analyze them when compiling the standalone binary.

`playgrounds/` holds three manual smoke-test apps (vite + React, nextjs, v3) wired via root scripts `pnpm vite` and `pnpm nextjs`; the Vite one is a two-line config registering `@tailwindcss/vite` alongside `@vitejs/plugin-react`.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface is (a) the CSS authoring language — a set of at-rules parsed in `parseCss`, (b) the `tailwindcss` CLI with `build` and `canonicalize` subcommands, (c) five build-tool integrations, (d) a zero-build browser CDN script, and (e) the `@tailwindcss/upgrade` migration CLI. The compat layer additionally re-exposes the entire v3 JS plugin API (`addUtilities`, `matchVariant`, `theme()`, etc.) so existing plugins keep working. IntelliSense-facing APIs (`getClassList`, `getVariants`, `canonicalizeCandidates`) are first-class exports of the design system rather than an afterthought.

claims.claim: The CSS at-rule vocabulary handled in `parseCss` is `@tailwind utilities`, `@utility`, `@source` (with `not`, `inline(…)`, and brace-expansion via `expand()`), `@variant`, `@custom-variant`, `@theme` (with `reference`/`inline`/`default`/`static`/`prefix(…)` options), `@apply`, `@import`, `@plugin`, and `@config`.

`@import "tailwindcss" theme(reference)`, `prefix(ident)`, `important`, and `source(…)` are implemented by rewriting the `@media` node that `postcss-import`-style resolution produces — `@media theme(reference)` is transformed into a `context({ reference: true })` wrapper rather than being a distinct parser path.
The `tailwindcss` CLI exposes `build` (default when no subcommand is given) and `canonicalize`, with root-level `--help` dispatch in `run()` that also errors on unknown non-flag commands.

`tailwindcss build` supports `--input/-i` (including `-` for stdin), `--output/-o`, `--watch[=always]`, `--poll[=ms]`, `--minify/-m`, `--optimize`, `--cwd`, `--map`, and `--silent`; when no `--input` is given it defaults to compiling `@import 'tailwindcss';`.

`tailwindcss canonicalize` rewrites candidate lists to their canonical form, reading from argv or stdin, with `--css` to point at a design-system entry, `--format text|json|jsonl`, and `--stream` for line-by-line stdin processing — aimed at tooling like Prettier plugins and linters.

`@tailwindcss/vite` ships as an array of three Vite plugins — `@tailwindcss/vite:scan` (config capture), `:generate:serve` (dev), and `:generate:build` (production, which additionally runs `optimize()`) — each with `transform.filter` id include/exclude regexes that skip `?raw`, `?url`, `?worker`, and CommonJS proxy requests.

`@tailwindcss/postcss` accepts `base`, `optimize` (defaults to `NODE_ENV === 'production'`), and `transformAssetUrls`, and bundles a `fixRelativePathsPlugin()` that repairs paths when `postcss-import` ran before it.

`@tailwindcss/webpack` and `@tailwindcss/turbopack` are near-identical webpack `LoaderContext` loaders taking `{ base, optimize }`, both keyed into a shared `QuickLRU` cache of max size 50 via `getCacheKey(resourceId, opts)`.

`@tailwindcss/browser` is a CDN build that reads `<style type="text/tailwindcss">` blocks, auto-injects `@import "tailwindcss";` when the user's CSS has no `@import`, and serves `tailwindcss`, `/preflight`, `/theme`, and `/utilities` from inlined `assets.css.*` strings; plugins and config files throw.

The v3 JS plugin API is fully re-implemented in `compat/plugin-api.ts`: `addBase`, `addVariant`, `matchVariant`, `addUtilities`, `matchUtilities`, `addComponents`/`matchComponents` (which just delegate to the utility variants), and a `theme()` function built by `createThemeFn`.

`tailwindcss` re-exports v3 compatibility entry points as separate package exports: `tailwindcss/colors`, `tailwindcss/defaultTheme`, `tailwindcss/plugin`, and `tailwindcss/lib/util/flattenColorPalette`, each with paired `.ts`/`.cts` implementations for ESM and CJS.

`@tailwindcss/upgrade` is a standalone migration CLI (`--config`, `--force`, `--version`) that refuses to run on a dirty git tree, migrates stylesheets, migrates `tailwind.config.js` into CSS, rewrites class names in templates, and then shells out to the detected package manager to bump `tailwindcss` and friends to `@latest`.

The Oxide scanner ships language-aware pre-processors for 14 template dialects, dispatched by file extension: Clojure, Elixir/HEEx, Razor, Haml, JSON, Markdown, Pug, Ruby/ERB, Slim, Svelte, Rust, Template Toolkit, Twig, and Vue.

Source maps are a supported output across surfaces: the core exposes `buildSourceMap()` returning a `DecodedSourceMap`, the CLI writes it inline or to a file via `--map`, and Vite emits it when `config.css.devSourcemap` is on.

data_flow.summary: There are two independent input streams that converge at `build()`. Stream one is CSS: a stylesheet string is parsed by `CSS.parse`, `@import`s are inlined, at-rules are walked to populate a `Theme`, a `Utilities` registry, and a `Variants` registry, and the result is a `DesignSystem`. Stream two is candidates: the Rust `Scanner` walks the filesystem (gitignore-aware), pre-processes files by extension, runs byte-level state machines to extract class-name-shaped strings, and returns a sorted `Vec<String>` across the NAPI boundary. `build(candidates)` compiles those strings against the design system into AST nodes, splices them into the `@tailwind utilities` placeholder node, runs `optimizeAst`, and prints CSS via `toCss`. State ownership is explicit: `Theme` owns variables, `DesignSystem` owns caches, and the Rust `Scanner` owns file/mtime/candidate sets.

claims.claim: Input boundary one: `compile(css, opts)` calls `CSS.parse(css, { from })` then `parseCss`, which first wraps the AST in `contextNode({ base }, ast)` and resolves `@import`s through `substituteAtImports` before any at-rule walking happens.

`@theme` declarations are drained into a `Theme` map keyed by unescaped custom-property name, carrying `ThemeOptions` bit flags (`INLINE`, `REFERENCE`, `DEFAULT`, `STATIC`, `USED`) and a source location; `@keyframes` inside `@theme` are pulled out into `theme.addKeyframes` and re-hoisted as `atRoot` nodes.
The first `@theme` rule is replaced by a `:root, :host` style rule whose body is filled in *after* the compat hooks run, so JS-config theme extensions land in the same emitted variable block.

`@source` at-rules are split at parse time: `inline(...)` forms are brace-expanded into `inlineCandidates` (or `ignoredCandidates` when negated, which seed `designSystem.invalidCandidates`), while path forms become `{ base, pattern, negated }` entries returned as `compiler.sources`.

Every integration builds the scanner source list with the same three-branch rule: `root === 'none'` → no sources, `root === null` → `{ base, pattern: '**/*' }`, else the explicit `source(…)` root, concatenated with `compiler.sources`.

Input boundary two: `Scanner::scan()` calls `discover_sources()` (a `WalkBuilder` walk that populates `files`, `dirs`, `extensions`, and `mtimes`), then `extract_candidates()`, and returns a `par_sort_unstable`-sorted candidate vector.

File bytes are transformed before extraction: `pre_process_input(content, extension)` rewrites dialect-specific syntax (e.g. Pug/Haml/Slim shorthand) into something the generic extractor can read, then `Extractor::extract` runs a `CssVariableMachine` and a `CandidateMachine` over the bytes, emitting `Extracted::Candidate` and `Extracted::CssVariable`.

CSS files found during the walk are routed separately: `extract_candidates` calls `extract_css_variables` on them so that `--my-var` references in stylesheets count as used variables, distinct from utility candidates.

Candidate strings beginning with `--` are not compiled as utilities at all — `build()` routes them to `designSystem.theme.markUsedVariable(candidate)`, which is how theme variables referenced only from markup survive tree-shaking.

`compileCandidates` parses each raw candidate into `Candidate[]`, compiles each to AST nodes via `designSystem.compileAstNodes`, and sorts the result by a BigInt variant bitmask first, then by `GLOBAL_PROPERTY_ORDER` index, then by property count, then alphabetically — this is what produces Tailwind's stable output ordering.

Output boundary: `build()` mutates `utilitiesNode.nodes` in place, runs `optimizeAst(ast, designSystem, opts.polyfills)`, and `compile()`'s wrapper only re-runs `toCss` when the returned AST object identity changed — an explicit identity-based memoization.

Polyfills are a caller-controlled bitfield (`Polyfills.AtProperty`, `Polyfills.ColorMix`, `Polyfills.All`); the PostCSS plugin masks out `AtProperty` for `.module.css` files because the emitted global `*` rules break CSS Modules purity checks.

The PostCSS integration converts between AST dialects on both ends — `postCssAstToCssAst(root)` on the way in and `cssAstToPostCssAst(postcss, tailwindCssAst, root.source)` on the way out — and caches the converted PostCSS root so unchanged builds clone rather than re-convert.

Asset URL rewriting is an opt-in transform in the IO layer, not the core: `@tailwindcss/node`'s `loadStylesheet` wrapper calls `rewriteUrls({ css, root, base })` only when `shouldRewriteUrls` is set, which Vite always sets and PostCSS gates behind `transformAssetUrls`.

behavior_traces.summary: Three flows matter most: a cold CLI build, a CLI watch-mode rebuild, and the Vite dev-server transform. All three share the same skeleton — create compiler, derive sources, construct `Scanner`, scan, build, write — but differ in how they decide between a full and an incremental rebuild. The browser CDN build is a fourth, MutationObserver-driven variant of the same loop. The distinguishing detail across all of them is that 'full rebuild' means *discarding and recreating the compiler*, while 'incremental' means only feeding new candidate strings into the existing one.

claims.claim: Cold CLI build order: `run()` → `build.handle(flags)` → resolve `--cwd`/`--input`/`--output` to absolute paths and reject identical in/out → read input (or `drainStdin()`, or default `@import 'tailwindcss';`) → `createCompiler(input, I)` → `scanner.scan()` → `compiler.build(candidates)` → `write(output, map, args, I)` → print `Done in …`.

`createCompiler` registers an `onDependency(path)` callback that pushes into `fullRebuildPaths`, and then deliberately appends a *negated* source for `path.basename(process.execPath)` so the standalone binary never scans itself — a rename-proof self-exclusion.
Watch mode calls `loadWatcher()` first (so a missing `@parcel/watcher` fails with a useful message before any watcher is registered), then `createWatchers(await watchDirectories(scanner), handle)`.

The watch handler short-circuits when the only changed file is `args['--output']`, preventing the write-triggers-rebuild infinite loop, then calls `getRebuildStrategy(files, fullRebuildPaths)` to choose a branch.

On a `full` rebuild the CLI does, in order: re-read input → `clearRequireCache(resolvedFullRebuildPaths)` → snapshot `backupRebuildPaths` → reset `fullRebuildPaths` → `createCompiler` → `scanner.scan()` → set up new watchers → tear down old watchers → `compiler.build(candidates)`.

On an `incremental` rebuild it calls `scanner.scanFiles(rebuildStrategy.changedFiles)` and returns early without writing if zero new candidates were found — so touching a file with no new classes costs no disk write.

The watch `catch` block restores `fullRebuildPaths = backupRebuildPaths` before logging, with an inline comment explaining the recovery case: deleting a transitive dependency of `tailwind.config.js` would otherwise leave the compiler permanently unable to re-register that dependency.

Polling mode is a separate code path from event-based watching: `--poll` is validated to be a positive number (default 250ms), and it drives a `fullRebuild(I)` closure plus cursor-hiding escape codes with `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handlers that exit 130/143.

Vite dev transform order: `isPotentialCssRootFile(id)` gate → look up a `Root` in `rootsByEnv` keyed by `this.environment?.name` → `root.generate(src, addWatchFile, I)` → return `{ code, map }`; returning `false` from `generate` deletes the root from the map so it can be garbage collected.

`Root.generate` decides to rebuild by calling `requiresBuild()`, which stats every entry in `buildDependencies` and returns true if any mtime advanced or any file is missing — an mtime-map strategy mirrored in the PostCSS and webpack plugins.

After compiling, `Root.generate` bails with `false` unless the compiler reported at least one of `Features.AtApply | JsPluginCompat | ThemeFunction | Utilities | Variants` — this is how ordinary non-Tailwind `.css` files pass through Vite untouched.

The PostCSS plugin has an even cheaper bail: before touching the cache it does a `root.walkAtRules` scan for any of `import|reference|theme|variant|config|plugin|apply|tailwind` and returns immediately if none are present.

Browser CDN flow: `rebuild('full')` → `createCompiler()` gathers all `style[type="text/tailwindcss"]` text, compares against `lastCss` to skip needless recompiles → `build(kind)` collects `element.classList` across `[class]` elements, diffs against a global `classes` Set, and assigns `sheet.textContent = compiler.build(newClasses)`; builds are serialized through a `buildQueue` promise chain.

Two MutationObservers drive the browser build: one watches each known `<style>` element for `characterData`/`childList` changes (→ full rebuild), the other watches `document.documentElement` for `class` attribute changes and added nodes (→ incremental), explicitly skipping the injected output `sheet` to avoid a feedback loop.

Upgrade flow order: dirty-git check → version match check → glob `**/*.css` → `Stylesheet.load` → `analyzeStylesheets` → `linkConfigsToStylesheets` (v3 only) → `migrateJsConfig` → `migrateStylesheet` → `splitStylesheets` (v3 only) → `postcss([sortBuckets(), formatNodes()])` → `writeFileSafely` → package-manager upgrade → template migration.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is unusually thorough and layered: Vitest for ~80 co-located unit/snapshot suites, `cargo test` for the Rust scanner and the vendored `ignore` crate, a bespoke Vitest-based integration harness that materializes real temp projects and installs packed tarballs, and Playwright for browser-truth assertions about computed styles. CI runs unit and integration suites as two separate workflows, each with a three-OS matrix that is trimmed to Linux-only on feature branches unless the PR body contains `[ci-all]`. The gaps are mostly in the thin adapter layers — the CLI watch/poll machinery, the webpack/Turbopack loaders, and the release scripts have no direct unit tests.

claims.claim: Vitest is configured at the root with `projects: ['./packages/*']` and excludes `*.spec.*` files and `integrations/**` — the `.spec.ts` extension is reserved for Playwright so the two runners never collide.

Roughly 80 `*.test.ts` files live beside their sources under `packages/`, dominated by `utilities.test.ts` at ~31,600 lines and `index.test.ts` at ~7,300 lines — the utility matrix is tested exhaustively by snapshot.

`packages/tailwindcss/vitest.config.mts` registers a custom snapshot serializer at `src/test-utils/custom-serializer.ts`, which is why CSS snapshots read as formatted stylesheets rather than escaped strings.

Rust coverage centers on `crates/oxide/tests/scanner.rs` (~4,080 lines, 80+ `#[test]` cases inside a `mod scanner` block) covering source resolution, gitignore interaction, and symlink handling; the vendored `ignore` crate carries its own upstream tests.

The integration harness in `integrations/utils.ts` exports a custom `test(name, config, cb)` that mkdtemps a real project directory, writes a `fs` map of files, and hands the callback `exec`, `spawn`, `fs.expectFileToContain`, and `parseSourceMap` helpers.

Integration tests run against real packed tarballs: `PUBLIC_PACKAGES` is derived by reading `dist/` and mapping `tailwindcss-*.tgz` back to `@tailwindcss/*` names, which is why `pnpm build` must precede `pnpm test:integrations`.

There are 42 integration test files across six suites — `cli`, `oxide`, `postcss`, `turbopack`, `upgrade`, `vite`, `webpack` — with the Vite suite alone covering Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit, SolidStart, Qwik, React Router, Preact, Vue, CSS Modules, SSR, and source maps.

The integration harness compensates for known CI flakiness: timeouts are 120s on Windows vs 60s elsewhere, `retry` defaults to 2 under CI, and on Windows CI the temp root is derived from `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` because `tmpdir()` returns a `RUNNER~1` short path that breaks Vite builds.

Playwright covers browser-truth behavior that unit tests cannot: `packages/tailwindcss/tests/ui.spec.ts` (~2,480 lines) asserts *computed* values such as `touch-action` after `page.hover()` and resolved `linear-gradient(... in oklab ...)` strings.

The Playwright config sets Firefox `ui.primaryPointerCapabilities`/`ui.allPointerCapabilities` to `0x02 | 0x04` because headless Firefox otherwise reports no pointer, which would silently break every `hover:` variant assertion relying on `(hover: hover)`.

WebKit is skipped on Windows in both Playwright configs (a hanging-worker workaround) and the CI matrix pins macOS to `macos-15` for the unit job because Playwright 1.62+ dropped WebKit on macOS 14 and hangs rather than failing.

CI has two independent workflows: `ci.yml` (build → lint → `pnpm test` → Playwright) and `integration-tests.yml` (a 6-way `integration` matrix crossed with the OS matrix), both notifying Discord via `secrets.DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` on `main` failures.

Windows and macOS runners are excluded on feature branches unless the PR body contains `[ci-all]` (or the author is `depfu[bot]`), so most PRs only get Linux coverage by default — a documented, deliberate trade-off.

CI lint is effectively Linux-only *and* currently dead: the step is gated on `matrix.runner.os == 'ubuntu-latest'`, but the Linux matrix entry sets `os: namespace-profile-default`, so the condition never matches.

Benchmarks are a first-class suite run via `pnpm bench` (`vitest bench`), with `*.bench.ts` files for the CSS parser, candidate parser, AST, sorting, brace expansion, and `infer-data-type`; the Rust side has its own throughput harness in `crates/oxide/src/main.rs`.

risk_map.summary: Security surface is narrow but real: the compiler loads and executes arbitrary user JS via `@plugin`/`@config` through jiti, the upgrade CLI shells out to git and the package manager and rewrites source files in place, and the scanner walks the filesystem outside the repo root whenever `@source` points there. The larger operational risks are correctness-of-caching risks — every integration hand-rolls its own mtime-based invalidation, and the core `build()` explicitly assumes candidates are only ever added, never removed. Cross-platform fragility (Windows paths, symlinks, Bun/USERPROFILE) shows up repeatedly as inline workarounds, which is a reliable signal of where regressions land.

claims.claim: `@plugin` and `@config` execute arbitrary user code: `loadModule` resolves the id and calls `importModule`, which falls back to `createJiti(...).import(path)` when native `import()` fails — so a `.ts` config file is transpiled and run in-process with full Node privileges.

`globalThis.__tw_resolve` and `globalThis.__tw_load` are ambient global escape hatches consulted before every CSS and JS resolution; the standalone binary installs them to serve embedded assets, but any code loaded into the process can override module resolution by setting them.

`@tailwindcss/upgrade` shells out with `execSync` to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git status --porcelain`, and `npm ls tailwindcss --json`, then calls `pkgManager.add(...)` to install packages — it mutates the user's dependency tree as part of a 'migration'.

The upgrade tool's only safety net for in-place source rewriting is the `isRepoDirty()` check, which `--force` disables outright; after that it rewrites every matched CSS file and every template file via `writeFileSafely` with no backup.

Template rewriting is heuristic and acknowledged as such: `isSafeMigration` maintains hand-written regex denylists for Vue `v-if`, Alpine `wire:`, shadcn `variant:` props, Next.js `placeholder=`, and `$emit(` — any unlisted pattern risks a class-name rewrite inside a string that is not a class attribute.

File IO reaches outside the repo root by design: `SourceEntry::External` exists specifically to let `@source "../node_modules/my-lib"` bypass the default ignore rules, and `resolveJsId` extends module search with `process.env.NODE_PATH`.

`build()` carries a documented soundness assumption — 'this currently assumes that we only add new candidates and never remove any' — appearing twice as an early-return condition, so a candidate disappearing from source will not shrink the emitted CSS without a full rebuild.

Cache invalidation is duplicated four times with slightly different shapes: `Root.requiresBuild()` in Vite, the `context.mtimes` loop in PostCSS, `getRebuildStrategy` in the CLI, and per-loader `CacheEntry.mtimes` in webpack/Turbopack — a bug fixed in one will not propagate to the others.

`@tailwindcss/webpack` and `@tailwindcss/turbopack` are near-verbatim copies of each other down to identical `LoaderOptions`, `CacheEntry`, `getCacheKey`, and `getContextFromCache` definitions — divergence between them is a live duplication hazard.

The PostCSS plugin deliberately swallows errors — it `console.error`s and then throws `root.error(...)` after resetting `context.compiler = null`, with a comment that throwing directly 'will cause PostCSS to no longer watch for changes' — so genuine compile failures can surface as an empty stylesheet plus console noise.

The Vite plugin carries two hardcoded upstream-bug workarounds — skipping `addWatchFile` for the input file itself (Qwik) and ignoring `.svg` paths containing `#` or `?` (tailwindcss#16877) — meaning edits to those files silently do not trigger rebuilds.

Windows and symlink handling is a recurring fragility: the scanner canonicalizes via `dunce::canonicalize` with a cached parent-directory map, inserts both symlinked and canonical paths into `self.files`, and `scan_content` has to re-walk the tree to validate previously-unknown changed files.

The standalone build re-spawns itself as a nested Bun process with `USERPROFILE` blanked out to work around Bun binary downloads failing on Windows CI when Turborepo passes the variable through — a build-time landmine with no test coverage.
`packages/tailwindcss/src/feature-flags.ts` is an empty file still present in the tree — dead scaffolding that suggests a removed flag system.

`crates/ignore` is a vendored fork of BurntSushi's crate carrying local `# CHANGED:` edits (e.g. pinning `edition = "2024"` instead of inheriting from the workspace), so upstream security or correctness fixes require a manual re-vendor.

The CLI watch path is a ~600-line function with no unit tests of its own — `getRebuildStrategy`, `watchDirectories`, `createWatchers`, and the polling loop are only exercised indirectly through `integrations/cli/index.test.ts`.

extension_points.summary: The system has three distinct extension tiers. Tier one is CSS-native: `@utility`, `@custom-variant`, and `@theme` register directly into the design system with no JS. Tier two is the JS plugin API, preserved wholesale from v3 in `compat/plugin-api.ts` and loaded via `@plugin`. Tier three is internal: the `Utilities` and `Variants` classes are plain registries with `static`/`functional` methods that core code and plugins call identically, and the upgrade tool has its own ordered `DEFAULT_MIGRATIONS` array. Adding a new template language to the scanner is a matter of one new pre-processor module plus one match arm.

claims.claim: `Utilities` is the utility registry — `static(name, compileFn)` and `functional(name, compileFn, options)` push into a `DefaultMap<string, Utility[]>`, with a parallel `completions` map driving IntelliSense suggestions.

`Variants` is the variant registry, offering `static`, `functional`, and `fromAst(name, ast, designSystem)` (which powers `@custom-variant` with a body), and tracking `compounds`/`compoundsWith` bit flags that decide which variants may be composed with which.

`@utility` is the CSS-native extension point: `createCssUtility(node)` turns the at-rule into a `(designSystem) => void` registration function, with explicit validation that functional utilities end in `-*` and that `@utility` is never nested.

`@custom-variant` registrations are topologically sorted before application via `topologicalSort(customVariantDependencies, { onCircularDependency })`, so variants may reference each other and circular references produce a rendered CSS error rather than a stack overflow.

`buildPluginApi` is the JS plugin extension surface, exposing `addBase`, `addVariant`, `matchVariant`, `addUtilities`, `matchUtilities`, `addComponents`, `matchComponents`, and a `theme()` accessor, with name validation that rejects non-single-class selectors and non-lowercase-leading utility names.

`@plugin` supports typed options passed as a declaration body — `CssPluginOptions` values are parsed from the declaration text into JSON primitives (`null`, `true`, numbers, comma-separated lists) before being handed to the plugin factory.

`applyCompatibilityHooks` is the single seam where all v3 behavior is grafted on — it registers `darkModePlugin`, `registerContainerCompat`, `registerLegacyUtilities`, `registerScreensConfig`, and `registerThemeVariantOverrides`, keeping legacy concerns out of core.

`DesignSystem.storage` is an explicit general-purpose extension slot — a `Record<symbol, unknown>` documented as requiring unique symbol keys to avoid collisions; the canonicalization code uses it via `prepareDesignSystemStorage` and `UTILITY_SIGNATURE_KEY`.

Adding a new template language to the scanner requires two edits: a new module in `crates/oxide/src/extractor/pre_processors/` re-exported from `mod.rs`, and a new extension arm in the `pre_process_input` match statement.

The extractor is itself a pluggable set of state machines all implementing the `Machine` trait — `ArbitraryPropertyMachine`, `ArbitraryValueMachine`, `NamedUtilityMachine`, `NamedVariantMachine`, `ModifierMachine`, `StringMachine`, and others — which `main.rs` can benchmark individually via `_run_machine::<T>`.

The upgrade tool's template codemods are an ordered array `DEFAULT_MIGRATIONS: Migration[]` where each entry is `(designSystem, userConfig, rawCandidate) => string`; order is load-bearing, flagged by the inline comment that `migrateVariantOrder` must run before variant-modifying migrations.

CSS-level codemods are a parallel, separately-composed pipeline in `codemods/css/` (`migrate-at-apply`, `migrate-at-layer-utilities`, `migrate-import`, `migrate-media-screen`, `migrate-preflight`, `migrate-tailwind-directives`, `migrate-theme-to-var`, `migrate-variants-directive`), each with a co-located test file.

The CLI command table is a literal dispatch in `run()` — `command === 'build'` and `command === 'canonicalize'` — with options merged from `build.options()` and `sharedOptions`, so a new subcommand means a module exporting `options()`/`handle()` plus one branch.
`internal-example-plugin` is a workspace package existing purely as a plugin-resolution fixture, consumed as a devDependency by `@tailwindcss/postcss` tests.

agent_handoff.summary: Read the core compiler before touching anything: `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.ts` (`parseCss` → `compileAst` → `compile`), then `design-system.ts` and `compile.ts`. Almost every behavioral change belongs in `packages/tailwindcss` or `crates/oxide`, not in the integration packages — those are thin and near-duplicative on purpose. Conventions are enforced mechanically: Prettier config lives inline in the root `package.json` (no semicolons, single quotes, 100 columns, organize-imports), and `pnpm lint` runs `prettier --check` plus `turbo lint` (which is `tsc --noEmit` per package). The project explicitly does not accept feature PRs without prior discussion, and does not accept any PR without tests.

claims.claim: Read first, in order: `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.ts` (the at-rule walk and `build()` contract), `packages/tailwindcss/src/design-system.ts` (the `DesignSystem` type and its caches), `packages/tailwindcss/src/compile.ts` (candidate → AST + sorting), and `crates/oxide/src/scanner/mod.rs` (the scan lifecycle).

Setup is `pnpm install`, `rustup default stable`, `rustup target add wasm32-wasip1-threads`, then `pnpm build`; the WASM target is mandatory because `@tailwindcss/oxide`'s `build` script always runs `build:wasm` after `build:platform`.
Day-to-day loop is `pnpm tdd` (Vitest watch with `--hideSkippedTests`); for browser or integration behavior you must run `pnpm build` first because both harnesses consume built artifacts.
Before submitting: run `pnpm test` (cargo + vitest), `pnpm build && pnpm test:integrations`, `pnpm build && pnpm test:ui`, and `pnpm run lint`; `pnpm run format` auto-fixes style.

Code style is Prettier with `semi: false`, `singleQuote: true`, `printWidth: 100`, and `prettier-plugin-organize-imports`; `integrations/**/*.ts` additionally uses `prettier-plugin-embed` so embedded CSS/HTML template literals are formatted.

Safe edit boundary: the core compiler must stay IO-free. Anything needing `fs`, module resolution, or Lightning CSS belongs in `@tailwindcss/node`, which is the only package allowed to be the bridge between core and the runtime.

A change to utility or variant output almost always needs a snapshot update in `packages/tailwindcss/src/utilities.test.ts` or `variants.test.ts`, plus a check of `packages/tailwindcss/src/__snapshots__/`; these files are enormous, so target specific test names rather than running the whole suite.

Trap: output ordering is not alphabetical. It is governed by `GLOBAL_PROPERTY_ORDER` in `property-order.ts` combined with a BigInt variant bitmask; reordering that array silently reshuffles every generated stylesheet.

Trap: `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'test'` gates both the license banner comment prepended in `compileAst` and the Lightning CSS warning output, so CSS produced under test differs from production output.

Trap: the integration packages duplicate the same source-derivation block (`root === 'none'` / `root === null` / explicit root, concat `compiler.sources`). Changing that contract in core requires updating the CLI, Vite, PostCSS, webpack, and Turbopack call sites together.

Trap: Rust edits need `pnpm build` (or `pnpm --filter @tailwindcss/oxide build`) to regenerate the `.node` addon before JS tests see them; `turbo.json` declares the cross-crate `inputs` that make this cache correctly.

Debugging hook: set `DEBUG=1` (or `DEBUG=tailwindcss`) to enable the `Instrumentation` timers that bracket every phase — 'Setup compiler', 'Scan for candidates', 'Build CSS', 'Optimize CSS' — across the CLI, Vite, PostCSS, and loaders.

Debugging hook for the scanner: `crates/oxide/src/scanner/init_tracing.rs` gates `tracing` events behind a `SHOULD_TRACE` lazy static, logging both provided and optimized source entries at INFO level.

Process convention: PRs need a test plan and tests; feature PRs are likely to be closed without prior discussion in GitHub Discussions; adding `[ci-all]` to the PR body opts into the full Windows/macOS CI matrix.

Do not hand-edit release plumbing: `scripts/version-packages.mjs`, `scripts/lock-pre-release-versions.mjs`, `scripts/release-channel.js`, and `scripts/pre-publish-optimizations.mjs` are driven by `prepare-release.yml`/`release.yml`, and npm trusted publishing validates the calling workflow filename.

readmePreview: tRPC Move fast and break nothing. End-to-end typesafe APIs made easy.

overview.summary: tRPC 11.19.0 (this checkout of github.com/trpc/trpc) is a TypeScript monorepo for end-to-end typesafe RPCs without schemas or code generation. Application authors define procedures once with initTRPC; clients call them through a typed Proxy that never imports server runtime code, only its types. @trpc/server is transport-agnostic and ships adapters for Fetch, Node, Express, Fastify, Next.js, AWS Lambda, a standalone HTTP server, and WebSockets, while @trpc/client, @trpc/react-query, and @trpc/tanstack-react-query consume the same router type. The repo also contains runnable examples (Next/Prisma, a Drizzle SSE chat, Cloudflare Workers, Nuxt, Lambdas), an alpha OpenAPI generator, a jscodeshift upgrade CLI, and the Docusaurus docs site in www/.

system_map.summary: The publishable libraries live under packages/ and are wired as a pnpm workspace (packages/*, examples/*, www) driven by Turborepo. @trpc/server is the runtime and type core; adapters are thin wrappers around resolveResponse or, for WebSockets, applyWSSHandler. The client is a link chain terminated by HTTP or WS. There is no database inside the library — persistence shows up only in examples (Prisma, Drizzle). Release is Lerna at 11.19.0, with @trpc/openapi published separately as 11.19.0-alpha. Docs are a Docusaurus app deployed with a large Vercel redirect map.

claims.claim: Root package.json names the workspace root, requires Node ^24.0.0 and pnpm ^12 (packageManager pnpm@12.4.1), and exposes build (turbo --filter=./packages/* build), dev, test (vitest), typecheck-packages, lint, and Lerna canary/prerelease scripts.

pnpm-workspace.yaml includes packages/*, examples/*, examples/.* /*, examples/minimal*, and www plus www/og-image. The default catalog pins vitest ^5, vite ^8, turbo ^2.10, next ^15.5, fastify ^5, and typescript ^7.0.2, while catalog ts-api pins typescript ^6.0.3 and the root package depends on catalog:ts-api.

Published library versions in this tree are @trpc/server, @trpc/client, @trpc/react-query, @trpc/next, and @trpc/tanstack-react-query at 11.19.0. lerna.json version is 11.19.0 with npmClient pnpm. @trpc/openapi is 11.19.0-alpha and is not on the same stable version line.

Server public API is packages/server/src/@trpc/server/index.ts, re-exported by packages/server/src/index.ts. It exports initTRPC, TRPCError, lazy, tracked, callProcedure as callTRPCProcedure, and inference helpers. Implementation lives under packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/, which is also a package export named ./unstable-core-do-not-import.

initTRPC is a single TRPCBuilder instance. context() and meta() only change generics; create() builds RootConfig (transformer, isDev from NODE_ENV, allowOutsideOfServer, errorFormatter, isServer) and returns procedure, middleware, router, mergeRouters, and createCallerFactory. It throws if isServer is false unless allowOutsideOfServer is true.

HTTP handling is resolveResponse in unstable-core-do-not-import/http/resolveResponse.ts. Official adapters that call it or nodeHTTPRequestHandler include fetchRequestHandler, createNextApiHandler, createExpressMiddleware, fastifyTRPCPlugin, awsLambdaRequestHandler, and createHTTPServer/createHTTPHandler. WebSockets use applyWSSHandler instead.

@trpc/client exports createTRPCClient plus subpath links httpBatchLink, httpLink, loggerLink, splitLink, and wsLink, and an ./unstable-internals export. Peer dependency is @trpc/server 11.19.0. Each library package builds with tsdown (build / dev --watch) rather than tsc emit.

turbo.json caches build outputs dist, .next, and build, makes dev persistent and uncached, and declares global env CI, NODE_ENV, DATABASE_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, AUTH_GITHUB_ID, and AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET. Lint and typecheck depend on ^build.

CI workflow .github/workflows/main.yml runs on pull_request and on push to main, next, and canary. PR jobs build, typecheck packages, typecheck www, unit tests with coverage, and an examples e2e matrix that includes Postgres. Release is .github/workflows/release-manual.yml (workflow_dispatch patch/minor with dist-tag latest or canary, plus push to main touching packages). NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE is true.

www/package.json is a private Docusaurus 3 site (docusaurus start/build) that depends on the workspace tRPC packages. www/vercel.json is a large permanent-redirect table from old /docs paths onto the current docs IA, plus /discord, /sponsor, and /drift.

The library has no storage layer. examples/next-prisma-starter persists posts with Prisma. examples/next-sse-chat persists Channel and Post with Drizzle (pgTableCreator prefix sse-chat_) and Postgres. examples/cloudflare-workers is a WorkerEntrypoint whose fetch() calls fetchRequestHandler with an empty context and no database.

Vitest resolves @trpc/<pkg> imports to each package src/ via aliases built by reading package.json exports, so unit tests execute TypeScript source rather than dist. Root vitest.config.ts merges that shared config and sets test.projects to ./packages/*.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface area is the procedure builder (query, mutation, subscription), a middleware pipeline with pluggable validators, several HTTP and WebSocket client links, React Query hook and options-object integrations, Next.js SSR helpers, and framework adapters. Examples demonstrate the same API on Next pages, the Next app router, Cloudflare Workers, Express, Fastify, AWS Lambda, Bun, Deno, and Nuxt. Ancillary products are an OpenAPI generator CLI, a codemod upgrade CLI, and TanStack Intent skills shipped inside the packages.

claims.claim: ProcedureBuilder.input(), .output(), .use(), .query(), .mutation(), and .subscription() are the authoring API. createResolver appends a final middleware that awaits the user resolver. experimental_caller can wrap invoke. Calling the resulting procedure without a getRawInput option throws and points at server-side calls.

getParseFn accepts Standard Schema (~standard), Zod parseAsync/parse, Valibot functions, Yup validateSync, Superstruct create, ArkType assert, and custom functions. Input and output parsers are installed as middlewares by createInputMiddleware and createOutputMiddleware.

Routers are plain records. createRouterFactory flattens nested routers into _def.procedures keyed by dotted path, supports lazy() dynamic imports, and rejects duplicate keys and the reserved names then, call, and apply. mergeRouters concatenates records.

createCallerFactory returns a proxy caller that resolves ctx (value or function), looks up the procedure with getProcedureAtPath, and invokes it in-process. This is the server-side call path and is re-exported on the router as createCaller.

Client links implemented in packages/client include httpLink, httpBatchLink (default batching link), httpBatchStreamLink, httpSubscriptionLink, wsLink plus createWSClient, splitLink, loggerLink, retryLink, and unstable_localLink, which calls callProcedure in-process and never hits HTTP.

@trpc/react-query exports createTRPCReact, getQueryKey, getMutationKey, and createTRPCQueryUtils, and re-exports @trpc/client. It also ships ./rsc and ./server (ssgProxy) entry points for RSC and static helpers.

@trpc/tanstack-react-query exports createTRPCContext, createTRPCOptionsProxy, and useSubscription. The upgrade CLI's first transform is 'Migrate Hooks to xxxOptions API' and the second is 'Migrate context provider setup', optionally installing this package unless --skipTanstackQuery.

@trpc/next's package entry re-exports withTRPC and createTRPCNext for the Pages Router. App Router helpers are experimental and live in packages/server/src/adapters/next-app-dir.ts as experimental_nextAppDirCaller, experimental_redirect, and experimental_notFound.

Subscriptions over HTTP are async iterables served as SSE. RootConfig.sse defaults enabled to true and accepts ping, maxDurationMs, emitAndEndImmediately, and client reconnect options. jsonl options configure httpBatchStreamLink. tracked() marks resumable events. The legacy sse() helper is deprecated in favor of tracked.

Non-JSON bodies are first-class for octet streams: octetInputParser accepts Blob, Uint8Array, or File-like values and requires the parsed value to already be a ReadableStream. Batch JSON uses content-type application/json and a batch=1 query flag.

@trpc/openapi exports generateOpenAPIDocument(GenerateOptions) where exportName defaults to AppRouter, and paths such as /user.create are relative to an optional servers URL. The package bin is trpc-openapi. It also ships an intent bin, as do server, client, and next.

examples/next-prisma-starter exposes healthcheck plus post.list, post.byId, and post.add through pages/api/trpc/[trpc].ts via createNextApiHandler. The React client entry used by the minimal example is examples/minimal-react/client/src/main.tsx, and Playwright asserts the text 'tRPC user'.

examples/next-sse-chat is an app-router chat: GET and POST /api/trpc/[trpc] use fetchRequestHandler, NextAuth (GitHub or a mocked Credentials provider), Drizzle posts, and procedures post.add (authed), post.infinite, and post.onAdd (SSE subscription with tracked event ids).

README documents the product promise (typesafe APIs, no codegen, batching, subscriptions, React/Next/Express/Fastify adapters) and tells AI agents to install skills with npx @tanstack/intent@latest install. Package keywords include tanstack-intent and files lists include a skills directory.

data_flow.summary: A call is a typed operation that becomes an observable, passes through a link chain, and is encoded as JSON (or JSONL/SSE/WebSocket frames). On the server, getRequestInfo splits batch paths, deserializes inputs with the configured transformer, and resolveResponse invokes procedures with one shared context. Middleware, including validators, runs before the resolver. Outputs are serialized by transformTRPCResponse. Errors are a fixed shape keyed by JSON-RPC-style codes. Persistence, when present, is inside user resolvers, not the framework.

claims.claim: createTRPCClient constructs a TRPCUntypedClient and wraps it in createTRPCClientProxy. The proxy pops the last path segment, maps query/mutate/subscribe through clientCallTypeMap, joins the rest with dots, and calls client.query, client.mutation, or client.subscription.

TRPCUntypedClient.$request increments requestId and calls createChain with the operation. createChain walks links[index].next until a link terminates the observable. requestAsPromise converts the observable with observableToPromise and returns envelope.result.data, wrapping failures in TRPCClientError.from.

httpBatchLink builds separate dataLoaders for query and mutation. A batch is valid only when length <= maxItems (default Infinity) and the joined URL length <= maxURLLength (default Infinity). fetch() joins paths with commas, combines abort signals, and calls jsonHttpRequester. Subscriptions throw and must use httpSubscriptionLink or wsLink.

jsonContentTypeHandler treats batch=1 as a batch, splits opts.path on commas, enforces maxBatchSize, and reads inputs from the input query param on GET or from req.json() otherwise. Each input is passed through router._def._config.transformer.input.deserialize before the procedure sees it.

resolveResponse creates context exactly once via ctxManager.create. Each call in info.calls loads the procedure, checks TYPE_ACCEPTED_METHOD_MAP, and invokes proc with path, getRawInput, ctx, type, signal, and batchIndex. Non-batch JSON responses set content-type application/json and JSON.stringify(transformTRPCResponse(config, res)).

createProcedureCaller refuses direct calls, then callRecursive runs _def.middlewares[index] and threads ctx, input, and getRawInput overrides into next(). A missing result throws INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR ('did you forget to return next()'). A failed middleware rethrows its TRPCError. The resolver middleware is appended last by createResolver.

defaultTransformer is an identity serialize/deserialize pair. getDataTransformer splits a single DataTransformer into {input, output}. transformTRPCResponse serializes error payloads and result.data with config.transformer.output.serialize and leaves other envelopes unchanged.

getErrorShape builds {message, code: TRPC_ERROR_CODES_BY_KEY[code], data:{code, httpStatus}} and, only when config.isDev and error.stack is a string, copies the stack onto data.stack. The user errorFormatter then receives that shape. isDev defaults to NODE_ENV !== production.

Mutations accept only POST. Queries and subscriptions accept GET, or GET and POST when allowMethodOverride is true and the request method is POST. allowMethodOverride defaults false. allowBatching defaults to batching.enabled or true. A batch call when batching is disabled throws BAD_REQUEST.

fetchRequestHandler trims slashes, slices the endpoint off the pathname, and delegates to resolveResponse with error: null. createNextApiHandler reads req.query.trpc (string or array joined by /) and delegates to nodeHTTPRequestHandler. The Cloudflare example mounts endpoint /trpc on the Worker fetch handler.

In next-sse-chat, createContext calls NextAuth auth() and returns {session}. authedProcedure throws UNAUTHORIZED unless ctx.session.user.name is set, then overrides ctx.user. post.add inserts a Drizzle Post row, emits on an in-memory emitter, and post.onAdd yields tracked(post.id, post) from both a DB replay and that emitter.

In next-prisma-starter, post.list/byId/add call prisma.post with an explicit defaultPostSelect (id, title, text, createdAt, updatedAt). byId throws TRPCError NOT_FOUND when missing. Context is an empty object; createContextInner exists so tests can skip the Next req/res.

behavior_traces.summary: Startup is initTRPC.create once per backend, then router({...}) which flattens procedures. An HTTP query or mutation enters through an adapter, resolveResponse, getRequestInfo, one context factory, the procedure middleware stack, and transformTRPCResponse. A chat send is a mutation that writes Drizzle and an SSE subscription that replays and tails an emitter. In-process calls skip HTTP via createCaller or unstable_localLink.

claims.claim: Server startup in the Prisma starter: initTRPC.context<Context>().create({transformer, errorFormatter}) returns router and publicProcedure; appRouter = router({healthcheck, post: postRouter}); pages/api/trpc/[trpc].ts default-exports createNextApiHandler({router: appRouter, createContext, onError}). No listen() call exists in that file because Next invokes the handler.

HTTP query order: adapter (fetchRequestHandler or createNextApiHandler to nodeHTTPRequestHandler) calls resolveResponse; HEAD returns 204; getRequestInfo parses path and inputs; ctxManager.create(info) runs createContext once; the procedure function from createProcedureCaller runs callRecursive from middleware index 0 through input parsers to the resolver; non-stream results go through getErrorShape or {result:{data}}, initResponse, transformTRPCResponse, and new Response.

Client query order: user calls proxy path ending in .query; createTRPCClientProxy maps it to TRPCUntypedClient.query; $request builds an Operation and createChain walks links; httpBatchLink's query dataLoader.load joins the batch and jsonHttpRequester fetches; transformResult applies transformer.output; requestAsPromise returns result.data.

Prisma post.add trace: publicProcedure.input(zod).mutation receives {ctx, input}; prisma.post.create({data: input, select: defaultPostSelect}) runs; the row is returned as result.data. list uses cursor pagination (take limit+1, pop the extra row into nextCursor) and returns {items, nextCursor}.

SSE chat send trace: POST /api/trpc hits the route handler, fetchRequestHandler, resolveResponse. createContext loads the NextAuth session. authedProcedure checks user.name. post.add inserts into Drizzle Post, clears currentlyTyping, ee.emit('add', channelId, post). Subscribers in post.onAdd already hold ee.toIterable('add') and yield tracked(post.id, post) after filtering by channelId.

SSE reconnect trace inside post.onAdd: input.lastEventId selects that Post's createdAt, a findMany loads newer rows for the channel, they are yielded first, then the function for-awaits the emitter. Root config sets sse.maxDurationMs to 5 minutes, ping every 3s, and client.reconnectAfterInactivityMs of 5s. resolveResponse arms a timer that aborts the combined signal when maxDurationMs elapses.

In-process caller trace: createCallerFactory(appRouter) then caller(ctx).procedure(input) hits createRecursiveProxy, getProcedureAtPath, and procedure({getRawInput: async () => args[0], ctx, type, signal, batchIndex: 0}). onError receives the TRPCError and the original cause is rethrown. unstable_localLink is the client-side equivalent and calls callProcedure without a socket.

Lazy router trace: lazy(importRouter) marks the function with lazyMarker. createRouterFactory records a LazyLoader instead of walking the record. getProcedureAtPath, if the path is missing, finds a lazy key that is a prefix, awaits loader.load(), which imports the module (must be a router or a module with exactly one router export) and splices it into the aggregate record.

WebSocket server trace starts at applyWSSHandler(opts) in adapters/ws.ts. It uses parseTRPCMessage from @trpc/server/rpc, callTRPCProcedure, getErrorShape, and transformTRPCResponse. keepAlive defaults to a ping every 30_000ms and pong wait 5_000ms when enabled. fastifyTRPCPlugin can attach the same WS handler when useWSS is set.

Dev loop from CONTRIBUTING: pnpm install && pnpm build, then pnpm dev watches packages/* via turbo. A second terminal runs an example such as examples/next-prisma-starter pnpm dev against the workspace packages. pnpm test filters by substring, including GitHub issue numbers.

testing_signals.summary: Unit and integration tests are Vitest projects rooted at every packages/* package, with jsdom, globals, Istanbul coverage, and two CI retries. The heaviest behavioral coverage is packages/tests/server (adapters, batching, streaming, websockets, regressions) plus colocated tests in server, client, and react-query. Playwright smoke tests live in selected examples and run in a GitHub Actions matrix that is allowed to fail. OpenAPI fixture drift fails the unit job. App-dir, upgrade, vendor, www, and examples are excluded from coverage.

claims.claim: Root test script is vitest. vitest.shared.ts sets environment jsdom, globals, setupFiles packages/tests/suppressActWarnings.ts, coverage provider istanbul including **/src/**, restoreMocks, execArgv --expose-gc, and retry 2 when CI is set.

Coverage excludes www, examples, packages/next/src/app-dir, packages/server/src/adapters/next-app-dir, packages/upgrade/src, and vendor. codecov.yml sets project target auto with a 1% threshold, turns patch status off, ignores deprecated, form-data, app-dir, openapi cli.ts, and openapi test routers, and disables PR comments.

packages/tests is the integration package described in CONTRIBUTING. Its server suite includes batching.test.ts, streaming.test.ts, websockets.test.ts, middlewares.test.ts, caller.test.ts, adapters/, and a regression/ directory. React act warnings are muted in CI via MUTE_REACT_ACT_WARNINGS=1.

@trpc/react-query colocates dozens of hook tests under packages/react-query/test, including useQuery, useMutation, useInfiniteQuery, useSubscription, suspense variants, ssr/ssg, formData, and a regression/ folder. @trpc/tanstack-react-query tests options proxies under packages/tanstack-react-query/test.

The unit-test CI job runs pnpm test --coverage and then fails if git status shows changes under packages/openapi/test/routers, telling contributors to run pnpm -C packages/openapi codegen. Codecov upload uses codecov-action@v6 and only passes CODECOV_TOKEN for non-fork PRs.

Playwright is the e2e runner for examples that have playwright.config.ts. examples/minimal-react/test/smoke.test.ts loads / and waits for text=tRPC user with a 35s timeout. The e2e job runs, per example, test-dev, build, typecheck, and test-start via turbo, after copying .env.example to .env.

The e2e matrix covers .experimental/next-app-dir, diagnostics-big-router, internal-types-export, ssg, cloudflare-workers, express-minimal, express-server, fastify-server, minimal-react, next-formdata, next-minimal-starter, next-prisma-starter, next-prisma-todomvc, next-prisma-websockets-starter, openapi-codegen, soa, standalone-server, vercel-edge-runtime, and nuxt. next-sse-chat is commented out. The job sets continue-on-error true.

E2E Postgres is a GitHub service container with POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD trust and user postgres. NEXTAUTH_SECRET is set to the literal supersecret in that job's env. Separate jobs e2e-deno (deno-deploy) and e2e-bun exist; both are also PR-only.

Build and typecheck jobs run only on pull_request, not on push. The test job runs on both. Concurrency cancels in-progress runs for the same ref. Turbo remote cache uses secrets TURBO_TOKEN and vars TURBO_TEAM.

examples/next-prisma-starter has both a Vitest test at src/server/routers/post.test.ts and Playwright at playwright/smoke.test.ts. Its CI path is included in the e2e matrix, so the example is part of the PR gate even though example sources are excluded from Istanbul coverage.

Server package colocates tests such as procedureBuilder.test.ts, router.test.ts, initTRPC.test.ts, sse.test.ts, and adapters/node-http/incomingMessageToRequest.test.ts, including a case titled POST with body and maxBodySize. Client colocates createChain.test.ts, dedupeLink.test.ts, splitLink.test.ts, and localLink.test.ts.

@trpc/upgrade tests live in packages/upgrade/test with fixture TSX files and transforms.test.ts, but upgrade/src is excluded from coverage, so the CLI's git and package-manager side effects are not in the Codecov gate.

risk_map.summary: The framework does not authenticate requests; authorization is a user middleware. The risky defaults are unlimited Node request bodies, batching on with no max batch, stack traces in any non-production NODE_ENV, and transformer.deserialize running on attacker-controlled JSON. Several high-churn areas (Next app dir, the upgrade CLI, the SSE chat example) are outside the coverage gate or marked continue-on-error. WebSocket and HTTP stacks duplicate procedure invocation, so adapter bugs do not all flow through resolveResponse.

claims.claim: getErrorShape copies error.stack into the client-visible error when config.isDev is true. isDev defaults to process.env.NODE_ENV !== production, so any deployment that forgets NODE_ENV=production leaks stacks. The Prisma and SSE examples' errorFormatters return the shape unchanged.

nodeHTTPRequestHandler passes maxBodySize: opts.maxBodySize ?? null. incomingMessageToRequest only rejects PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE when maxBodySize is truthy and size exceeds it, so the default null means no body cap. The check also treats 0 as unlimited because it uses !opts.maxBodySize.

Batching is on unless the adapter sets allowBatching or batching.enabled to false. maxBatchSize is optional; jsonContentTypeHandler checks it only when it is a number. httpBatchLink defaults maxURLLength and maxItems to Infinity, so a client can build arbitrarily large batched URLs or bodies unless the app opts in.

GET query inputs are a raw JSON string in the input search param, then JSON.parse, then transformer.input.deserialize. Mutations cannot use GET: TYPE_ACCEPTED_METHOD_MAP and the method-override map both list mutation as POST only, with an explicit comment that GET must never perform a mutation.

resolveResponse returns 204 for every HEAD with no router or auth check, documented as a Lambda warmup. Subscriptions cannot be batched. A single-call JSON response that is an async iterable or contains promises/async iterables throws UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE and tells the client to use httpBatchStreamLink.

There is no auth inside @trpc/server. The SSE example's authedProcedure only checks that session.user.name is non-empty. post.onAdd and post.infinite are publicProcedure, so channel messages are readable without that check. When GitHub credentials are absent outside production, auth.tsx installs a Credentials provider that authorizes any name.

CI e2e sets NEXTAUTH_SECRET to the literal supersecret and starts Postgres with trust auth. That is test-only, but the workflow file is the template people copy. SECURITY.md supports versions greater than 9.x and says to report vulnerabilities by Twitter DM to alexdotjs or email alex@kattcorp.com.

eval() appears only in tests that round-trip a devalue/uneval transformer (packages/tests/server/transformer.test.ts, httpSubscriptionLink.test.ts, and packages/next/test/issue-4130-ssr-different-transformers.test.tsx). It is not on the request path. The production risk is user-supplied transformers: deserialize runs on request JSON, and next-sse-chat uses superjson.

@trpc/upgrade shells out: src/lib/execa.ts imports node:child_process exec, the CLI calls assertCleanGitTree unless --force, and it can installPackage/uninstallPackage. OpenAPI tests call execFileSync. Standalone HTTP/2 tests import child_process. These are maintainer and test tools, not the RPC runtime.

The e2e job is continue-on-error: true, and next-sse-chat (the Drizzle plus auth plus SSE example) is commented out of the matrix. App-dir sources are excluded from coverage and from codecov ignore paths. A green unit job does not prove the example apps or the experimental Next app-dir caller.

Client and server both depend on the unstable-core-do-not-import export for proxies, callProcedure, and transformResult. A breaking change there breaks @trpc/client even if the public index stays stable. Several v12 removals are already marked: inferRouterClient, header objects that are not Headers, experimental_lazy, and the sse() alias.

Adapter duplication is a blast-radius hotspot. Express and Next pages share nodeHTTPRequestHandler, but WebSockets call callTRPCProcedure directly and Fastify has its own fastifyRequestHandler. A procedure-lookup bug fixed only in resolveResponse will not automatically apply to applyWSSHandler.

extension_points.summary: New behavior is meant to plug in at initTRPC factories, the middleware and parser pipeline, client links, and HTTP adapters. Cross-cutting hooks are errorFormatter, transformer, responseMeta, createContext, and onError. Routers can be merged or lazy-loaded. Standard Schema is the validator seam. OpenAPI generation, the upgrade codemods, and the skills directories are the extension points outside the RPC runtime.

claims.claim: initTRPC.create() is the composition root. It returns five extension factories: procedure (createBuilder), middleware (createMiddlewareFactory), router (createRouterFactory), mergeRouters, and createCallerFactory. Docs and CONTRIBUTING tell app authors to call initTRPC once per backend.

Middleware is a list, not a class hierarchy. MiddlewareBuilder.unstable_pipe and ProcedureBuilder.use() append functions. next() may override ctx, input, or getRawInput. The marker field on MiddlewareResult is what forces middleware to return next()'s output.

A client link is a function from TRPCClientRuntime to an OperationLink. createChain is the registry: links run in array order and the last must be a terminating link or it throws 'did you forget to add an ending link?'. splitLink, retryLink, and loggerLink are non-terminating; http*, wsLink, and unstable_localLink terminate.

New HTTP adapters are expected to import AnyTRPCRouter from @trpc/server and HTTPBaseHandlerOptions from @trpc/server/http, then call resolveResponse. That comment is copied at the top of fetch, express, next, fastify, and standalone adapter files.

Per-request extension hooks on the HTTP handler are createContext, onError, responseMeta, allowBatching, allowMethodOverride, and maxBatchSize. responseMeta can set status and headers; passing a plain object of headers is deprecated in favor of Headers and scheduled for deletion in v12.

RootConfig is the place for cross-cutting server plugins that are not procedures: transformer, errorFormatter, sse, jsonl, defaultMeta, isDev, isServer, and allowOutsideOfServer. experimental is an empty object type reserved on the config.

Validator plugins hook getParseFn. Adding a library means detecting a discriminant (parseAsync, ~standard, validateSync, create, assert) without breaking the function-schema case used by Effect. ProcedureBuilder.input() stores both the raw parser (for types) and the middleware (for runtime).

Content types plug in as ContentTypeHandler objects with isMatch and parse. The JSON handler is jsonContentTypeHandler. Octet streams plug in via octetInputParser. Batch calls share one parsed input record indexed by batch position.

Router extension without editing the root object is mergeRouters(...) or lazy(() => import(...)). lazy() requires the module to be the router itself or a module with exactly one router export, otherwise it throws a fixed error string that shows the expected import pattern.

experimental_caller on the procedure builder replaces the exported function while keeping _def and the original invoke. That is the seam for custom server-side call conventions. createCallerFactory is the supported in-process API and is what app routers re-export.

WebSocket extension options on applyWSSHandler include prefix, keepAlive.enabled, keepAlive.pingMs, and keepAlive.pongWaitMs. An encoder seam exists as adapters/wsEncoder.ts with jsonEncoder imported by ws.ts. Fastify opts into it with useWSS on fastifyTRPCPlugin.

OpenAPI extension is GenerateOptions (exportName, title, version, servers) passed to generateOpenAPIDocument, which walks TypeScript types rather than executing procedures. Upgrade extension is a new jscodeshift transform registered in the multiselect in packages/upgrade/src/bin/index.ts and exported from package exports ./transforms/*.

agent_handoff.summary: Read the procedure and HTTP core before editing. Tests run against source via Vitest aliases, but typecheck and consumers need pnpm build because packages ship dist built by tsdown. Keep adapters thin, put behavior changes in unstable-core-do-not-import, and add a regression under packages/tests. Do not treat examples or www as the library. OpenAPI fixtures are generated and checked in CI. Public types are the product, so signature changes are breaking even when runtime behavior is not.

claims.claim: Files to read first: CONTRIBUTING.md (package map and the resolveResponse walkthrough), initTRPC.ts, procedureBuilder.ts, router.ts, http/resolveResponse.ts, http/contentType.ts, createTRPCClient.ts, and the adapter you are changing. The CONTRIBUTING page names those as the mental model for server, client, react-query, and next.

Safe command set is pnpm install, pnpm build, pnpm dev, pnpm test <filter>, pnpm lint, and pnpm typecheck-packages. pnpm test 3085-style filters are the documented way to run one regression. Do not run publish-canary, publish-prerelease, or the release workflow unless asked.

Each of @trpc/server, @trpc/client, @trpc/react-query, @trpc/next, and @trpc/openapi sets eslint no-restricted-imports on its own package name. Inside a package, import sibling files relatively. Cross-package imports must use the public export, and client code reaches internals only through @trpc/server/unstable-core-do-not-import.

Vitest aliases point at src, so a unit test does not require dist. turbo typecheck and lint depend on ^build, and the e2e job runs pnpm build first. After a type-only change, run pnpm typecheck-packages; after a runtime change, run pnpm test with a filename filter before the full suite.

Put new behavioral regressions in packages/tests/server, matching existing names (regression issue tests, batching, streaming, websockets). Colocate type-level tests next to the module when that is the local pattern (procedureBuilder.test.ts, router.test.ts). React hook tests belong in packages/react-query/test.

Do not hand-edit packages/openapi/test/routers. CI fails the unit job if that tree is dirty and prints the exact command pnpm -C packages/openapi codegen. @trpc/openapi is version 11.19.0-alpha, so treat its API as unstable relative to the 11.19.0 libraries.

Router keys then, call, and apply throw at createRouterFactory. Procedures are functions; isProcedure uses typeof === 'function', which is also why lazy loaders are stored separately. Do not add callable properties that would be mis-detected as procedures.

Never invoke a procedure as a normal function from application code. createProcedureCaller throws a fixed message unless opts contains getRawInput. Server-side calls go through createCallerFactory. Client calls go through the proxy.

isDev and isServer are environment gates. isServerDefault is true when window is undefined, Deno is present, or NODE_ENV is test, or JEST_WORKER_ID or VITEST_WORKER_ID is set. Forcing the server build into a browser bundle requires allowOutsideOfServer and will throw otherwise.

Examples and www are not safe refactor targets when changing the library. Examples pin workspace packages and demonstrate patterns (some insecure on purpose, such as the mock GitHub provider and empty Prisma context). www/vercel.json redirects are easy to break by renaming a docs slug.

Peer dependencies are exact: @trpc/client requires @trpc/server 11.19.0. Shipping a server change without bumping the peer, or testing with mismatched workspace versions, will not match what npm users install. prepack and version run tsx scripts/version.ts.

The widest blast radius is the procedure and router generics (ProcedureBuilder, DecorateCreateRouterOptions, DecoratedProcedureRecord). They are copied into every client package. A type-only break will fail pnpm typecheck-packages and the example typecheck step even when Vitest is green.
